home_pitcher_note: Acquired from the Orioles for five players, Bedard makes his regular-season debut hoping to pick up where he left off last season, when he won nine of his final 10 decisions before an injury in August.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood is making his third straight Opening Day start for the Rangers. He was the losing pitcher in the past two, going just five innings both times.

home_pitcher_note: The Mariners' Opening Day starter a year ago, Hernandez starts the season as the No. 1a starter behind left-hander Erik Bedard, but he definitely has ace capabilities. He would gladly take a first start like the one he had a year ago, when he shut out the Athletics for seven innings, striking out 12.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla was limited to 23 starts last year because of an elbow injury, but he was 3-2 with a 3.86 ERA in eight starts after coming off the disabled list in August. He was a 15-game winner for the Rangers in 2006 and was 1-2 with a 7.20 ERA in three starts against the Mariners last year.

home_pitcher_note: An innings-eater when he pitched for the Twins the past four seasons, Silva is being counted on to do the same for the Mariners. He has worked at least 200 innings two of the past four seasons and logged at least 180 in the other two, giving the Mariners a potential staff workhorse. He relies on getting early-count outs and should benefit greatly by Seattle's rock-solid defense and pitcher-friendly ballpark.
away_pitcher_note: Jennings was signed as a free agent in the offseason. The National League Rookie of the Year when he won 16 games for the Rockies in 2002, Jennings spent last season with the Astros and had his season cut short by injury. He finally underwent surgery to repair a torn flexor tendon. He is 0-1 with a 4.97 ERA in two career starts against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Trachsel pitched relatively well for the Orioles last season, but left the team in a trade for two prospects at the end of August. Seeking stability for their youth-filled rotation, the Orioles brought him back.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander enters the third year of a four-year contract with strong visions of having his first winning season with the Mariners. He has an 18-29 record so far, but he's capable of better than that.

home_pitcher_note: Loewen, one of the linchpins to Baltimore's rebuilding movement, made just six starts last season before succumbing to a stress fracture in his left elbow. The former first-round pick had a brief shoulder problem in spring, but appears to be fully healthy as the season begins. Loewen still has issues with his command and control, but a full season may help iron those problems out.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners' staff leader in wins last season with 16, Batista begins '08 as the No. 5 starter. The right-hander had a team-leading 18 quality starts in '07 and has pitched at least 180 innings in four of the past five seasons.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie will make his second start before the rotation turns around, thanks to the presence of an off-day early in the schedule. The right-hander started on Opening Day for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed ace of the starting rotation had a peculiar outing in his first start of the season. He surrendered one unearned run over seven innings, walked three, struck out three, had five assists, one putout and committed one error. It was one of the busiest games of his career on defense and all he received was a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera struggled in his season debut Wednesday, allowing six earned runs and not making it out of the fifth inning. The right-hander walked five batters -- one of them intentionally -- and gave up six hits, two of which went for home runs. Cabrera led the league in walks and losses last season, and the Orioles are watching his progress carefully.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander gave Seattle seven solid innings in his regular-season debut against the Rangers. The only run he allowed was on a solo home run to former Mariner Ben Broussard. As advertised, Silva was around the plate and was the first starter to go at least seven innings. He is built for endurance and now takes the show inside the Tropicana Dome in the opener of a three-game series.

home_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his second start for the Rays in the home opener after making his debut Wednesday night against the Orioles. He got a no-decision after allowing five earned runs on six hits, including two home runs, in 5 1/3 innings. The 24-year-old right-hander has a fastball that occasionally touches 97 mph, a curveball, a slider and a changeup. He is 1-1 with a 9.64 ERA in two career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard was originally slated to start Sunday against his former team, the Orioles, but was pushed back.  Bedard bobbed and weaved his way through five innings on Opening Day, settling for a no-decision. He threw 106 pitches, but the only run he allowed was a solo home run.

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine is a master of deception employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Since making that adjustment he has been a lot more successful. Friday night he survived a four-run third against the Yankees and did not allow any further damage in six innings to pick up his first win of the season. Sonnanstine has one career start against the Mariners, which came Sept. 16 at Seattle when he held the Mariners to one run on six hits in seven innings to pick up the win in a 9-2 Rays victory.
away_pitcher_note: The first Mariners starter this season to surrender more than one run in a game, Washburn tries to notch his first win of the season against the Rays in the middle game of a three-game series. Washburn surrendered three runs against the Orioles after his three predecessors -- Erik Bedard, Felix Hernandez and Carlos Silva -- each held the Rangers to one run. Washburn had been 1-0 with a 1.89 ERA in his previous three first regular season starts.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson got off to a shaky start Saturday against the Yankees when he surrendered a run in the first and then loaded the bases with one out in the second. But the right-hander escaped the second-inning jam without allowing any runs and didn't allow any more runs during his six-inning stint -- retiring the final nine hitters he faced -- to pick up his first win of the season. Jackson will be making his first start against the Mariners in this one.
away_pitcher_note: Three of the four walks the veteran right-hander surrendered in his first start of the season came in the same inning and helped erase the second of the two-run leads he had to work with against the Orioles. It didn't help that the usually reliable Seattle defense committed two errors on the same play, leading to an unearned run. Batista threw hard but didn't change speeds well enough to keep opposing hitters off balance.

home_pitcher_note: It might take a complete game for the right-hander to get his first victory of the season. Hernandez surrendered one unearned run in his first start of the season, handed the lead to the bullpen, and the Mariners lost to the Rangers at home in the ninth inning. In his last outing, against the Orioles in  Baltimore, Felix pitched eight scoreless innings and handed the 'pen a two-run lead, only to receive a no-decision in an eventual Mariners loss in the ninth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Showing his maturity on the mound in his third season, Weaver has repeatedly worked out of jams by making the right pitch at the right moment. That was clearly the case against the Rangers on Saturday, holding them scoreless for seven innings with a substandard fastball that only rarely cracked 90 mph. The team's ace until John Lackey returns, he is 4-1 with a 4.68 ERA in seven career starts against the Mariners, and he was 2-0 in four starts last year with a 6.08 ERA. He's 2-1 at Safeco Field in four career starts.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander showed true grit in his last start, going seven innings against the Orioles and departing with the game tied. Silva pitched his type of game, which is challenging hitters. He struck out five and didn't walk anyone. The only major glitch was a 0-and-2 fastball that he threw Melvin Mora in the third inning. It landed in the left field seats for a two-run home run. After throwing at least 100 pitches three times in 33 starts for the Twins last season, Silva has reached triple digits in each of his two starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Garland had an inauspicious home debut in his first start at Angel Stadium as a member of the Halos, surrendering seven earned runs in five innings in Sunday's loss to Texas. The righty was off for most of the game, allowing eight hits, walking two and hitting two batters. He looks to get back on track against a Seattle club that he has had success against in the past. Garland is 6-2 with a 3.15 lifetime ERA against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Baek fills in for scheduled starter Erik Bedard, who was a late scratch.
away_pitcher_note:
Saunders has been stellar after two starts. His latest effort Monday night against the Indians indicated that this time, the left-hander is in the Major Leagues to stay. He pitched eight innings against a difficult lineup, scattering four hits, walking two and striking out five. He left the game with a 2-1 lead, but wound up with a no-decision. Saunders has moved over to the
third-base side of the rubber this year with quality
results. He continued to show refined command of a
fastball, breaking ball and changeup.

home_pitcher_note: The secret to Washburn's success is going in and out, up and down, something he did with regularity in his start against the Rays, which resulted in his first win of the season. This will be Washburn's first home start in 2008. The veteran has a 15-18 career record at Safeco Field, but he has performed well against the Royals regardless of where the games are played. He is 8-4 with a 3.36 ERA in his career against Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke could have used water wings in his last start, a rain-drenched 4-0 victory over the Yankees. He swam through eight innings, giving up six hits, and generally kept the Yankees guessing with off-speed pitches and step-ladder fastballs. He threw 107 pitches and matched his career-best eight innings. Greinke was much more effective than in his first start although in that one he held the Tigers to one run in seven innings. He's pitched five times against Seattle with a 4.22 ERA, but no decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Batista's solid outing against the Rays -- he limited them to two runs over six innings -? was overshadowed by a shutout performance from his pitching counterpart, leaving the Mariners' top winner in '07 winless after two starts in '08. He pitched into the seventh inning for the first time and now turns his attention to the Royals, a team he didn't face last season, and has faced only twice in his career, posting a 1-0 record and 0.00 ERA in 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Bale was hurt by one home run hit by Miguel Cabrera and some defensive lapses in his second start of the season against the Yankees. He�s lost twice now and wasn�t hit all that hard in either outing. He made his first Major League start since 2003 against the Twins on April 4 and took a 4-3 loss. When Bale does post a victory as a starter, it would be his first such victory since Aug. 29, 2003, when he was pitching for the Reds and beat the Cardinals and Dan Haren, 8-5.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton picked up his first win of the season against the Indians, allowing five runs and eight hits in 7 2/3 innings. The right-hander cruised through the first seven innings, giving up only Jhonny Peralta's home run in the second. Staked to an early 9-1 lead, Blanton still went after the Indians' hitters and let his defense do the work.
away_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander surrendered his first earned runs of the season in his last start, which ended a 17-inning streak, but he battled his tail off against the Angels, throwing 117 pitches over 6 2/3 innings. The two-seam fastball has been Felix's best pitch, locating it down and in to right-handed hitters. He also is pitching inside more this season, and it is keeping hitters honest.

home_pitcher_note: DiNardo picked up his first win of the season Saturday against the Indians. Starting in place of the injured Rich Harden, the left-hander allowed two runs and six hits in five innings. He struck out three and didn't walk a batter. DiNardo was removed after allowing two singles to start the sixth. He threw 73 pitches and was around the strike zone in his first start of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is a contact pitcher, and in his last start Saturday against the Angels he was contacted. The Angels knocked out 11 hits in Silva's eight innings to score three runs. But a stout defense behind him -- turning three double plays -- prevented any more Angels rallies. Silva went eight innings, throwing 98 pitches, to save the bullpen and pick up his second victory for his new team. He is 3-2 with a 3.12 ERA in nine career starts against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: He wasn't as sharp with his control as in his first two outings, but Saunders found the right pitches when he needed them and held the Mariners to two runs in 5 1/3 innings in Seattle on Sunday. He was in hitters' counts from the start, struggling to control the movement on his two-seam fastball and slider. He'll try to get deeper in the game when he faces the Mariners at home. He's 2-1 in four career starts against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey will start in place of Erik Bedard, who was placed on the 15-day DL on Tuesday with a sore left hip. Dickey, who was promoted from Triple-A Tacoma on Monday, had been out of the big leagues since April 6, 2006, with Texas. He was bombed that day and was quickly dispatched to the Minors. That also was the beginning of his knuckleball transition. He won't say he has mastered the pitch, but it is effective enough to get out big league hitters. He had a 2.25 ERA in seven Spring Training appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Santana gave up three runs in seven innings to beat the Rangers on Monday in Arlington. The 25-year-old right-hander will be facing Seattle for the first time this season. In seven career starts against the Mariners, he is 3-2 with a 5.73 ERA. Santana is 25-9 with a 3.14 ERA through 44 career starts at Angel Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn got hit early -- allowing three runs to the Royals in the second inning -- on Monday, but he settled down to allow just two singles over the next four innings. He didn't have much the offensive support as the Mariners lost. All three runs came on home runs. Last year, he gave up 23. He needs to be more efficient, as he threw 104 pitches in his six innings. Against the Angels, his old team, Washburn has a 4-2 record with a 4.26 ERA in seven appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Moseley gave up four runs on seven hits in four innings but escaped with no decision Tuesday against the Rangers in Arlington. He will be facing the Mariners for the first time this season and for the first time in his career as a starter. In four career relief appearances against Seattle, Moseley has posted a 1-0 record and 0.84 ERA, allowing only one run on three hits in 10 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Batista, a team-high 16-game winner last season, finally won his first game Tuesday, 11-6 over the Royals. He went five innings, allowing seven hits and four runs. He said afterward that he had a "dead arm," but said it wasn't serious. It stemmed from a back injury in Spring Training. He had been unable to get into his usual routine between starts. He is 5-4 with a 5.60 ERA in 13 appearances against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old right-hander became the first starter to pitch a complete game, throwing 115 pitches in a victory over the Athletics. He threw first-pitch strikes with his fastball and retired 13 of 14 batters he faced from the second through sixth innings. His two-seamer has been his bread-and-butter pitch this season.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie has worked to three straight no-decisions, and he's been bailed out of losses by a pair of late Baltimore comebacks. The right-hander worked into the seventh inning for his third straight start his last time out. Guthrie allowed two home runs in his last start and has allowed five this year, the second-highest total in the league.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander has been everything the Mariners had hoped for when they signed him to a lucrative multiyear contract during the offseason. He has won his first three decisions and looked especially sharp in his last start, holding the Athletics to four hits and one run over seven innings. He has worked at least seven full innings in all four of his starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera has pitched to contact much better in his past two starts, allowing hitters to put his heavy fastball in play. The right-hander has also streamlined his delivery and added a slider to complement his curveball and changeup. Cabrera has pitched into the seventh inning in each of his past two starts, winning one and taking a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn is giving his team the chance to win with each of his starts, but it's just not winning many. Only one thus far. He has pitched at least six innings in his last three starts and has allowed three runs or fewer in three of his four outings. In 12 career starts against Baltimore, he is 6-3 with a 4.46 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Loewen allowed a three-run home run in the first inning of his last start but calmed down to throw five scoreless innings after that. The southpaw has made it through six innings just once in three starts and has walked more batters (12) than he's struck out (11). Loewen made just six starts before an injury wiped out his 2007 season.

home_pitcher_note: The 37-year-old right-hander pitched one of his best games with Seattle in his last outing, holding the Angels scoreless over 7 2/3 innings in a game the Mariners had to win to avoid being swept. Batista had great command of his fastball, moving it in and out, up and down and recording eight strikeouts. He also walked only one. Six of the eight hits he allowed came with two outs.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland rebounded from a loss with another fine outing against the Royals in which he allowed one run on three hits in 5 2/3 innings. He walked four and struck out three. Eveland, one of the key players involved in the trade that sent Dan Haren to the D-backs, never faced more than four batters in an inning, with the only run (as a result of a walk) scoring on a double play. He retired 10 of 11 before running into some trouble in the sixth.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Bedard's first start in 18 days, a delay caused by time spent on the disabled list with a sore left hip. He had his second start pushed back, finally working six innings in a 6-5 win over Tampa Bay on April 8. His third start was again pushed back until the club finally decided to place him on the DL. He threw a couple bullpens this week without discomfort. He is 1-3 with a 4.12 ERA in seven appearances against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Duchscherer had thrown five shutout innings against the Indians on April 4 when he was lifted from his first start of the season because of a strain in his right biceps. Duchscherer ended up getting the win for his four-hit work, but he also ended up on the disabled list. He was cleared to resume throwing withing a few days, and he threw 48 pitches in a rehab start at Triple-A Sacramento on Monday. A converted reliever, Duchscherer likely will be working with a pitch limit of between 70-85 if he's activated to face the M's.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez, coming off his complete-game victory April 16 against Oakland, was tough again Tuesday against the Orioles. He allowed just two runs in his seven innings but left with the score tied at 2-2. Now he faces the A's again, carrying in a five-game win streak and an overall 6-2 record against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton is a workhorse, having pitched into the sixth inning in each of his six starts and past the sixth four times, but he's allowed at least seven hits each time out, and he's gotten more than two runs of support only twice. In his start at home against the Twins Tuesday, Blanton stuck around for 7 2/3 innings, but he gave up a game-tying homer to Craig Monroe in the seventh, and a bloop single off reliever Alan Embree allowed Minnesota to score the go-ahead run in the eighth and pin Blanton with the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona's control, an issue in his first few starts of the season, was again a bit out of whack in his start against the Royals on Thursday. After sitting for a week because of an off day and a rained-out game, Carmona wasn't at his sharpest. He allowed four runs on nine hits with four walks and one strikeout in five innings. Still, he was able to pick up his third win. Carmona was 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in one start against the Mariners last season.
away_pitcher_note: Tightness in his right thigh spoiled Silva's 29th birthday as it prevented him from having a chance of improving his record to 4-0 in his last start. He shrugged off the ailment afterward, saying he would definitely be good to go in his next start, which would be the game that begins a three-game series against the Tribe. Of the 84 pitches he threw against the Orioles, 51 of them were strikes. That's the name of the game for the veteran right-hander, who was stopped short of pitching into the seventh inning for the fifth straight time this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his strongest start of an already impressive season, Lee held the Royals to a mere three hits in the first complete-game shutout of his career on Thursday. He walked none and struck out nine. Lee continues to pound the zone early in the count with his fastball, and his command of that pitch has been precise in each of his four starts. He's been able to successfully work in his secondary stuff as well, but his fastball has led the way. Lee is 5-1 with a 3.83 ERA in nine career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander continues to pile up the pitches, throwing 97 over five innings in his most recent start. It was the first time in five starts he didn't reach the 100-pitch mark, but the second time he has been lifted after five innings. He has logged six innings twice and seven innings once. Washburn has a career record of 7-6 against the Indians, most of his success coming in Cleveland, where he is 6-2 with a 3.31 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Byrd is known for his fly-ball-inducing tendencies, but he had trouble keeping those fly balls in the park in his last outing against the Yankees on Friday. In 5 2/3 innings, he gave up four runs on six hits with no walks and no strikeouts. All the runs he allowed came on three homers. In fact, Byrd has now given up seven homers in 26 innings of work this season. Byrd is 6-3 with a 3.38 ERA in 10 career starts against the Mariners, but he was 0-1 with a 9.58 ERA in two starts against them last year.
away_pitcher_note: The 37-year-old right-hander had his fourth start of the season come to a screeching halt barely after it got started. He lasted just one-plus innings against the Athletics before a mild groin strain sent him to the trainer's room. He threw 47 pitches and only 21 of them were strikes, a total flip-flop from the game he pitched against the Angels five days earlier, when he tossed 7 2/3 scoreless innings. Batista has an 0-3 career record against the Indians, all three losses coming in Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: Wang continued his undefeated opening to the season by pitching seven scoreless innings over the Indians on Sunday, finishing the month of April 5-0 and joining Arizona's Brandon Webb as the Majors' only five-game winners -- though Webb won his sixth later Sunday. Wang showcased his improving slider to strike out a season-high nine, one shy of a career high, and only allowed one runner to get as far as third base. Wang scattered four hits while walking two in a 113-pitch (73 for strikes) performance.
away_pitcher_note: Erik Bedard returned from the disabled list to throw 6 2/3 innings of shutout ball in a 5-3 win over the Athletics in his last start. The left-hander allowed only two hits in his first action in 18 days after being sidelined with inflammation in his hip. The former Oriole returns to the American League East to face the Yankees, a team he dominated in 2007, posting a 2-0 record with a 1.29 ERA in three starts against the Bronx Bombers.

home_pitcher_note: Mussina limited the Indians to two runs over five innings on Monday, winning his second consecutive start. away_pitcher_note: Felix Hernandez fired seven shutout innings in his last start against Oakland before running into trouble in the eighth. away_pitcher_note: Gabbard has made four starts for the Rangers and is coming off the disabled list. He has been sidelined with a strained muscle in his lower back. away_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, Floyd came within five outs of hurling a no-hitter. away_pitcher_note: The left-hander pitched another superb game in his start against the Rangers at Safeco Field, surrendering six hits and two runs over seventh innings. away_pitcher_note: Silva dropped his second consecutive decision despite a seven-inning effort against the White Sox in his last outing. home_pitcher_note: Batista rebounded well from one of his shortest outings of the season, going from a brief and ineffective 2 1/3-inning performance against the Rangers to a workmanlike 5 1/3-inning effort against the White Sox. away_pitcher_note: After dropping two of his first three decisions, Young has won two of his past three starts. He allowed one run on five hits in six innings in a 6-1 win over the Rockies on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez has lost four consecutive starts, the longest losing streak of his young career. His last win came April 16 against Oakland. away_pitcher_note: Estes looks to build off his first start in two years when he toes the rubber in Seattle on Sunday. away_pitcher_note: Silva allowed two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings and got a no-decision in his last start against the Rangers as he continues to be a consistent member of the Seattle rotation. home_pitcher_note: After three consecutive quality starts helped him even his record following three straight losses to open the season, Rogers had one of his worst starts as a Tiger on Thursday at Kansas City. away_pitcher_note: It has been six days since the veteran left-hander had his first career save with a scoreless inning of relief agains the Rangers in Arlington. away_pitcher_note: Early game blues continue to haunt the veteran right-hander who been nowhere near as effective as a year ago when he led the team in wins with 16. home_pitcher_note: Mussina couldn't escape the first inning on Tuesday night against the Orioles, allowing seven runs in all. away_pitcher_note: The month of May probably can't end soon enough for the veteran right-hander, who has an 0-3 record in four starts this month, including a brief and ineffective four-inning outing against the Tigers to start the road trip. home_pitcher_note: The Mets battered Wang for seven runs in 7 2/3 innings last Sunday night, managing only six hits off him but making each one count. But history says he's not apt to lose to the Mariners. In seven career starts against the team that almost signed him in 2000, Wang is 7-0 with a 2.39 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: After being skipped for the first time in his MLB career, the left-hander wobbled badly in his return to the rotation, surrendering 12 hits and nine runs in a 2 1/3-inning nightmare against the Tigers at Comerica Park. home_pitcher_note: The young right-hander, whose start was pushed back two days because of a calf injury, has pitched better than his record indicates. The 22-year-old has allowed two or fewer runs in six of his 10 starts but takes a three-game losing streak into his start against the Red Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Colon performed exactly how Boston wanted him to heading into his last start against Kansas City. And while he didn't hit the high-90s velocity he did during his dominant years, Colon managed to escape jams in the third and fifth innings. Lifetime against the Mariners, Colon is 12-10 with a 4.40 ERA. But he tends to pitch well in Seattle; the righty is 8-1 with a 2.17 ERA at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: The first-inning blues that have haunted Batista this month were somewhat solved in his last outing as he held the Tigers to one run. He has used a short-arm technique since tossing 7 2/3 scoreless innings against the Angels on April 20 and it might be time to scrap it and go back to his old style.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka struggled mightily in earning his eighth win of the season May 22 against Kansas City. Matsuzaka will get the nod against Seattle having gone 1-1 with a 4.33 ERA against the Mariners in his career. His lone win against the Mariners came at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander got his wish and worked with backup catcher Jamie Burke in his last start, hoping to duplicate his previous start when he allowed just two runs over seven innings and struck out 10 in a game against the Padres. In 11 career starts against the Red Sox, the lefty has a 4-4 record and 4.95 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer will try to recover from a rough start in Oakland, when he gave up eight hits and eight runs over four innings. home_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander makes his fifth start of the month still looking for his first win in May. Silva is a battler, though, and is determined to get on a roll. As a pitch-to-contact pitcher, he needs the defense to be at the top of its game when he pitches.
away_pitcher_note: After going his first seven outings without a quality start, Robertson has two of them in his past three games, the latest a victory over the Twins during which he pitched 6 1/3 innings of three-run ball. Robertson was miserable against the Mariners last year, allowing a combined 10 earned runs on 17 hits over 9 1/3 innings with seven walks and 13 strikeouts. Both outings were at home; Robertson hasn't pitched at Safeco Field since tossing seven scoreless innings on April 22, 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez had terrific stuff for seven innings Monday against Boston. Even manager John McLaren said it was the best he'd seen him pitch all season. Either he stays too long with his fastball or his late-game sequencing is off. He is 2-2 with a 3.86 ERA in four career starts against Detroit. He beat the Tigers twice last season.
away_pitcher_note: How feast or famine is the Tigers offense? While Kenny Rogers is averaging an AL-best 7.18 runs of support per nine innings as the pitcher of record, and Armando Galarraga is averaging 6.75, Verlander is stuck near the bottom at 3.44. He had only one run of support in his last outing Sunday against the Twins, spoiling his second straight strong outing. Not only did he throw seven innings of one-run ball, he hit 99 mph on the Comerica Park radar gun. That's the strongest sign yet that Verlander is getting his usual stuff back. If so, that's further bad news for the Mariners, whom he held to one run over six innings with seven strikeouts last Tuesday in Detroit for a victory. He has won all five of his outings against Seattle over his career, including two at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Batista held the Red Sox to two hits over five scoreless innings last Tuesday night when, with one out and none on in the sixth inning, an easy ground ball to shortstop Yuniesky Betancourt was mishandled, opening the door to an eventual game-tying, three-run home run by Manny Ramirez. Batista departed after seven innings and did not get a decision.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman has quality starts in his last three outings, but one win and a pair of no-decisions to show for it. The good news for Bonderman is that a flip in the rotation allows him to pitch close to home in Washington state. He has quality starts and victories in his last two outings at Safeco Field, one in each of the last two seasons.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, the veteran lefty was skipped one turn in the rotation and will face his former team instead of the Tigers, who roughed him up in Detroit during the most recent road trip. Only three of the 18 outs he recorded were made by a Mariners outfielder.
away_pitcher_note: Santana's complete-game victory over the Tigers on Tuesday was a study in Angels baseball, 2008. home_pitcher_note: The left-hander rebounded magnificently from a rocky start in Yankee Stadium, holding the Red Sox scoreless for seven innings at Safeco Field. He was the first starting pitcher to face Red Sox slugger Manny Ramirez with him needing one home run to reach the 500-home run mark, and he kept him in the park in three at-bats.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders had arguably his worst outing of the season against the Tigers on Wednesday when he lasted just five innings, allowing five runs on seven hits. home_pitcher_note: Thank goodness for a new month. Silva made five starts in May and did not win any of them. The last one, Friday night against the Tigers, was among the shortest of his career. He went a season-high eight innings, surrendering 11 hits, but only three runs.
away_pitcher_note: After three straight solid efforts, Weaver regressed Friday night against the Blue Jays with his second shortest outing of the season. Unable to get an out in the fifth inning, he gave up 10 hits and six earned runs, striking out two. He was in trouble from the start, unable to find a consistent rhythm and struggling with command of his fastball. Weaver gave up five earned runs in 5 2/3 innings in an April 11 loss to the Mariners in Seattle. He's 4-2 with a 5.06 ERA in eight career outings against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: As optimistic as the Red Sox were after signing Colon, the righty is even exceeding expectations. Colon hopes to fare as well in this outing against the Mariners as he did at Safeco Field, when he limited the Mariners to one run over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez comes off of a very impressive start against the Detroit Tigers on Saturday, when he threw seven shutout innings and gave up only two hits while striking out seven. The only thing that stopped Hernandez from making a run at a complete game -- he threw just 87 pitches -- was tightness in his right calf. He's battled the problem for a couple weeks now, although it seems to be more of a cramp rather than a sharp pain. It didn't appear to affect Hernandez on the mound, where he lowered his ERA to 3.29. He's also averaging nearly seven innings a start this season.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield has had some tough luck in his last two starts, turning in strong performances without a victory to show for it. Prior to that, Wakefield lost a complete-game, 1-0 contest to Erik Bedard. At Fenway this season, Wakefield is 2-1 with a 4.26 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Batista hurt his right groin in Sunday's loss to the Tigers, but he said it wasn't as bad as when he did it in April. Batista has shown a low 90s velocity on the mound and has lowered his ERA by 0.57 in his last two starts to 5.90 for the season.

home_pitcher_note: While it wasn't his most dominant performance of the season, Masterson filled in for injured Daisuke Matsuzaka Tuesday against Tampa Bay by holding the Rays to four runs on six hits in six innings. Masterson, a young, talented hurler who was called up from Triple-A Pawtucket to make the appearance, has made spot starts three times this season filling in for injured members of the rotation. His first two starts raised eyebrows as Masterson allowed just two runs and five hits in 12 1/3 combined innings against the Angels and Royals.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard will be looking to bounce back from a lackluster performance against the Angels. The left-hander worked 3 1/3 innings at Safeco Field and three of the five runs he allowed came with two outs. He has been on a good-bad routine for this last five starts, looking sharp one outing and rocky the next.

home_pitcher_note: Litsch struggled to command his sinker on Wednesday and absorbed a loss against the Yankees in the process. He surrendered a season-high 10 hits and saw his pitch count climb to 99 before being pulled after 5 1/3 innings -- his shortest start since April 22. The four runs and two walks he allowed were also his worst marks in a start since that April outing. Litsch had gone 5-0 with a 1.96 ERA in his previous seven appearances. Litsch is 0-1 with an 8.31 ERA in his career against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn has been a mystery so far this season. He was blasted by the Tigers on May 21, rebounded with a solid six innings against the Yankees on May 25, and was mediocre against the Angels in his most recent start, with four earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. His ERA sits at 6.56, well above his career mark of 4.16. Washburn pointed out after Monday that he has to be more precise as he gets older, and right now he's having his struggles. Lefties are hitting just .229 against Washburn this season, but that number is offset by the .346 righties are hitting. The left-hander might want to try pitching on turf more often, where he has a 1.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: McGowan struggled in his last start while facing the Yankees in New York. The Blue Jays right-hander allowed five runs on seven hits over 5 1/3 innings. He walked two while striking out five. In four career appearances -- including two starts -- against the Mariners, McGowan is 1-1 with a 3.24 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander atoned for the shortest outing of his career -- two-thirds of an inning against the Tigers -- with an eight-inning effort against the Angels. But it did not materialize into a victory, extending his winless streak to eight starts. He last experienced the thrill of victory on April 17 against the Athletics in Oakland. Six straight losses is a career high for the veteran. Silva has a 2-3 career record against the Blue Jays and is 0-2 at Rogers Centre.

home_pitcher_note: Facing the Orioles in his last start, Marcum tossed seven-plus gutsy innings, allowing just one run on seven hits and two walks, but the bullpen faltered behind him and he was left with a no-decision. Marcum went 3-1 in May in seven starts. Although this is the first time this season Marcum will face the Mariners, he 1-1 in six games with a 3.93 ERA against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: The bookends of this six-game road trip, Hernandez goes for his fifth win of the season, and third straight, in the series finale against the Blue Jays. Felix extended his consecutive scoreless inning streak at Fenway Park to 15 with six scoreless innings against the Red Sox to begin the trip. He stranded all eight runners that reached and came up with key pitches when needed.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey, a knuckleballer, moves into the spot previously held by Miguel Batista, who has been largely ineffective after leading the team with 16 wins last season. Dickey has done a good job in the few relief appearances he has made, allowing one run on six hits while striking out 10 in his past 10 1/3 innings. He has started once this year and allowed five runs on eight hits in six innings against the Angels on April 18.
away_pitcher_note: Hill had some of his best stuff last Saturday against the Giants. He threw 7 1/3 innings, giving up just two runs on seven hits while striking out two. But he ended up saddled with the loss, as three San Francisco pitchers combined to shut out Washington in a 6-0 loss. Regardless, Hill had his second-longest outing of the season, and dropped his ERA to 4.35.

home_pitcher_note: Cooler temperature and lower humidity will be a welcome sight for the Canadian-raised left-hander, who wilted in the Boston heat in his last outing. He limited the Red Sox to one run over five innings, departing because the 98-degree heat and 102-degree heat index wore him out more than the Red Sox hitters. Bedard has faced the Nationals once in his career, limiting them to one run over seven innings in an Interleague Play game, receiving a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: A mainstay of the Triple-A rotation, Clippard will again be asked to toe the rubber for the big league club after lefty Odalis Perez was forced to miss another start due to shoulder tendinitis. In his last start, Clippard was effective through four innings but struggled in the fifth before being replaced. In total, the right-hander threw 4 1/3 innings, giving up five hits and three runs. He walked four and struck out six.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn put together his third consecutive solid outing with an impressive performance during his last start against the Blue Jays. The Seattle left-hander allowed just one run on five hits while striking out four over six innings. His only trouble came during the bottom of the fourth inning when he surrendered a two-out RBI double off the bat of Jays first baseman Lyle Overbay. Washburn was forced to take the no-decision due to a lack of run support, but he now possesses a 3.63 ERA over his past three outings. The 33-year-old has only faced the Nationals once during his career. In that start, he allowed just one run over six innings en route to victory.
away_pitcher_note: Redding's last outing didn't start out as planned. He gave up three runs in a matter of minutes. But he settled down and limited the Pirates to only one run the remainder of his six innings. He earned a no-decision when the Nationals hit three home runs in one inning to tie the game. Redding was a member of the Padres when he faced Seattle for the only time in his career. He pitched 3 1/3 innings of relief, giving up six runs on five hits.

home_pitcher_note: Despite earning the loss facing Toronto in his last start, Silva still had a "quality" start. He allowed three runs on nine hits over seven innings. The right-hander walked none and struck out three. Silva has not recorded a win since April 17. Since that win, he has gone 0-7 with a 7.36 ERA. In his career against the Marlins, Silva is 2-0 with a 2.90 ERA over 31 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Miller best performance of the season ended up with a no-decision. The 23-year-old left-hander tossed seven sensational innings against the Phillies. He allowed one run on four hits with one walk and seven strikeouts. He came out for the eighth inning, but issued a leadoff walk to Jayson Werth, ending his night. The seven innings matched a career high, and in the seventh inning, he was throwing 96 mph. Formerly with the Tigers, Miller has faced Seattle two times in his career, and he is 0-2 with a 3.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez put forth a dominating performance during his last outing against the Blue Jays. Seattle's young hurler allowed just four hits while striking out eight over eight innings of work. The only blemish on his impressive afternoon was an unearned run he allowed to score during the bottom of the fourth inning. The 22-year-old has won his past three starts and has not allowed an earned run over those 21 innings. Hernandez left after eight innings against Toronto because of tightness in his legs, but the cramps were not considered to be a major issue and likely had to do with fatigue and the high temperatures at Rogers Centre. He is expected to make his scheduled start against the Marlins, a team Hernandez has never faced during his four-year career.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen had his second straight solid outing on Thursday, but he once again fell short of earning a win. After falling victim to four unearned runs against the Reds on June 7, Olsen made just one bad pitch against the Phillies, but it was a wild pitch that led to two runs in the sixth. Olsen, who retired 12 straight at one point, finished giving up two runs (one earned) on six hits while striking out seven and left after tossing 104 pitches in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey's return to the starting rotation didn't go nearly as well as the knuckleball specialist had planned. The pitch wasn't moving the way it normally does, coming toward the hitting area, and the Nationals had eight hits and seven runs in the first two innings off the veteran right-hander, who was lifted in the second inning. Dickey has faced the Marlins twice in his career and owns a 1-0 record and a 4.50 ERA in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Tucker went five innings while giving up just one run on two hits and striking out six on June 8. Unfortunately, the young right-hander saw his ERA balloon after his struggles vs. the Rays on Friday night. Tucker tossed five innings but was tagged for seven hits and five runs in his first Major League loss. Of the 97 pitches he tossed at Tropicana Field, 58 were strikes, as Tucker issued three walks and will look for more command vs. Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo lost his first start of the season Sunday against the Angels, despite allowing two runs on seven hits in a career-high eight innings. The Angels' two runs off Campillo came on a good pitch -- a changeup down in the zone that Casey Kotchman looped down the right-field line and into the second row. Campillo struck out seven, but lost for the first time in 28 career appearances. He has not given up more than four runs in any of his six starts this season. Campillo made eight appearances with the Mariners from 2005-2007, and will be facing them for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander gave the Mariners a quality start against the Nationals, but they didn't get him his fifth win. He settled for a no-decision in a game he surrendered two earned runs over six innings, striking out eight. 63 of his 100 pitches were strikes and, for the fourth consecutive start, did not allow a home run. Bedard has never faced the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: After missing a start when he rolled his ankle on the Wrigley Field dugout steps, Jurrjens rebounded in commanding fashion Monday, shutting down the Rockies for 7 2/3 innings, the longest start of his career. He pounded the inside of the strike zone and went to a rejuvenated and devastating changeup for big outs, repeatedly stranding runs in scoring positions. Jurrjens was efficient with his pitches, taking advantage of an overly aggressive Rockies lineup that swung at a lot of first pitches, and pitching to contact, allowing eight hits and two walks while striking out seven.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn put together his fourth consecutive solid outing with an impressive performance during his last start against the Nationals, holding the NL East team to one run over six innings, nearly a carbon copy of his previous outing against the Blue Jays. Washburn settled for another no-decision and remained stuck on two wins this season. The Braves are one of three MLB teams Washburn never has faced.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson gave up a season-high six runs in a loss Tuesday to the Rangers, his first start since he was treated for dehydration following a game against the Cubs. Hudson allowed six hits and walked two. He struck out three of the first six batters he faced, but struggled through 4 1/3 innings. It was the first time Hudson had allowed six runs since he gave up that many in a July 5, 2007, loss to the Dodgers, a span of 30 starts. Entering his start Sunday against the Mariners, Hudson is 0-10 with a 7.82 ERA in Interleague Play with the Braves. He is 12-6 with a 3.32 ERA in 23 career starts against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander's last start ended prematurely, not because of his pitching but his deportment. He said something he shouldn't have to first-base umpire Bill Welke and was ejected from his start against the Marlins two outs into the fifth inning. Silva has gone more than two months since his last win, which came on April 17 against the Athletics. He was 3-0 at the time, but has lost eight straight since. The veteran has a 2-0 record and a 2.12 ERA in his career against the Braves, tossing a shutout against the National League East team last season.

home_pitcher_note: The Angels battered Santana for five runs -- four of them earned -- in six innings last Tuesday against the Angels. He allowed at least one base runner in each of those innings, eventually losing his second straight decision. The Mets have lost each of the last games that Santana has started, despite the fact that he allowed a combined two runs over the previous two. His next chance for a victory comes in Interleague play against the Mariners, a team that hasn't beaten him since 2002.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez is still having a little trouble with his right calf, but it doesn't seem to affect the quality of his pitching. He has won his past four starts while allowing just three earned runs -- all in his last start against the Marlins on Tuesday. Hernandez is shutting down most of the right-handed bats that come up against him, allowing just a .213 average. He is also continually getting deep into games and saving Seattle's bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Perez labored through six innings on Wednesday against the Angels, skating out of jams until the first five batters to face him in the fifth inning all reached base. Three of them scored, and that was enough to put Perez on the hook for a loss. He allowed four runs on nine hits in all, striking out two and walking three, and Perez ultimately earned a no-decision when the Mets scored in the ninth. His career against the Mariners includes a 4.41 ERA and 15 walks over 16 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: If Erik Bedard is unable to make his start on Wednesday -- manager Jim Riggleman said after Sunday afternoon's game in Atlanta that the chance of Bedard pitching "was probably not realistic" -- Dickey would get the start. The knuckleballer, who would be making his Shea Stadium debut, has dropped two straight starts since earning his first win, on June 9 at Toronto, in relief. In his only career appearance against the Mets, he allowed two runs and four hits in 2 2/3 innings, but that was back on June 12, 2003.

home_pitcher_note: The first two batters to face Maine last Friday in Denver scored, and his outing looked ominous. But Maine recovered from those early struggles -- not to mention a quickly-escalating pitch count -- to last 6 2/3 innings against the Rockies. He retired seven straight at one point, striking out six in total and tying Johan Santana for the team lead with seven wins. Maine has never faced the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Take the "interim" tag from in front of closer and replace it with "former" for Batista. With R.A. Dickey pitching two innings on Sunday, the veteran right-hander will be moved back into the starting rotation, where he is 3-7, with a 6.16 ERA, actually a run and a half  lower than his ERA as a reliever. The 37-year-old Batista is pitching to a 4.93 ERA on the road this season, but is 2-1 with a 2.38 ERA in nine career games at Shea Stadium. He is 4-3 lifetime against the Mets, with a 3.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf leads the Padres with 11 quality starts and in his last outing, the left-hander tied a season high with 10 strikeouts but took the loss. Wolf allowed three runs, two earned, on six hits and four walks against the Tigers. Wolf will be making his first career start against the Mariners and is 8-9 in 21 career Interleague starts.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn made the best of his first career appearance against Atlanta, throwing 5 2/3 innings and striking out a season-high eight batters, while allowing only one run and six hits, but because of a blown save in the ninth, he did not enter in the decision. He is now winless in his last seven starts despite allowing two runs or less in four times. The lefty is 1-0 lifetime against San Diego in four games, with a 3.72 ERA. He last faced them with Seattle on May 19, 2006, going six innings, allowing two runs and five hits, but getting no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Baek will face his former team for the first time when Seattle makes its annual visit to San Diego. Baek has been a part of the Padres rotation with injuries to Chris Young and Shawn Estes. In his last start, Baek allowed six runs on eight hits with seven strikeouts for the loss against the Tigers. Baek came to the Padres on May 28 in exchange for right-hander Jared Wells.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is in the throes of a career-worst nine-game losing streak. In his last start in Atlanta, he lasted only four innings, allowing four runs and nine hits, including a season-high three home runs. The veteran right-hander finished Sunday tied for the Major League lead for most earned runs allowed with 61. He is 1-0 with a 3.44 ERA lifetime against San Diego and is making his first career appearance at PETCO Park.

home_pitcher_note: Consider Peavy's elbow issues -- which sidelined him on the disabled list for a month -- far, far in the past as the reigning National League Cy Young Award winner continues to throw well since coming off the DL earlier in June. Peavy allowed one run in six innings in his last start, Tuesday against the Twins. He struck out five and walked just one batter in his third start since his time on the DL with the right elbow strain.
away_pitcher_note: The left-handed Bedard, who has been on the disabled list once this season and missed more than a week because of back spasms, returns to action in the final Interleague game of the season. Even if he's 100-percent healthy, which is unlikely, Bedard probably won't throw more than 100 pitches in this game. He seems to have adopted a 100-pitch maximum for himself during his first season with the Mariners, who are more than willing to end their brief and ineffective association with the 29-year-old.

home_pitcher_note: The knuckleball specialist made his latest venture into the rotation a good one, tossing seven shutout innings against the Mets, winning his first big league game in a starting role in more than two seasons. His knuckler danced all night long, keeping the Mets befuddled from the get-go. He held the NL team to six hits. Dickey has pitched two scoreless innings in his career against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay struggled against the Reds in his last start. The right-hander allowed five runs on nine hits over 6 2/3 inning for the no-decision. In the outing, Halladay walked a season-high four batters and tossed a season-high 121 pitches. He did strike out seven batters though, and has reached that total in three of his last four starts. In his career against Seattle, Halladay is 4-4 with a 3.00 ERA over 72 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith has been effective this season out of the bullpen, and he will now be called upon to start Tuesday�s game with Felix Hernandez still out with a bad ankle. In 40 2/3 innings this season, he has struck out 33, walked 17 and given up three homers. In his last two outings, both two-inning stints against the Mets on the past road trip, he struck out four and did not give up a hit or a walk. Right-handers have hit just .159 against Rowland-Smith this season.
away_pitcher_note: Litsch provided a stellar performance against the Reds in his last start. The right-hander one-hit Cincinnati through the first 5 2/3 innings on his way to earning his eighth win of the season -- which tied him with Roy Halladay for the team lead. Litsch allowed one run on three hits over eight innings. He walked one and struck out six. The start was also a reversal of fortune for the pitcher, who had struggled over his previous four starts. Over that span, dating back to June 4, he was 0-3 with a 6.46 ERA. The righty had allowed a total of 17 earned runs in 23 2/3 innings during the stretch, with opponents hitting .330. Litsch was a totally different pitcher before that span, though, going 5-0 with a 1.96 ERA over seven games from late April to the end of May.

home_pitcher_note: Another solid outing finally paid off for the left-hander, who ended a seven-start winless streak in his last outing, beating the Padres in an Interleague game in San Diego. He surrendered two runs, the fifth time in his past eight starts that he allowed fewer than three runs. The only walk he allowed was an intentional pass to the last batter he faced in the eighth inning, his longest outing of the season.
away_pitcher_note: McGowan took the loss against the Braves in his last start. He allowed four runs on eight hits over 7 1/3 innings. He walked three, struck out four and needed 108 pitches in the outing. Lifetime against the Mariners, in five games -- three of which were starts -- the right-hander is 2-1 with a 2.45 ERA. He has not pitched well on the road this year, posting a 2-4 record over 10 starts, with a 6.19 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Precision was the name of the game for Silva in his last start as 62 of the 87 pitches he threw the Padres were strikes, which ended a career-high nine-game losing streak for the right-hander. He had not won a game since April 17, a stretch of 12 starts. He pitched ahead in the count and kept the ball down, two things he must do to be successful. He won?t strike out a lot of batters -- he fanned two Padres -- and stresses putting the ball in play early in the count. It worked perfectly against the Padres, and now he tries to do it against the Tigers, a team that has given him trouble this season, with 14 earned runs in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Rockies came into Verlander's last start hoping to make him work, and they executed the game plan. Verlander left after 5 2/3 innings with a pitch count of 118. He had only one quick inning and averaged 22 pitches in the other five frames. He earned the no-decision and allowed two earned runs or fewer for the fourth straight start. Verlander has made two starts this season against the Mariners, which came 11 days apart in late May. In those outings, he gave up a combined five earned runs on 12 hits in 13 innings. Jose Vidro has hit .563 (6-for-19) with two doubles against Verlander.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander returned to the Mariners' rotation last Sunday after missing more than a week because of back spasms, and he threw 94 pitches over 5 2/3 innings against the Padres. He was in control of the game until the sixth, when he walked the bases loaded and surrendered his only run. The lefty has now pitched into the sixth inning eight times in 14 starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers didn't have his best stuff in his last start, but he kept the Tigers in the game long enough for them to pull out a win. He also displayed some fancy defense, snaring a rocket line drive by Matt Holliday and making a nice stretch while covering first base to get a double play. The 43-year-old allowed three runs in the second inning but limited the damage and retired the final seven batters he faced. Rogers faced the Mariners once this season and earned the win after allowing four runs in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey put up his second effective start in a row on Monday, giving up two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings while striking out three. He couldn't pick up the win, thanks to an even better performance by Toronto's Roy Halladay. Of the nine hits Dickey gave up, eight were singles, and he mentioned afterward that some of the batted balls seemed to find holes. There has also been warmer weather in Seattle lately, which Dickey said can help his knuckleball move.
away_pitcher_note: Galarraga is coming off an underwhelming start against Minnesota in which he went six innings, allowing nine hits and three earned runs while striking out three. He received a no-decision. The Tigers beat the Twins 5-4, however, improving the club's record in Galarraga's starts to 11-3. Galarraga's next start will come at Seattle. He has never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith got his first Major League start on Tuesday and experienced mixed results. He sailed past the first three innings, but then gave up three earned runs before exiting with two outs in the fourth. The 62 pitches and 3 2/3 innings were both season-highs, and it will be interesting to see how the Australian responds to a second consecutive start with Felix Hernandez on the disabled list. He has communicated that he would like to be a starter eventually.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson had a rough outing Tuesday against the Twins, going four innings while allowing six earned runs on 11 hits in a 6-4 Tigers loss. The start comes following a stretch where he had allowed no earned runs in two of his last three starts. Robertson's next start comes against the Mariners. Robertson went 5 2/3 innings while surrendering four earned runs on four hits in a 7-4 victory over Seattle on May 30.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland gave up three runs on four hits and three walks while striking out four over 5 2/3 innings in his previous outing, Wednesday at Anaheim, on the way to losing for the first time in four starts. Eveland hasn't allowed a home run in his past seven starts, and his outing against the Angels snapped his streak of four starts of working at least six innings. He walked 13 batters in his first two starts of June, but he hasn't walked more than three in a start since then.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn is on a roll right now with five consecutive strong starts. His fastball has been effective, and he unleashed some successful split-finger fastballs during his last outing against the Blue Jays on Wednesday. He made just one mistake in that game with a two-run homer to Adam Lind, but finished up strong. He's now riding a two-game winning streak and has lowered his ERA by nearly two runs in his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer made the All-Star team in 2005 as a reliever and, manager Bob Geren said, "deserves a bid" as a starter this season. He continued pitching like an All-Star, shutting down the White Sox after a rough first inning in his previous start. Duchscherer allowed two runs and five hits, walking two and striking out five over seven innings to get the decision in the A's 3-2 victory on July 3. He has six victories in his past eight starts with a 1.54 ERA. He has allowed 33 hits over 58 1/3 innings, and opponents are slugging .260 against him in that span. Duchscherer is 0-5 in his career, mostly in relief, against the Mariners. They beat him 5-3 on April 26 when Duchscherer had not pitched in three weeks because of a strained right biceps.
away_pitcher_note: Silva welcomes a start against just about anybody except the Tigers. After finally ending a nine-game losing streak, including two to Detroit, the veteran right-hander met the Bengals one last time in his latest start. He was more effective, surrendering five runs in five innings, but absorbed his 10th loss of the season. The Tigers know Silva throws a lot of strikes and came out swinging, accumulating nine hits. A sinker-ball specialist, the first six outs he recorded were on fly balls. Silva is 1-0 against the Athletics this season, beating them on April 17. He allowed four hits and one run over seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton had a poor start against the Giants on June 29, but rebounded against the White Sox by dominating the inside part of the plate. Blanton allowed a run and six hits over seven innings -- establishing four types of pitches -- in the A's 7-1 victory. His performance contrasted his previous six starts, in which he had a 7.49 ERA and opponents slugged .511 against him. Usually it was one poor inning, Blanton said, that would bite him in his rough stretch. Ideally, he would like to find consistency.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander, who led the team in wins last season with 16 as a starting pitcher, returns to the rotation in place of ailing (shoulder) Erik Bedard. Batista worked two solid innings of relief against the Tigers on Saturday night and his fastball was clocked at 98 mph, prompting interim manager Jim Riggleman to say it's the best he has seen Batista throw all season. When he has good command of his fastball and is able to locate it, the 37-year-old can be extremely effective.

home_pitcher_note: Smith tossed a complete game against the Angels on June 30, but was unable to pitch six innings -- for the fifth time in seven starts -- against the White Sox. He also struggled with his command, walking six (tying a season high for the rookie) and allowing four runs in a 6-1 defeat to Chicago. Smith said he wants to try and get outs without going so deep into counts -- which will help him last longer in games and won't put the A's bullpen on alert as early.
away_pitcher_note: The knuckleball specialist battled his control at times during his start against the Tigers, issuing five walks during his six-inning stint. But it was the long ball that prevented him from winning his third game of the season, as solo pokes by ex-Mariner Carlos Guillen and Miguel Cabrera left Dickey on the short end of a 2-1 game when he departed. The five free passes were a single-game season high, as were the two home runs. He had surrendered just three home runs in 31 innings entering the game at Safeco Field. This will be Dickey's first outing of the season against the Athletics. He is 0-4 with a 9.00 ERA in seven career games against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar did not fare well in his first career appearance vs. the Rays, as the right-hander was tagged for nine hits and seven runs in just four innings. He was haunted by a big four-run third inning, in which Tampa Bay scored all its runs with two outs, and exited after only throwing 67 pitches. In nine home starts, Hochevar is 3-3 with a 3.50 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez returns to action after missing almost three weeks. A sprained left ankle on June 23 suffered during a collision at home plate with Mets outfielder Carlos Beltran put Hernandez on the 15-day disabled list. He's good to go again but will be watched closely, probably being limited to around 100 pitches. He was in a good groove prior to the injury, going 3-0 with a 1.38 ERA in four June starts, walking five and striking out 24 during a 26-inning stretch. He also hit a grand slam in the same game he was injured. Hernandez has a career record against the Royals of 2-0 with a 2.11 ERA in three starts.

home_pitcher_note: The power pitcher returned to form on Monday afternoon against the Rays, following a strikeout-less outing in Baltimore by fanning five Tampa Bay batters. More importantly, Meche scattered seven hits on two runs and exited with the lead after 5 1/3 innings, despite the no-decision.  He will look to build on that appearance Saturday night, as  Meche will face his old team for the first time in a Royals uniform.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn's streak of quality starts ended at five in his last outing, but he pitched a complete game against the Athletics. That was small consolation as he lost his 93rd Major League game and remains three shy of 100 big league victories. A backdoor slider that ended up in the left-field seats proved to be his downfall. Washburn has pitched much better in the past five weeks than his 4-8 record would indicate. He's throwing more quality strikes early in the count and keeping his pitch count at a reasonable level.

home_pitcher_note: Davies rebounded from a poor start at Baltimore and worked five strong innings on Tuesday night against the White Sox. He faltered in the sixth, however, and gave up two runs, although he left the game with a 4-3 lead. He was touched for nine hits in his 5 2/3 innings but hung tough and kept the Royals in the game. Davies won three of his first four starts after being recalled from Triple-A Omaha but hasn't had a victory in his last four outings. Twice he escaped losses when the Royals rallied to win. Davies has never faced the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: A minor mechanical adjustment worked wonders for the veteran right-hander in his last start. On the suggest of pitching coach Mel Stottlemyre, Silva lowered his arms and hands prior to going into his delivery, allowing his hands to be more relaxed, and he pitched his first complete game of the season in a 2-0 loss to the Athletics. He threw 94 pitches, 62 of them for strikes, and retired 20 of the last 23 batters he faced. He pitched the way the Mariners expected him to pitch most of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Well, the first four innings were a blast. Hernandez dazzled against the Royals in his first start back since sustaining ankle sprain on June 23 until the fifth inning rolled around. He gave up three runs and was pulled out before the sixth. His numbers were still good: Five innings pitched, eight strikeouts, four hits and three earned runs. Manager Jim Riggleman thought that Hernandez might have lost some of the bite on his breaking ball in the fifth. Hernandez said he could've thrown 40 more pitches than the 83 he threw in the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey finished up an impressive first half with a quality start and victory over the Rays on July 10. He limited the Rays to a pair of runs on four hits with three walks and four strikeouts over six innings. What stands out about Laffey is his poise in pressure situations. He is often able to get the big double-play ball to get out of jams. He's certainly taken advantage of the opportunity presented to him by the Indians' injury-ravaged rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Batista was moved up from Monday because of Jarrod Washburn's bout with the flu. The veteran right-hander makes his first post-All-Star Game start as one of five MLB pitchers who have won at least one game this season and also registered at least one save. He has held opposing hitters to a .172 batting average as a reliever, but opponents are batting .309 against him as a starter. Batista's 53 walks have been a problem, as it averages out to be 6.6 free passes every nine innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sowers set a career high with eight strikeouts in his last outing, but it didn't make up for the control problems he had in a no-decision on July 13 against the Rays. The lefty couldn't pick up his first win because he simply couldn't throw a strike when the count was full, piling up a career-worst seven walks and racking up his pitch count in the four-inning effort. If anything might be able to rectify Sowers' disappointing season, it might be a date with the Mariners. Sowers picked up one of his two career complete-game shutouts in 2006 against Seattle and threw five scoreless innings at Safeco Field in a spot start near the end of last season.

home_pitcher_note: Maybe now the pitcher Seattle broke the bank for is starting to live up to the expectations. After a mechanical change a couple weeks ago, Silva has had two solid outings. His most recent one came in a no-decision at Kansas City on Sunday. He went six innings, allowing just two runs while striking out five. Silva has now given up just two runs in consecutive starts after giving up five runs on July 3. It was after that game when Silva made the mechanical change.
away_pitcher_note: Lee wasn't lights out in his last outing, but he was good enough to keep the Rays scoreless in six innings of work. The left-hander never had a 1-2-3 inning in his 12th win of the year, but he allowed just one baserunner in each frame, facing four batters each time. It capped a surprising 12-2 first-half start, which helped earn his first-ever nomination to the AL All-Star team. In his one start against the Mariners this season, Lee went six-plus innings and allowed three runs in the winning effort. All-time against Seattle, Lee has been strong, going 6-1 with a 3.90 ERA in nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn said his arm was zapped after a 39-pitch first inning on Saturday night, but he grinded out a quality start anyway. He gave up two runs in that first inning and another one in the second, then settled down. Washburn went six innings, giving up just those three runs, and only one was earned. He was in line for the win until Brandon Morrow blew a save in the ninth. Washburn has given up two earned runs or less in six of his last seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Lester was likely the most consistent Boston starter throughout the first half, and even though he was touched up for five runs in his last outing against Minnesota, the Sox have to be encouraged by what lay ahead for the young lefty. After a no-hitter in May and a shutout win at Yankee Stadium in July, Lester was right at the top of the list as a viable candidates for the All-Star Game who were not selected. He pitched a team-high 125 innings in the first half of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey, a knuckleball specialist, is working on a seven-inning scoreless streak and has strung together four quality starts. Claimed from the Twins' Minor League system for $50,000, Dickey could be the best acquisition former GM Bill Bavasi made during his three-plus seasons with the Mariners. Dickey might not look flashy with his mid-70s pitches, but he gets the job done.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka battled through six innings against Baltimore in his final start of the first half, throwing 115 pitches and walking five batters. But he also allowed no earned runs in that stretched and scattered four hits, proving once against that the right-hander's free passes do not correlate with the number of runs he gives up. He's been virtually unhittable in the first half, and if he wasn't touched up for seven runs against St. Louis just after he spent time on the disabled list, his ERA would be even lower.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander was sharp in his first post-All-Star start, holding the Indians to four hits and two runs over six innings, striking out nine along the way. It was his second-highest strikeout total of the season, one fewer than he fanned during a loss to the Athletics on April 27. Lack of run support had been a problem for Hernandez, who had to make due with an average of 3.47 runs in his first 17 starts. The Mariners scored eight runs in the first four innings against Cleveland. Perhaps the best game of Hernandez's career came against the Red Sox. That was more than a year ago, when he tossed a one-hit shutout at Fenway Park.
away_pitcher_note: The wiry right-hander was pounded for eight hits and eight runs -- four earned -- in his last start, a loss to the Angels. Buchholz lasted 4 2/3 innings. What set the tone was a 37-pitch first inning in which Buchholz gave up three runs. For whatever reason, the righty has struggled in the first inning this season, posting a 9.00 ERA. One thing Buchholz has been unable to give the Red Sox this season is innings. He's thrown less than six innings in his last five starts. This is Buchholz's first career start against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The Jays are going to give Parrish at least one more start before re-evaluating their rotation. Toronto wants to promote left-hander David Purcey from Triple-A for an extended look at some point, so Parrish may be on a short leash. In his last start on Sunday, Parrish allowed four runs on four hits, including a pair of home runs, in three innings of a no-decision against the Rays. In his career against Seattle, Parrish is 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in nine outings.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran right-hander made his first start after the All-Star break a short one, lasting five batters into the third inning in a losing effort against the Indians. It was the seventh time this season that he didn't make it past the fifth inning, but he remains in the Mariners' starting rotation. Exactly half of his 58 pitches were strikes, which fueled his early departure. He has held opposing hitters to a .172 batting average as a reliever, but opponents are batting .315 against him as a starter, and his 53 walks have been costly.

home_pitcher_note: Toronto optioned right-hander Jesse Litsch to Triple-A Syracuse on Wednesday night, giving the young starter a chance to work through a persistent slump in the Minors. In his past nine outings, Litsch had gone 1-6 with a 6.12 ERA, after beginning the year 7-1 with a 3.18 ERA. The demotion opened the door for Purcey, who is going to get an extended look with the Jays. In 19 starts at Triple-A this season, Purcey went 8-6 with a 2.69 ERA, striking out 121 and walking 34 over 117 innings.
away_pitcher_note: A conventional fastball/breaking ball pitcher with Texas, Dickey has made it back to the Major Leagues with a knuckleball being his main weapon, and it has worked well for him. He had allowed two or fewer runs in five consecutive starts before the Red Sox scored four runs off him in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Marcum wasn't sharp in his last outing, but he escaped with a no-decision on the road against the Orioles on Tuesday. In his first start off the disabled list, following a month-long bout with a right elbow injury, Marcum allowed a season-high seven runs (six earned) on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings. The right-hander yielded three home runs and finished with three walks and three strikeouts. Marcum is 1-1 with a 3.20 ERA in seven career games against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Working with two extra days of "rest" because of a bout with the flu, Washburn pitched well against the Red Sox, but the lack of run support proved costly once again. Washburn held the Sox to two runs over 5 2/3 innings, but the Mariners scored none and the veteran lefty remained stuck on four wins this season and 97 in his career. He has surrendered two or fewer earned runs in seven of his last eight starts and won just two of them. Washburn has faced the Blue Jays twice this season, beating them 4-2 in Seattle on July 2 and taking a no-decision in a 3-2 Mariners loss on June 9 in Toronto. He has surrendered three earned runs and 12 against the Blue Jays this season.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman will be making his second spot start of the month. Texas optioned Feldman to the Minors earlier in the month to keep his innings down, but he was called upon last Monday to fill in for Eric Hurley. Feldman came through in the start, going six innings and holding the White Sox to one run while earning the victory. This time around, he'll be replacing Kevin Millwood, who is out with a pulled groin. Monday will mark Feldman's second start of the season against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander had to work especially hard to keep the Mariners in their series finale against the Red Sox, finally departing after 108 pitches over six innings -- including 31 in the sixth, when he loaded the bases with none out and escaped with just one run being scored. Felix walked a season-high five, but the Red Sox are known to force opposing pitchers into high pitch counts. Hernandez is 0-1 in two starts against the Rangers this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Rangers haven't officially announced who will start Tuesday's game against Seattle, but Mendoza will have already been skipped in the rotation, so he will likely get the nod. If not, the Rangers could look to Scott Feldman. It all depends on how healthy Kevin Millwood is Monday. If he can't go, either Mendoza or Feldman could get the nod Monday.
away_pitcher_note: Silva was scratched from his last start against the Blue Jays because of tightness in his lower back.
