The right-hander informed manager Jim Riggleman he could have started on Monday, but the club opted to err on the side of caution and give Silva an extra day of rest. The tightness in his lower back is the same injury that forced Silva to leave after three innings against the Indians on July 20. Silva is 4-4 with a 4.11 ERA in his career against the Rangers.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla was without his best stuff in his last start against Oakland, but he got plenty of offensive support -- 14 runs on 17 hits to be exact -- to tally the victory. In six innings of work, he allowed five runs on seven hits while walking four and fanning nine A's batters. In three starts against Seattle this year, Padilla is 1-0 with a 2.00 ERA. He is just three victories shy of tying his career-high win count of 15 in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Batista surrendered a run in each of the first two innings during his last start against the Blue Jays but quickly settled down and finished with a strong performance. The early runs were the only ones Batista would surrender over 5 1/3 innings. He allowed five hits while walking two before being forced to depart after 82 pitches because of fatigue. He appeared set to win his fifth game of the season but Seattle's bullpen was unable to hold the lead and as a result he was forced to take the no decision. The 37-year-old is 4-4 with a 5.12 ERA in 13 career appearances against the Rangers. Texas shortstop Michael Young has caused him the most difficulty, hitting .400 (8-for-20) with four RBIs in his career against the veteran righty.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison beat the Athletics, 9-4, on Saturday, allowing three runs (one earned) in five innings. He beat Justin Duchscherer, who entered the game with the lowest ERA in the American League. His other victory came against Angels All-Star left-hander Joe Saunders. This is his fifth start for the Rangers since being promoted from Triple-A Oklahoma.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey will return to the Ballpark in Arlington to face the team which drafted him in the first round during the 1996 Draft. He was a conventional fastball/breaking-ball pitcher earlier in his career with Rangers but now uses a knuckleball as his main weapon. Dickey made his last start on just three days' rest against the Blue Jays. He allowed a run during every inning he pitched and finished his 5 1/3 innings of work with eight earned runs on 10 hits while issuing four walks. With the loss, Dickey's record as a starter fell to 1-6 with a 6.06 ERA and it was the fifth time he has allowed four or more runs in an outing this season. This will be the first time he has faced the Rangers during his career.

home_pitcher_note: Silva will make his first start since he was put on the disabled list two weeks ago with right triceps tendinitis. Silva felt soreness in his elbow after his last start, which came Aug. 15 against his former team, the Twins. The Mariners will feeling a little sore after the outing as well. The 29-year-old right-hander was rocked for nine hits and nine runs over 3 1/3 innings to pick up his 14th loss of the season. In his last five starts before we went on the DL for the fourth time of his career, Silva racked up an 11.39 ERA and had struck out as many as he walked. In three starts against the Rangers this season, Silva is 1-0 with a 5.17 ERA. Lifetime, he is 4-4 with a 4.76 ERA in 12 starts.
away_pitcher_note: There's a good chance Olson will be glad to make his first start out of the month of July. It was a rough month for the left-hander who had given up 24 runs in just 19 2/3 innings in four starts before his last outing, July 27, against the Angels. Olson pitched well enough -- and deep enough -- to get the Orioles first quality start since July 11, holding the Angels to just two runs over six-plus innings. The key for the southpaw will be to repeat a similar performance in Seattle to try and bring some stability to a rotation that is scuffling. Olson has not made a start against Seattle this season.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander tacked on another quality start in his previous outing, holding the American League's top-scoring team to three runs over six innings in a no-decision effort against the Rangers in Arlington. The heat was oppressive, but King Felix threw 112 pitches in a game that started with a 101-degree temperature. He walked four, giving him nine walks in the past two starts after going seven starts without walking more than three.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie has averaged six innings per start since the All-Star break, notching a 2-1 record and a 3.50 ERA. The right-hander has been consistent this season, registering a 3-4 record and a 3.69 ERA at home and a 4-4 record and a 3.30 mark on the road. Guthrie has gone 5-2 in his past seven decisions after starting 2-6.

home_pitcher_note: After being pushed back several days because of tightness in his lower back, Silva was pushed around by the Rangers during a 2 1/3-inning outing in Arlington in his 22nd start of the season. The pitcher known as "Buffalo" by his teammates, surrendered seven hits and six earned runs, ballooning his ERA to a season-high 5.95. This will be his third start of the season against the Orioles. He received no decisions in his first two outings, surrendering 10 earned runs in 13 innings. And that was back in April, when he was unbeaten (3-0) and had a 2.79 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera provided a strong outing in his last start, but wound up ejected after hitting a batter who had previously homered off him. The Orioles still went on to win the game, and Cabrera earned his first victory in 27 days and his second since mid-May. The right-hander appears on pace to throw 200 innings for the second consecutive season.

home_pitcher_note: His last outing made it two straight strong starts, as he held the run-happy Rangers to three runs -- two earned -- over six innings in Arlington. He had excellent control, throwing just 28 balls during an 88-pitch outing. The various ailments that have bothered him off and on most of the season appear to be behind him heading into the final two months of the season. This will be his -- and the Mariners' -- first appearance against the Twins this season. He is 2-1 with a 4.70 ERA in his career against the Minnesota.
away_pitcher_note: Perkins received the victory in his last start against Chicago, but he was not at his best. The rookie left-hander went six innings while allowing four earned runs on seven hits and two walks in the 6-5 Twins triumph. The Twins are 10-6 in Perkins' 16 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey got things back on track on Thursday by giving up two earned runs and six hits in 7 2/3 innings to pick up the win against the Rangers. He struck out two and walked one. In his previous two starts, the knuckleballer had given up eight and four earned runs, respectively. Those two starts were quite different than the four that preceded them -- a stretch that saw Dickey gave up a combined four earned runs. Dickey has a 4.78 ERA at home this season, and right-handed hitters are batting above .300 against him.
away_pitcher_note: Baker allowed four earned runs on five hits and three walks while receiving a no-decision in his last start against Chicago. He labored early, throwing 61 pitches through three innings, but ended up striking out eight batters. Despite the less than stellar start, Baker has still allowed three earned runs or less in 23 of his 26 starts this season. Baker will next take the bump against Seattle, a club he has not faced in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander stayed put as the Trade Deadline came and went, and his first start since didn't go the way he wanted. Facing the Orioles in the fifth inning, a two-out, none-on situation turned into an eight-run rally and Washburn's 96th career loss. It was his rockiest outing in more than two months. Washburn, who is 6-5 with a 3.46 ERA in his career against the Twins, went 1-2 with a 3.26 ERA against them in 2007. He needs two more victories to reach 100 in his MLB career.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander was superb in his most recent start, against Cleveland on Friday, lasting seven innings while allowing one earned run on six hits and one walk in Minnesota's 4-1 victory. It was Blackburn's second consecutive stellar start against the Indians in a week -- going 2-0 in 14 innings while allowing only two earned runs in those outings. Blackburn will next face Seattle for the first time of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez hasn't been getting hit hard lately, but he's not taking the Mariners deep into ballgames like he was earlier in the season. His last start was a classic example, as he gave up two earned runs in five innings against the Orioles on 109 pitches. He threw 37 pitches in the first inning, which set him up for a high pitch count. Since returning from the disabled list (sprained left ankle) on July 11, Hernandez has been unable to go more than six innings in each of his five outings.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine picked up his 11th win of the season Saturday night, when he held the Tigers to two runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out six in six innings. The right-hander is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Sonnanstine is 1-1 with a 3.46 ERA in two career starts against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Silva battled against the Orioles on Sunday and gave up four earned runs in 6 2/3 innings while striking out two and walking one. That was an improvement upon his last two starts, which lasted 2 1/3 and three innings, respectively. This will be the first time the big right-hander has gone against his former team since coming over to Seattle as a free agent in the offseason. He has not recorded a win since June 28 against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Shields made his 16th quality start of the season by allowing two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings on Sunday against the Tigers, but he came away with a no-decision. The 26-year-old right-hander's best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve, and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handed hitters. He is 0-1 with a 1.57 ERA in three career starts against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander from Australia returns to the Mariners roster as a starting pitcher, possibly for the remainder of the season. Used exclusively as a long reliever, Rowland-Smith was sent to Triple-A Tacoma more than two weeks ago to be converted to a starter and he pitched well in three starts, surrendering two runs in each of them and working his pitch-count to 101 in his most recent outing. He isn't overpowering, relying instead on command of this fastball and off-speed pitches to keep hitters on their toes. He replaces right-hander Miguel Batista in the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his first career shutout, Garza wasn't nearly as economical on the hill on Monday night. The right-hander exited after five innings, in which he threw 102 pitches and was plagued by the long ball. Cleveland's No. 9 batter, Asdrubal Cabrera, opened the third inning with a solo shot, and David Dellucci went yard for a two-run homer two innings later, as Garza never appeared to settle in on the mound. Garza has faced the Mariners once this season already, in an April 8 contest in which he left with radial nerve irritation after pitching a season-low 2 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey has put together two solid starts in a row, seemingly securing his spot in the Mariners' fluid rotation. He held the Twins to three runs over seven innings in his last start, making big pitches when he had to, and handed a three-run lead to the bullpen, which didn't hold it, costing the knuckleball specialist a win. He has not faced the Rays this season and is 0-1 with a 7.38 ERA in his career against them.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson got the win in Tuesday's game, tossing 5 2/3 innings against Cleveland. Although hardly dominant, the 24-year-old Jackson gave the Rays a chance to win -- allowing seven hits and three runs -- and left the game with a 4-3 lead. Jackson is at his best when he is locating his 97-mph fastball, which sets up his array of other pitches, particularly his slider. The young flamethrower has won his only career appearance against Seattle, tossing eight shutout innings and allowing just two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Garland settled down after a shaky first inning, in which he allowed two runs on four consecutive hits to open the game against the Orioles last Tuesday. Garland remained in the game and tossed seven innings, allowing three runs on nine hits while striking out one and walking none, but was charged with the loss. It was the 16th time in 23 starts that he lasted at least six innings. Garland is 6-3 with a 3.30 ERA in 12 career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn returns to his old stomping grounds in search of his 99th career victory. The lefty spent his first eight seasons in the Angels organization, winning 75 games for the Halos, including 18 in 2002, when he helped the Angels win their only World Series title. He found fame in Southern California and fortune in Washington, signing a four-year, $37.5 million contract prior to the 2006 season. He needs pinpoint control to be most effective and has provided the Mariners with consistent work since the end of May. He is 0-2 against his former team this season, surrendering eight runs in 11 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Santana had the luxury of pitching with a large lead Wednesday as the Angels scored nine runs in the first four innings against the Orioles. Santana plugged away for seven innings, making just two mistakes on a solo home run by Luis Montanez and a three-run homer by Nick Markakis. Santana allowed four runs on eight hits and struck out seven batters to earn his 13th win of the season. Santana is 5-2 with a 4.56 ERA in nine career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander is coming off one of his best outings of the season, holding the Rays to one run over eight innings. But all he got out of the solid outing was his eighth non-decision of the season, which leads the staff. His pitch count was night-and-day different than his previous outing, when he threw 109 pitches in five innings against the Orioles. He threw 105 pitches during the eight innings he worked against Tampa Bay. Hernandez is 1-0 against the Angels this season, beating them on April 11 at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano's second start brought him back even closer to the form he showed in 2006, but still not quite there. He went 5 2/3 inning and gave up three runs in earning the win. In his two starts since returning from Triple-A, Liriano is 2-0 with a 2.31 ERA. He said he felt more relaxed physically and mentally on the mound against the Royals on Saturday. Liriano also threw more sliders, a sign that he is getting closer to where he used to be.
away_pitcher_note: The trials and tribulations of Silva's first season with the Mariners continue in his old stomping grounds -- the Metrodome. The veteran right-hander, who won 47 games for the Twins between 2004 and 2007, including 13 last season, has won one game with the Mariners since the end of April. He started the season with three straight wins, but has struggled ever since, losing nine consecutive decisions before beating the Padres on June 28. He has not won a game at Safeco Field in his last seven starts at home.

home_pitcher_note: Baker had one thing in mind coming into his last start, against the Royals: keep the ball down. He did that, at least better than he did against Seattle when it was a major problem. Baker said he used a mechanical change to ensure that the ball would stay lower and for the most part, it worked. He went seven innings and gave up just two runs. Defensive miscues prevented him from getting the win.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season that he actually was able to prepare for, the left-hander from Australia had a solid outing against the Rays, pitching into the sixth inning for the first time. Rowland-Smith departed with a four-run lead but had to settle for an undeserved no-decision as the Seattle bullpen came undone after he left. A pitch-to-contact hurler as a reliever, Rowland-Smith struck out five Rays. This will be his third career appearance against the Twins. He is 0-0 with a 3.00 ERA in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Perkins was 0-2 against the Yankees prior to Monday's start, but the left-hander found the third start to be a charm. He pitched eight shutout innings and struck out four while allowing four hits and three walks en route to a win. Perkins will next face Seattle. In his last start against the Mariners, on Aug. 4, a Raul Ibanez grand slam ruined the lefty's night. Perkins allowed five earned runs on 12 hits over 6 1/3 innings at Safeco Field.
away_pitcher_note: All signs point to the left-hander making his first start of the season. Manager Jim Riggleman announced on Wednesday that R.A. Dickey was being reassigned to the bullpen, but did not say who Sunday's starter in the series finale against the Twins would be. Feirerabend, who went into Wednesday night's start for Triple-A Tacoma with a 7-1 record and 2.11 ERA, surrendered two runs in the first inning and was replaced with one out in the third inning. The left-hander had a 1-6 record and 8.03 ERA in 13 appearances, nine of them as a starter. He never has faced the Twins.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle was outstanding for a second consecutive start Wednesday, throwing seven shutout innings against Kansas City to earn the win. He allowed only five hits and struck out five batters. He also didn't walk anybody, bringing his K/BB ratio to 7-to-1 over his last three starts. Buehrle brought his record to .500 for the first time since April 14, and has truly re-established himself as the captain of the staff. Buehrle has yet to face Seattle this season but owns a 6-4 record with a 3.75 ERA against them lifetime.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander surrendered just one earned run in his last outing, but three unearned runs sent him to his 12th loss of the season and 98th of his MLB career. Two of the seven hits he allowed were home runs, the first time since May 10 that he gave up more than one home run in a game. Washburn has had nine quality starts in his last 14 outings and has two wins to show for it. He is 3-4 for a 3.92 ERA in nine career outings at U.S. Cellular Field.

home_pitcher_note: Ozzie Guillen chose to go with Richard for Tuesday's start against the Mariners. The left-handed rookie worked a perfect ninth inning on Sunday against the A's and struck out two batters. He struggled in each of his three starts during his first stint with the big league club, throwing just 13 innings and surrendering 19 runs. Richard has struggled particularly at adjusting to hitters late in the game. Batters are hitting .286 when facing him the first time, but that number goes up to .346 the second time around and .667 when he sees a batter a third time.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander had another quality start in his most recent outing, holding the Angels to three runs over six innings and four over seven, but had to settle for his ninth no-decision of the season. His ERA climbed over the 3.00 mark, but is still an impressive 3.04 after 23 starts, much better than his 7-7 record. He had gone four starts without surrendering a home run before Mark Teixeira hit a two-run homer to left-center. Hernandez has a career record of 1-1 against the White Sox with a 5.01 ERA in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't Floyd at his best during Friday's 6-4 loss to the A's in Oakland, but the right-hander certainly pitched well enough to win. He allowed one earned run on six hits over 5 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking two. Floyd also threw 110 pitches against an extremely patient Oakland offense. Floyd has one start against the Mariners this season, and it was not a good one, as he allowed five runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings during a loss at Safeco Park. Floyd has a career 0-2 record with a 10.13 ERA against Seattle, but he has an 8-2 record at U.S. Cellular Field this season.
away_pitcher_note: The knuckleball specialist returns to the rotation just three days after being sent to the bullpen, replacing the injured Carlos Silva (elbow tendinitis) for the time being. Dickey, 2-7 as a starter this season, tied a Major League record during a relief appearance against the Twins on Sunday by throwing four wild pitches in the fifth inning. For whatever reason, his knuckler was moving more than usual inside the Metrodome, compared to the movement it has outside. He figures to get at least two more starts before leaving the rotation again.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander from Australia got off to a rocky start against the Twins, surrendering five runs in the first two innings. But he regrouped magnificently and made it through the fifth inning leading by a run. Rowland-Smith turned his start around by throwing more first-pitch strikes and getting better command of his fastball. He didn't overpower anyone, striking out one batter, but kept the on the lower edge of the strike zone more consistently. Rowland-Smith has faced the Athletics three times in his career, holding them to one earned run in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: A rookie acquired in the Dan Haren trade with Arizona over the winter, Smith has been more impressive than his win-loss record indicates. He's struggled with his command at times, costing him a game here and there, but he's also been victimized more than any pitcher on the A's staff by Oakland's anemic offense. In 24 starts, he's received two runs or fewer of support 17 times, including his last time out, when he took a 2-1 loss to the White Sox. Smith is 0-6 in his past eight starts, but he's unbeaten against the Twins, having held them to two runs on seven hits over seven innings in his only start against them this season.

home_pitcher_note: With a rocky debut start in Minnesota behind him and preferably not to be remembered any time soon, the left-hander takes on the Athletics at Safeco Field. Feierabend earned a return to the big leagues with a solid season at Triple-A Tacoma, posting a 7-1 record and 2.04 ERA. But the Twins weren't, socking it to him to the tune of five hits and five runs in the first inning. The 22-year-old was lifted after surrendering 10 hits and six runs over three innings. He is 0-0 with a 2.89 ERA in two career appearances against Oakland.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez had a nightmare of an outing at home Sunday against the White Sox, the team that sent him to the A's in an offseason trade. Admittedly over-amped to face his former team, Gonzalez gave up three homers and gave up as many earned runs as he recorded outs (seven). One of Oakland's top prospects, Gonzalez was called up from Triple-A Sacramento earlier in the month and has made three starts. A rookie, he's never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander's disappointment in not being traded to the Twins last week could have been an underlining factor in one of his shortest outings of the season in his previous start against the White Sox. He did not make it through the fifth inning for only the fourth time in 24 starts, yielding eight runs in 4 1/3 innings. He absorbed the loss, the 99th of his MLB career. He has 98 wins. Washburn is 0-1 against the Athletics this season, dropping a 4-3 decision in Oakland on July 7.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland pitched well down in Triple-A Sacramento before coming back up to the big leagues thanks to some injuries in the starting rotation. In his three Minor League starts, he went 3-0 with a 2.57 ERA and 21 strikeouts in 21 innings pitched. He's already started 22 games with the big club this year, going 125 innings and striking out 85 hitters. Eveland has already faced Seattle twice this season, winning both times by giving up three earned runs over five and 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander had a rough start against the White Sox, yielding 11 hits and five runs over five innings to fall under the .500 mark this season. But the big news was the fact he did not strike out a batter for only the second time in 97 career starts. The only other time it happened was on April 8, 2007, when an injury limited him to one-third of an inning against the Twins. Also uncharacteristically, Hernandez was hurt by the long ball. He gave up two home runs for just the second time this season, and the first time since April 11 against the Angels. He is 1-1 against the Athletics this season, and 6-3 in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Meyer has gone 10-5 for Triple-A Sacramento this season and got the callup after injuries to starting pitchers Justin Duchscherer and Sean Gallagher. He's also appeared six times for the Athletics this year, including a start. He's thrown 14 2/3 innings in the Majors in 2008 and given up nine earned runs and 15 hits. He last faced Seattle on Sept. 19, 2007, when he gave up five earned runs in four and 2/3 innings to take the loss.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander returns to the rotation after spending a couple of weeks in the bullpen to get his act together after surrendering six earned runs over three innings in a start on August 4. He has made six relief appearances since then, allowing one earned run. His success often times is predicated by his control. The 37-year-old simply walks too many batters, which helps get his pitch count high. Throwing early strikes and getting early outs is imperative for him.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano allowed no earned runs in five innings but racked up 107 pitches Wednesday in a 3-1 Twins victory over the A's. The lefty struck out five while allowing five hits and three walks but stranded eight runners. Liriano is 4-0 with a 1.14 ERA in four starts since being recalled from Triple-A Rochester on Aug. 1. Next up for Liriano is Seattle. The lefty allowed no earned runs in seven innings on Aug. 15 against the Mariners at the Metrodome.

home_pitcher_note: The transition of Rowland-Smith from reliever to starter took a giant step Thursday as he had a career high for innings (seven), strikeouts (six) and pitches (114) in a 1-0 loss to the Athletics. He allowed just four hits, including the game-winning home run in the sixth. He has yet to record a decision in his five starts and carries a 4.79 ERA. This will be his second start against Minnesota. He received a no-decision Aug. 16, working five innings and allowing 10 hits and five runs.
away_pitcher_note: Baker's previous problems of "yanking the ball" seemed to disappear in his start against the Angels. The only run that the right-hander allowed over his eight innings came on solo home run by Mark Teixeira in the first inning. Baker scattered a total of just four hits in his outing, walking two and striking out six. He walked away with the no-decision for the fifth straight start. Next up for Baker will be the Mariners for the third time since Aug. 5. Baker has allowed 10 earned runs in 10 2/3 innings against Seattle this season.

home_pitcher_note: Feierabend's second start of the season was much improved, as he gave up one run to the Athletics in five innings while striking out five and walking none. But he will be going up against the Twins, who did not offer him a soft landing when he went against them on Aug. 17 in his first Major League start of the season. He lasted just three innings and gave up five runs in the first inning alone. The Twins got 10 hits off him, and he only struck out one.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander continues to be one of the best surprises in the starting rotation. Perkins picked up yet another victory in his first career start against the Angels, pitching eight shutout innings while scattering just five hits. He has now won nine of his last 10 decisions. He's also pitched at least six innings in each of his last 10 starts, dating back to June 30. The Twins will need Perkins to continue his trend of eating up innings in his next start against the Mariners. Perkins is 1-0 in two starts vs. Seattle this season.

home_pitcher_note: The Cleveland offense saved Sowers from earning his seventh loss of the season. Against the Rangers in a tough park for pitchers, Sowers allowed seven runs on eight hits and a walk and struck out only two in 3 2/3 innings. Manager Eric Wedge said Sowers struggled out of the stretch and that was evident when he allowed six runs in the fourth inning and couldn't get out of it. But he was solid early on, which hasn't always been the case. He faced the minimum through the first two innings and Texas manufactured a run off him in the third before its big innings. Sowers' next start will be against the Mariners, against whom he earned one of his two victories this season. It wasn't a glorious victory though as he allowed four runs in six innings in the start.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez pitched six innings in his last start, against the Athletics on Sunday, and struck out seven. The mistakes he made ended up in the seats, as all three runs allowed came on solo homers. Hernandez threw 106 pitches (67 strikes) and picked up the win. In his last start against the Indians, on July 18, Hernandez gave up two earned runs in six innings and struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Reyes did everything he could to earn a victory his last time out except go the distance. He pitched his longest outing of the season, seven innings, and tallied his highest pitch count of the year, 107 pitches. Those were the only high numbers he put up, though, holding the Rangers to just one run on four hits and four walks as he struck out four. He left in line for his third victory in four starts with the Indians, but the bullpen didn't hold his lead. Saturday will be Reyes' first career start against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn makes his final start of August still looking for his first win in the month. The veteran has lost all five of his starts this month, and the latest one was the 100th of his Major League career. Three of the losses occurred in games in which he surrendered three or fewer runs in at least six innings -- a quality start. Since the start of the 2005 season, he has the lowest run support among American League starters. This will be his second start of the season against the Indians, who beat him in Cleveland on April 30.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson notched his third no-decision in as many starts with the Indians on Monday in Detroit, though he certainly deserved a better fate. In 6 1/3 innings of work, Jackson limited the Tigers to three runs on seven hits with no walks and six strikeouts. He served up a pair of home runs, but both were solo shots. Jackson, who has never faced the Mariners, did a good job commanding his fastball and has shown improvement with his breaking and offspeed pitches.
away_pitcher_note: The Australian left-hander picked up his first career win as a starting pitcher in his outing Tuesday against the Twins. He went seven innings for the second straight start, allowing two runs and just five hits. The 25-year-old has looked solid in three of his four starts since returning from Triple-A Tacoma, where he went for a few weeks to stretch his arm out in late July. In two appearances out of the bullpen against the Indians this season, Rowland-Smith has given up one earned run over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Harrison beat the Royals, 3-2, on Wednesday by holding them to two runs in 6 2/3 innings. He possesses good fastball command but must mix in his slider and changeup. He is 5-2 with a 4.35 ERA in his last seven starts but one of those losses was to the Mariners in Arlington on July 31, when he allowed six runs in 42/3 innings. He is 3-2 with a 5.01 ERA at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: On Monday, Silva will make his first start since he was put on the disabled list two weeks ago with right triceps tendinitis. Silva felt soreness in his elbow after his last start, which came on Aug. 15 against his former team, the Twins. The Mariners were feeling a little sore after the outing as well. The 29-year-old right-hander was rocked for nine hits and nine runs in 3 1/3 innings to take his 14th loss of the season. In the five starts before we went on the DL for the fourth time of his career, Silva racked up an 11.39 ERA and had struck out as many as he had walked. In three starts against the Rangers this season, Silva is 1-0 with a 5.17 ERA. Lifetime, he is 4-4 with a 4.76 ERA in 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy has made two starts since being recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma. In his last start, against the Angels, he allowed two runs (one earned) in six innings, but the Rangers blew a 5-2 lead and he was left with no-decision. McCarthy is 3-4 with a 3.94 ERA in 14 career games, including 13 starts, at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington. He is 0-2 with a 9.28 ERA in four games, including two career starts, against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Feierabend looked solid against the Twins on Wednesday, when he went seven innings and gave up three earned runs while striking out four. He got stronger as the game went along and made a vast improvement upon his last time out against the Twins, on Aug. 17, when he gave up six earned runs in three innings. Two out of Feierabend's three starts since he came up for that first Twins game have been solid, and he's walked only three batters in 15 innings, while striking out 10.

home_pitcher_note: Nippert is filling in for Vicente Padilla, who is on the disabled list with a strained left hamstring. Nippert is 0-2 with a 9.64 ERA in two starts after losing to the Angels, 3-1, on Friday. He took a two-hit shutout into the sixth before growing tired and allowing three runs. Opponents are hitting .329 off him, including .357 with runners in scoring position. He allowed two runs in 4 1/3 innings in a relief appearance against the Mariners earlier this season.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez found trouble in nearly every inning against the Indians on Friday night. Though Hernandez never recored a 1-2-3 inning, he was still able to leave on top after six innings, allowing just two runs on six hits. Ground-ball double plays got him out of jams in the first two innings before the Indians cracked him for single runs in the third and fourth innings, respectively. Still, with the Tribe putting its first two runners on base in those particular innings, Hernandez showed enough poise to minimize the damage and keep the Mariners on top throughout his entire outing. In four starts against the Rangers this season, Hernandez is 0-2 with a 3.38 ERA. Lifetime, he is 4-6 with a 4.24 ERA in 14 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: The highly touted right-hander makes his Major League starting debut slightly more than a month after being sent to Triple-A Tacoma to make the transition from late-inning reliever to starter. He was superb out of the bullpen, leading the team in saves with 10 and posting a 1.47 ERA in 40 relief appearances. Morrow has a plethora of pitches that he has developed, including a 94-mph fastball and 78-79-mph curveball. He also worked on a changeup during his stint in the Minors to prepare for this month -- and beyond. His success as a starter could help determine how busy the front office is during the offseason in shoring up a rotation that has wobbled most of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte struggled early against the Blue Jays on Sunday and couldn't bounce back as he picked up his second straight loss. He surrendered three runs in the opening frame, and the Toronto batters worked Pettitte for 30 pitches in the first inning. The veteran was more economical as the game continued, leaving with 112 throws after 6 1/3 innings. Pettitte was tagged for six runs on 10 hits, striking out four with one walk. It marked his second straight start giving up six earned runs. In his only start against the Mariners this season, Pettitte held Seattle to two runs and eight hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Australian left-hander picked up his second consecutive win with another quality start on Sunday against the Indians. Rowland-Smith allowed two runs (one earned) in 6 1/3 innings to help the Mariners sweep the Indians. He struck out just two and walked one, primarily forcing the Indians to pound the ball into the ground. In his past two outings, Rowland-Smith has allowed four runs over 13 1/3 innings. In three relief appearances against the Yankees this season, Rowland-Smith is 0-0 with a 4.91 ERA over 3 2/3 innings. Last season, he picked up a win against the Bronx Bombers after throwing four scoreless innings of relief.
away_pitcher_note:
Ponson had his fourth consecutive subpar outing in a 13-9 win over Detroit on

home_pitcher_note: Feierabend will fill in for Carlos Silva, who was scratched from the start on Sunday afternoon.
away_pitcher_note: Mussina will try to close within two wins of his long-pursued 20-win mark when he takes on the Mariners on Sunday at Safeco Field, wrapping up New York's three-game series. Mussina pitched effectively into the seventh inning on Tuesday at Tropicana Field, tying a season high with eight strikeouts as he worked two-run ball. Mussina is 2-0 with a 4.09 ERA in two starts this season against Seattle, beating them on May 3 and May 24 at Yankee Stadium. He will be starting for the first time at Safeco Field since 2005, a facility where he is 3-0 with a 3.23 ERA in six career starts -- five with the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez gets another shot at the Rangers and his 10th victory of the season in the series opener against Texas. The right-hander surrendered a run in the first inning on Wednesday in Arlington, and it ended up being the only run of the game, as the ace lost his ninth game of the season. Hernandez has made 16 quality starts this season, but he lost two of them and settled for a no-decision in seven others. Only three other starting pitchers in the American League have received less run support than Hernandez this season, and one of them is teammate Jarrod Washburn. Pitching a shutout might be just the thing Hernandez must do to become Seattle's first double-digit winner in 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla is coming off the disabled list after being sidelined with both a strained left hamstring and inflammation in a muscle joint between his right shoulder and neck. The inflammation has been a problem for most of the second half and he is 0-2 with a 7.71 ERA in his last four starts. He is 9-3 with a 5.33 ERA on the road this year and 3-5 with a 4.86 ERA in 13 games, including 11 starts, against the Mariners in his career.

home_pitcher_note: After making 26 relief appearances this season, the rookie left-hander gets his first MLB start in the series finale. It's unlikely that he will pitch the necessary five innings to qualify for a win because the game plan is to make this a "Bullpen Day," with relievers needing the work getting to pitch one or two innings apiece. Jimenez has gone as far as four innings in relief, but that was more than a month ago and his arm is not stretched out enough to throw 60-some pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood had a three-game winning streak snapped when he lost to the Red Sox, 8-1, on Friday, allowing seven runs in six innings. He is now 3-3 with a 4.78 ERA in seven starts since the All-Star break while missing time because of a strained groin muscle. He is 4-5 with a 4.74 ERA on the road this year. Opponents are batting .312 off him, including .359 by right-handed hitters. He is 7-8 with a 4.51 ERA in his career against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Requiring more than a week of healing time after cutting his right middle and ring fingers in a dugout accident in Detroit on Sept. 2, Weaver has been cleared to return to the mound after several side sessions. He hasn't pitched since Aug. 30 when he went five innings against the Rangers, yielding three earned runs. Winless in his past four outings with one loss, he hasn't won a game since Aug. 8 against the Yankees. Weaver is 5-2 in nine career outings against the Mariners with a 5.17 ERA, and he's 1-1 in two starts against Seattle this year with a 6.94 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: For the second start of his career, it will be interesting to see how Morrow bounces back from losing a no-hit bid with two outs in the eighth inning of his first start. Morrow, who spent a month at Triple-A Tacoma making the transition from reliever to starter, had electric stuff in shutting down the Yankees at Safeco Field, commanding the strike zone with fastballs, curveballs and changeups. He also throws a slider and a cutter, which he didn't need against New York. After throwing 82 pitches in his last outing at Tacoma, the most the right-hander had thrown in his two professional seasons, Morrow was supposed to throw a maximum of 95 pitches against the Yankees. But he ended up throwing 106 pitches. The Rangers, who lead the Majors in runs scored, will offer a stout challenge.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders' seventh crack at his 15th win produced gold, as he allowed only two solo homers in 7 1/3 sturdy innings in Chicago on Sunday. An adjustment made with pitching coach Mike Butcher, bringing the lefty back in balance and getting the heat back in his fastball, has helped Saunders break out of a mini-slump with back-to-back efforts calling to mind his All-Star first half. Saunders was throwing 93 mph in the eighth inning on Sunday, a very good sign. Saunders is 1-1 with a 7.63 ERA in three career starts against the Yankees and took a no-decision in his start against them this year. He's 6-4 with a 4.60 ERA at home, having fared much better on the road.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander from Australia continues to impress as a starter. He held the Yankees to seven hits and three runs over 6 1/3 innings in his previous start, but settled for a no-decision in the only game the Mariners lost in the three-game series. Three of the four walks he surrendered came in the same inning, but he worked out of the jam without surrendering a run. He has had better luck against right-handed batters this season than lefties, holding the righties a .220 average (49-for-223) while lefties are 41-for-129, a .318 mark.

home_pitcher_note: It looked like it could be a long night for Garland, who struggled in the first inning against the Yankees on Monday. He allowed a run on three hits and a walk in the opening frame but settled down after that as he allowed just three hits and no runs over his next six innings. In all, Garland threw seven innings, allowing one run on six hits while striking out four and walking two. Garland is 7-3 with a 3.35 ERA in 13 career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching on two hours' notice worked remarkably well for the rookie left-hander, who was an emergency starter for right-hander Carlos Silva last Sunday against the Yankees and surrendered just two runs over seven innings. Both runs came via solo home runs. Feierabend relies on moving the ball around, and he's not afraid to challenge the hitters inside. He faced the Angels twice last season and was the losing pitcher in both games, allowing 16 hits and nine earned runs in 9 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Losing for the first time in eight starts, since July 27, Santana yielded six runs (five earned) on nine hits in 6 1/3 innings. There was nothing wrong with his mid-90s heater and slider -- he maintained his superb strikeouts-to-walks ratio with six whiffs and one free pass, giving him 85 strikeouts against 13 walks in his past 11 outings. Mistakes resulting in the long ball were Santana's undoing, with Alex Rodriguez going deep for three runs and Johnny Damon bashing a two-run homer. Santana is 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA in three starts against the Mariners this year and 5-2 in 10 lifetime outings with a 4.53 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed ace makes his third attempt at winning his 10th game of the season. It will be against the AL West Division champs, whom Felix defeated in his first start against them this season, an 8-5 victory on April 11. Hernandez is coming off a peculiar outing against the Rangers. He wobbled in each of the four innings he pitched, walking four batters and hitting three. He did not pitch at least five innings for just the second time in 28 starts; the first time was caused by an injury suffered at home plate in a game against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Davies allowed four earned runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings against the Twins on Wednesday in a 7-1 loss. He has had a problem with running up high pitch counts and did so again, needing 105 pitches before getting pulled. Davies will next kick off a four-game series against Seattle. He received a no-decision in a 4-3 loss on July 13 against the Mariners, going seven innings while allowing three earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: The big right-hander missed his last start because of back spasms and was away from the team for three days, returning to his home in Minneapolis for the birth of his second child. It has been a trying year for the veteran sinkerball specialist, who has left far too many pitches up in the strike zone, resulting in one victory since April and that is not what the organization had in mind when they signed him to a four-year, $48 million contract last November. He needs a string of quality starts to get a positive mindset heading into the winter and the offensively  challenged Royals could be just what he needs. Silva has a 5-3 career record against Kansas City and has faced the Royals once this season, holding them to two runs over six innings in a game the Mariners won, 4-3, on July 13. He received a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Duckworth went five innings while allowing two earned runs on seven hits in Thursday's 3-2 extra-inning win against the Twins. The right-hander received no decision while walking two and striking out five. He threw 55 strikes in 85 pitches. Duckworth has not faced Seattle this season.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander, who flirted with a no-hitter in his first Major League start before departing in the eighth inning, didn't have quite the same good fortunes in his encore start against the AL West champion Angels. Even so, the five hits and four walks he surrendered produced just two runs over five innings. A curveball that was sharp and effective against the Yankees, wasn't quite as brisk and sharp against the Angels, especially after the first two innings. He had good control with his first 30 pitches, throwing 21 strikes, but ended up with 51 strikes and 49 balls.

home_pitcher_note: Meche's command was off on Friday night at Cleveland, his pitches the most misdirected they've been since the All-Star break in the eyes of manager Trey Hillman. Meche lasted only five innings and ran up 108 pitches (72 strikes) and gave up six runs -- the most he's surrendered since way back in April. Still, he walked just one and had seven strikeouts, so he did have something working for him. He faces his old club, the Mariners, for the fifth time (1-1). This year, he had no decision on July 12, giving up four runs in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With another quality start behind him, the left-hander keeps strengthening his pursuit of a starting role on the 2009 pitching staff. He held the Angels to four hits and three runs over 6 1/3 innings in his last start but had to settle for his sixth no-decision in nine starts this season. His strikeout-walk ratio (65-42) is nothing to write home to Australia about, but he has demonstrated a knack for pitching out of trouble.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke perhaps wasn't at his sharpest on Saturday against the Indians, but he held them to three runs in six innings and notched his 11th victory. In his last six starts, he's given up just nine earned runs in 36 2/3 innings for a 2.21 ERA. In that stretch he has two wins, two losses and two no-decisions. There's little doubt that Greinke has pitched well enough this season to have a better record. Against the Mariners, he pitched one of his best games this year, going the distance on April 14 for a five-hit, 5-1 victory.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander breezed through seven out of nine Angels' batters in his last start, but the two he had trouble with -- Torii Hunter and Juan Rivera -- went 5-for-6 with two doubles, a home run and drove in three of the four runs Feierabend surrendered in his sixth start of the season. He continues to pitch well in a starting role, keeping the team in the game when he's on the mound, changing speeds and moving the ball around. Without overpowering stuff, Feierabend depends on precision to get the job done.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland labored through five innings against the Rangers on Sunday. The lefty allowed three runs on four hits while striking out six en route to a no-decision. Eveland said he felt a little out of sync, and he had to battle just to keep the team close. He gave up two RBI doubles to Nelson Cruz. Eveland, who has now thrown 30 more innings then his previous career high, said he feels like he's wearing down a bit. He is 3-0 with a 3.57 ERA in three starts against Seattle this season.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed ace makes his fourth attempt at winning his 10th game of the season as the Mariners try to keep from becoming the second team in franchise history to play an entire season without a double-digit winner. Hernandez has pitched plenty of games that were worthy of victory, but lack of run support has been an Achilles' heel for the 22-year-old. He has the second-lowest run support average in the AL this season (3.9).

home_pitcher_note: Saarloos will be making his first Major League start in more than a year, forced into emergency duty because All-Star Justin Duchscherer, who was hoping to be activated from the disabled list Saturday after spending a month on the shelf with inflammmation in his surgically repaired right hip, had to stop throwing after 10 pitches in a simulated game Thursday. Saarloos, who spent last season in the Reds organization, was promoted from Triple-A Sacramento on Aug. 18 for his second stint of the year with Oakland. A soft-tosser who doesn't get many strikeouts, Saarloos has tremendous movement on his pitches and gets a ton of ground balls with his two-seam fastball when he's on his game.
away_pitcher_note: Silva is coming off an encouraging outing at Kansas City. Although he wound up taking a loss, Silva allowed just two earned runs on eight hits through 5 1/3 innings. Silva did not allow a walk after issuing four in his previous start against Texas. He now has 58 zero-walk starts since 2004. Only Greg Maddux (67) has more over that span.

home_pitcher_note: A hard-throwing rookie who was acquired in the July trade that sent Rich Harden and Chad Gaudin to the Cubs, Gallagher put together the best start of his career on Tuesday against the visiting Angels. Coming off a strange outing in Detroit, where he threw four hitless innings but walked six and was lifted with a pitch count of 88, Gallagher didn't walk a batter over seven innings of four-hit work while striking out six to beat the Angels. Armed with a fastball that hits 95 on the radar gun and an above-average changeup and curveball, Gallagher, 22, will be making his first career start against the M's.
away_pitcher_note: Morrow will be making his fourth career start as he works through the transitional phase involved with going from reliever to starter. He took a step back last Tuesday in Kansas City, working just four innings and surrendering six earned runs. Morrow cited poor mechanics for that performance and hopes to have the flaws worked out so that he can go deeper in the game. Morrow threw two wild pitches in Kansas City, which underscored the mechanical problems. Over his previous 49 1/3 innings, Morrow had three wild pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith has a string of six consecutive quality starts. He worked six innings last Wednesday in Kansas City, allowing just one run on three hits. He did surrender four walks to the Royals and will be looking to cut down on that total as he continues his September rise. The six consecutive quality starts is the most for a Seattle pitcher since Jamie Moyer had six in a row in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Santana received a couple extra days of rest this time around the rotation, but he said it wasn't because he felt any fatigue, so it will be interesting to see how he pitches on rest he didn't necessarily need. His last start was against the Mariners at home and, despite allowing just two runs in seven innings, he didn't figure in the decision. He only struck out three in the outing, which was his first with fewer than five strikeouts since June 2 in Seattle. He's 2-0 in four starts against the Mariners this season with a 2.48 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: His last start notwithstanding, the rookie left-hander has done a solid job since he's been in the rotation. Feierabend doesn't have overpowering stuff, as evidenced by the .349 opponents' batting average, but has shown a knack for moving the ball around, challenging hitters inside and throwing strikes. A reliever early in the season, he could become a swingman in the future, a spot starter and lefty reliever.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver, pitching for postseason starting consideration, delivered one of his most impressive efforts of the year on Wednesday night in Oakland. He struck out eight hitters and walked three (one intentionally) while yielding six hits and one earned run in six innings. The right-hander showed his competitive nature when he left the bases loaded by striking out Jack Cust and Kurt Suzuki. With 12 days of rest before his previous start, Weaver said it was the best he's felt all year in terms of stuff and command. He's 2-1 with a 4.58 ERA in three outings against the Mariners this year and 6-2 with a 4.65 ERA in 10 career starts. Weaver is 3-2 with a 5.30 ERA lifetime in six starts at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: The best right-handed pitcher in the Major Leagues who hasn't won 10 games goes after the double-digit number for the fifth time against the Mariners' AL West rival Angels. Felix has pitched back-to-back stellar games, surrendering three runs, but the Seattle offense has been virtually non-existent. Hernandez, 22, will reach the 200-inning plateau by pitching 5 1/3 innings against the division champions. Felix is coming off a complete-game loss to the Athletics and has the lowest ERA in franchise history (3.38) for a pitcher with at least 10 losses.
away_pitcher_note: After making it through two innings unscathed in his last outing, Garland's third inning turned into disaster. In retiring just one batter, he faced 10 Rangers and allowed nine runs (eight earned) on eight hits. With that, his ERA rose from 4.47 and his September ERA rose from 3.79 to 6.75. His post-All Star ERA now stands at 5.78. With Wednesday likely his last start of the regular season to plead his case to be in the playoff rotation, he'll have to do better against the Mariners. He's 2-1 in three starts against them this season with a 4.00 ERA. His one loss against them came at Safeco Field, when he allowed six runs (three earned) in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: It isn't yet official, but Jimenez is the likely replacement for right-hander Carlos Silva, who has been scratched from what would have been his final start of the season because of back soreness. Jimenez has one start under his belt this season, tossing three scoreless innings against the Rangers in an emergency start situation. If he gets the call again, he probably would go no further than three innings again as he has not been stretched out.
away_pitcher_note: Joe Saunders' battle with a kidney stones, which forced him to be pushed back to the weekend, has given Moseley his 10th starting opportunity of the season. The right-hander has fared well in his past two starts, going five innings each time in games won by the Angels against the Yankees -- when they the AL West title -- and in Texas against the Rangers. He has yielded a total of 11 hits and five earned runs in those 10 innings, walking four and striking out nine. With good movement on his two-seam fastball and quality offspeed stuff, Moseley hopes to control the Mariners. He has had success against Seattle, with a 2.93 ERA and a 1-1 record in five career appearances, one as a starter. He's 0-1 with a 7.71 ERA against the Mariners this year.

home_pitcher_note: Morrow was stellar against the Athletics for 6 1/3 innings in his last start, holding Oakland without a hit until there was one out in the sixth inning. But Seattle's unpredictable bullpen helped lose a three-run lead and Morrow was left with a no-decision. Morrow is still building his arm strength after being converted to a starter, and he threw a career-high 113 pitches against the Athletics. The more stamina he builds, the longer he'll be able to go, but that likely won't be until next season. He has demonstrated a tendency to lose concentration after getting two quick outs, adding to his pitch count.
away_pitcher_note: Gallagher followed up his last outing, in which he allowed just one run over seven innings on Tuesday against the Angels, with another solid performance against the Mariners on Sunday. Gallagher went 6 2/3 innings, allowing three runs on four hits while striking out five in a loss. The righty left the game in the sixth with two runners on base and was credited with two more runs when reliever Jerry Blevins gave up two hits. Overall, Gallagher showed good command of his fastball and slider, and kept his pitches low and in the strike zone.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith makes his final start of the season, but certainly not the last one of his career. The lefty from Australia will report to camp next February with a spot in the five-man rotation virtually locked up after a string of quality starts. He worked seven innings against the AL West champion Angels in his last start, surrendering one earned run and one unearned. But he still didn't get a win as the Mariners scored one run for him. He has left games eight times with leads or the game tied, but the Mariners have lost six of them.
away_pitcher_note: Smith overcame a shaky first couple of innings in Texas on Monday to put in five solid innings of six-hit work, but the 3-2 lead he handed the Oakland bullpen was wiped out by a ninth-inning homer. Smith, a rookie acquired in the Dan Haren trade with Arizona, will be making 32nd start of the season, and the A's are 14-17 in his first 31. The Major League leader with 15 pickoffs this season, Smith is 1-0 with a 0.00 ERA in two starts against the Mariners this season, having allowed eight hits and four walks over 12 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The knuckleball specialist makes his 14th start of the season as a replacement for lefty Ryan Feierabend, knocked out of his scheduled outing because of elbow discomfort. Dickey will be well-rested. His last appearance came on Sept. 18, when he pitched one inning of relief against the Royals. He has pitched just 5 2/3 innings this month. His last start came on Aug. 20 and it was a rough one. The White Sox scored eight runs in two innings. He returned to the bullpen after that start and has surrendered one earned run in his last seven appearances.
away_pitcher_note: A rookie acquired in the July deal that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies, Outman gave up 10 hits and walked two over six innings on Tuesday in Texas, but he was leading 4-3 when he felt the game, which the Rangers rallied to win, leaving Outman with a no-decision. It was Outman's third and longest start for the A's, who view him as a potential mainstay of their starting rotation as early as 2009. Outman, who hasn't been allowed to throw more than 100 pitches in any of his outings, has never faced the Mariners.
