home_pitcher_note:
This will mark Liriano's first career Opening Day start, a significant achievement for the pitcher who is just 2 1/2 years removed from Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery. Liriano was given the nod in the contest after the club's projected Opening Day starter, Scott Baker, was placed on the 15-day disabled list with right shoulder stiffness.

As for Liriano, he's looking to deliver a standout season in his second full season back from surgery. The pitcher's velocity and trademark slider might not be the same as they were back in 2006, his breakout rookie season, but Liriano's pitching repertoire can still intimidate hitters. That's particularly true now thanks to his new changeup, which manager Ron Gardenhire described as "Santana-like" this spring.

After posting a 6-1 record with a 2.74 ERA in 11 starts when he returned to the Twins rotation on Aug.1 of last year, Liriano went 1-2 with a 4.94 ERA in eight Grapefruit League starts this spring.
away_pitcher_note:
The ace of the Mariners' starting rotation makes his second career Opening Night start in the past three seasons. The first one was an eight-inning shutout effort against the Athletic two years ago.

Hernandez is coming off an up-and-down Spring Training, pitching superbly for Venezuela in two World Baseball Classic appearances but scuffling a bit in Cactus League games. He finished camp with a 0-0 record and 8.36 ERA. But he pronounced himself healthy and ready to go in the opener against the Twins after his final outing of the spring and is looking for his first career victory at the Metrodome, have lost his only decision in the Teflon-roofed facility.

After finishing among the AL leaders in several categories last season, including the eighth-lowest ERA, sixth in road ERA (3.01), seventh with 7.8 strikeouts per nine innings, he is due for some run support. King Felix had a 2.72 ERA in the 11 games that he received a no-decision, allowing three or fewer runs in nine of those starts.

home_pitcher_note: Blackburn was limited for a time this spring by a sore left knee, which he had surgically repaired during the offseason, but the knee issue appears to be behind him now. Having logged close to 200 innings, Blackburn tired at the end of last season but he worked this winter to improve his stamina in order to try to pitch 200-plus innings in his second full Major League season. He'll be pitching on six days' rest for his first start of the season due to some late rotation changes, but the Twins still expect him to throw around 90 pitches when he faces the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard (6-4, 3.67 in '08) had a pain-free Spring Training, and that was the primary issue after having shoulder surgery last September. The Mariners' Opening Day starter last season had an injury-plagued first season with the Mariners. He was 1-1 with a 5.56 ERA during the Cactus League.

home_pitcher_note: The Twins starter who possesses the best command of his pitches, Slowey showed this spring why he's considered to be on the verge of a breakout season. Having averaged just 1.4 walks per nine innings in his career, Slowey continued that trend this spring. Heading into his final spring start, Slowey had issued just one walk in 20 1/3 innings. Another reason for optimism is that Slowey continues to improve his offspeed pitches as he starts the season in the rotation for the second consecutive year.
away_pitcher_note: Silva (4-15, 6.46 in '08) begins pursuit of a comeback season in his old stomping grounds. He had his best years with the Twins, from 2004-07, reaching double digits in wins three times and pitching at least 200 innings twice. He finished the spring strong, tossing four shutout innings before surrendering a two-run home run in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: One of the surprises for the Twins in the rotation last season, Perkins will try to see if he can duplicate that success in just his second stint as a starter in the Majors. One key for Perkins will be to limit the number of long balls that he gives up. The lefty has been working on a slider this spring to use against right-handers, which the Twins hope will be an additional pitch that he can trust in critical situations.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn (5-14, 4.69 in '08) begins the final year of his four-year contract with fingers crossed that he receives more run support. That has been an issue practically from the day he joined the Mariners, for whom he has a 23-43 record. He was 2-2 record with a 6.12 ERA in seven Cactus League outings.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, ranked by Baseball America as the top prospect in the A's organization and No. 7 in all of baseball, earned a spot in Oakland's rotation in his first trip to big league Spring Training, A 21-year-old who's drawn high praise from coaches and teammates for his poise on the mound, Anderson was a busy young man in 2008; he split the regular season at Single-A Stockton and Double-A Midland, pitched in the All-Star Futures Game at Yankee Stadium, played for Team USA in the Beijing Olympics, and finished the year on Triple-A Sacramento's playoff roster. A second-round pick of the Diamondbacks in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, Anderson was acquired by Oakland in the December 2007 trade that sent Dan Haren to Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: The reliever-turned-starter begins the '09 season exactly where he ended the '08 season -- as a member of the five-man rotation. The 26-year-old from Australia hopes to pick up where he left off. He was the Mariners' most effective starter the final six weeks of last season, reeling off eight consecutive quality starts during August and September. Rowland-Smith must keep the ball down and change speeds to be effective. He had a 1-1 record and 3.94 ERA in four appearances against the Athletics last season.

home_pitcher_note: Outman, 24, was acquired by Oakland last July in the trade that sent Joe Blanton to the Phillies. He made his big league debut with the A's in early September after compiling a 35-18 record with a 2.99 ERA over 107 Minor League appearances, including 67 starts, and four of his six appearances with Oakland came as a starter. Considered a longshot to win a spot in the starting rotation this spring, Outman secured the No. 5 job with a strong final outing against the Royals in the team's second-to-last day in the desert, earning the nod for Oakland's home opener. A 10th-round pick of the Phillies in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft, Outman made one start against the Mariners in 2008, allowing three earned runs over six innings of a loss.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed Hernandez twisted his ankle in the first inning of his first start and it bothered him off and on over eight innings, but he still held the Twins to one run in the regular season opener. Hernandez escaped a first-and-second, none-out jam in the first inning without allowing a run and dodged a bigger predicament in the fifth, when the Twins loaded the bases with none out. He surrendered just one run.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill, 21, wasn't particularly sharp in his big league debut Tuesday against the host Angels, but he did a nice job of limiting the damage done by the five hits and five walks (one intentional) he allowed over five innings. Making his big league debut and his first regular-season start above Double-A ball, Cahill might have earned the victory were it not for a dropped fly ball that led to the Angels' game-tying run in the bottom of the fifth. A sinkerball pitcher with above-average command, Cahill should be considerably more comfortable pitching in front of his home fans, and because he threw more than 100 pitches against the Angels, he'll be allowed to go six or seven innings if his pitch count allows it.
away_pitcher_note: The left-handed Bedard had his strikeout artistry working during his first start of the season, fanning eight Twins in a five-inning, 85-pitch outing at the Metrodome. He struck out at least one in each of the innings he pitched, but what could have been a called third strike on Michael Cuddyer in the fifth inning wasn't and the Twins' designated hitter delivered a two-run single to cut a four-run Seattle lead to a one-run nail-biter. Bedard hit a batter, but didn't walk anyone.

home_pitcher_note: The first start in Silva's second season with the Mariners had a few rough parts, most noticeably a pair of two-run home runs that he surrendered to the Twins. Silva got the ball up early in the game and his former teammates made him pay. He made an adjustment after the second inning and pitched the way a sinkerball pitcher is supposed to pitch, keeping the ball low, resulting in seven consecutive outs without having a ball leave the infield.  He will need more consistency to come out of the doldrums that started last May.
away_pitcher_note: Loux, who lives by the command of his sinking fastball, had a strong spring until a late outing against the Diamondbacks in which he yielded seven runs in four innings. He hasn't started a Major League game since 2003 with the Tigers and is 1-4 lifetime with a 6.41 ERA in 21 appearances, seven as a starter. He was out of baseball in 2007 before signing a Minor League deal with the Angels and emerging as the Pacific Coast League Pitcher of the Year with Salt Lake, earning seven relief appearances for the Angels. He'll throw a breaking ball and changeup to keep hitters off balance, but the sinker is his bread-and-butter.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn makes his first home start of the season on the heels of one of his best outings anywhere in a Mariners uniform. He held the Twins to five singles and a walk over eight innings and didn't allow of any them to reach scoring position until the eighth. He was efficient with his pitches, throwing just 96, and used an improved sinker to get key outs.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver had one of the most memorable outings of his young career on Friday when he allowed just one unearned run against the Red Sox in the Angels' first game since the death of pitcher Nick Adenhart. Weaver showed excellent poise despite the loss of one of his best friends, who was supposed to become his roommate on Sunday. Weaver honored his fallen teammate by striking out eight batters and allowing just four hits against the mighty Red Sox lineup. Weaver is 6-2 with a 5.07 ERA against Seattle in his career.

home_pitcher_note: An injury to left-hander Ryan Rowland-Smith gives Jakubauskas the first start of his Major League career but the 63rd of his professional career. The former Independent League hurler was the biggest surprise of Spring Training, compiling a team-best 1.99 ERA. That was good enough to earn a spot in Seattle's bullpen, where he has made two appearances this season. He has been able to handle left-handed and right-handed hitters equally well, but will be on a strict pitch-count limit in his first start, probably around the 60-pitch mark.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders seemingly made just two mistakes against the Red Sox on Saturday, but they both came in the form of two-run home runs in the Angels' 5-4 loss at Angel Stadium. Saunders actually pitched well despite the loss, allowing seven hits over seven innings while striking out two. The loss also marked the first time in his career that he's lost in April. Saunders is 4-1 with a 4.61 ERA in his career against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander struck out a season-best eight batters in his last start, but didn't have the same command he had against the Twins in his Opening Day win against the Twins. Three of the seven hits Hernandez surrendered to the Athletics went for extra-bases and drove in four of the five runs, including a decisive two-run home run to Oakland slugger Jack Cust, the second of his career off Hernandez.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander's second start of the season didn't last much longer than his first, with the Rangers chasing him after five innings and 97 pitches last Saturday. However, both Verlander and manager Jim Leyland pointed to a vast improvement in his pitches, both with good velocity and easier effort while regaining some movement, evidenced by his eight strikeouts against four walks. Leyland wants to see Verlander lasting around seven innings consistently within the next three to five starts, which makes Verlander's matchup with the Mariners a big stepping stone. The more outs he can get early in counts, the deeper he'll last into the game.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander pitched the best game of his tenure with the Mariners in his previous outing, holding the Athletics to two hits over the first eight innings and three hits in 8 1/3 innings. He retired 11 of 12 batters during one stretch and 13 straight in another. His left shoulder obviously is healthy again, and he threw 102 pitches overall, 67 of them for strikes. He has 14 strikeouts in his first two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson couldn't repeat the dominance from his first Tigers start when he took the mound last Sunday against the Rangers, but he kept the Tigers close enough for a late-inning comeback. The Rangers roughed up Jackson for two-run homers in the first and third innings, but he not only held Texas scoreless from there, he lasted six innings in the process. His 13 innings through two starts has reinforced team hopes that he'll emerge as an innings-eater on the staff, not to mention a maturing young starter set to follow up on last year's success with Tampa Bay. Jackson won both of his previous career starts against the Mariners, allowing a lone run on nine hits over 15 combined innings.

home_pitcher_note: Silva had his best outing in several months, holding the Angels to two runs over seven innings in the Mariners' home opener. Unfortunately for him, the Mariners also scored two runs while he was on the mound, so he had to settle for a no-decision. The good news is he had command of the strike zone and kept the ball down most of the time, resulting in just six outfield putouts.
away_pitcher_note: Porcello's Major League debut Thursday at Toronto turned on a pair of home runs that sent him to defeat. However, he still gave a good look at the poise and pitching acumen that convinced the Tigers he could handle the jump from Class A ball to the Majors at the age of 20. He was originally slated to make his follow-up start at home Tuesday against the White Sox, but the rainout prompted the Tigers to push him back to the weekend series and back on the road. It not only keeps Detroit's top three starts in line, it gives the Tigers a chance to conserve innings on their young starter, who pitched just 125 innings last year as a teenager at Class A Lakeland.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander retired the first 12 batters he faced in his previous outing on Wednesday, extending his scoreless streak to 12 consecutive innings to start the season. Both streaks ended during a two-batter sequence in the fifth inning, when a single and home run put a dent in his first home outing of the season. Even so, he took the game through six innings on 87 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine looked sharp in his last outing, his second of the season, when he held the Yankees to two runs in five innings to earn a no-decision on Wednesday. The right-hander is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Among those other pitches, Sonnanstine has added a changeup to his repertoire this spring, which he is fast gaining confidence in the more he masters it. The right-hander's mantra is to dispatch hitters one way or the other in three pitches, which allows him to get deeper into the games and save the bullpen. Sonnanstine is 1-1 with a 2.66 ERA in three career starts against the Mariners and is 1-0 with a 1.26 ERA in two starts at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: The right-handed Jakubauskas made a solid starting debut, holding the Angels scoreless for five innings before two singles in the sixth ended his strong outing. He became the tough-luck loser as the Mariners bullpen came apart, surrendering four hits and walking a batter during a five-run uprising. Jakubauskas, replacing Ryan Rowland-Smith in the rotation for a couple of weeks while the lefty recovers from triceps tendinitis, retired 15 of the first 18 batters he faced. He pounded the strike zone: 60 of his 81 pitches were strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann looked much improved in his second outing of the season Thursday night when he allowed two runs on nine hits while walking one and striking out three in six innings. The 6-foot-9, 280 pound right-hander, who was the Rays' No. 1 pick of the 2004 June Draft (fourth overall), had a slower than expected path to the Major Leagues due to injuries and problems with his mechanics. He showed marked improvement in pitching down with his fastball and with his breaking ball command, which proved exceptional all spring. While getting everything coordinated might be difficult for a taller pitcher, the downward angle of Niemann's pitches can make the baseball extremely hard to hit. This will be Niemann's first start and his first appearance against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander struggled through a 36-pitch second inning in his previous start, buckling down and taking the game into the seventh inning before calling it a night. He threw 104 pitches overall, and after the second inning, all of them were crucial as he tried to keep his team close -- which he did, striking out six and walking one. Hernandez has a career record of 1-1 against the Rays with a 2.54 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Shields wasn't as sharp as usual in his most recent start against the White Sox at Tropicana Field, where his career ERA is more than two runs better than it is on the road. Yet, even as he allowed five earned runs, he managed to pitch into the eighth and left with a lead. Shields is 1-1 with a 2.12 ERA in four career starts against the Mariners. In three starts at Safeco Field, his ERA is 2.38. He won his only start against Seattle in 2008.

home_pitcher_note: Loux is coming off the longest of his nine career starts in the Major Leagues, having gone seven innings while yielding three earned runs on 10 hits. Pounding the strike zone (no walks) and getting a dozen outs on the ground with his sinker, Loux struck out two hitters and would have yielded only two runs if a potential inning-ending double play had been turned cleanly. At 29, he is taking full advantage of his first starting opportunity since 2003 with the Tigers. He gets another shot at the Mariners after pitching effectively (5 1/3 innings, two earned runs) in Seattle's home opener.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard followed up the best outing of his Mariners career -- 8 1/3 innings of shutout ball in a 1-0 victory over the Oakland A's on April 12 -- with his second successive quality start in a loss to Detroit. Bedard went six innings against the Tigers, giving up two runs (one earned) on seven hits while striking out eight and walking two. Six of his eight punchouts were looking, and 68 of his 100 pitches were strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Ortega, a 23-year-old right-hander from Venezuela, makes his Major League debut hoping to emulate Matt Palmer, his teammate at Triple-A Salt Lake, who claimed his first Major League win on Friday night with six solid innings against the Tigers. Ortega has struggled in three outings at Salt Lake (1-1, 9.88 ERA) but he excelled there last season (5-0, 2.52 in six starts) after going 9-7 with a 3.73 ERA at Double-A Arkansas. The organization's Minor League Pitcher of the Year for 2008, he showed up in Spring Training with fatigue in the forearm/elbow area after throwing in the Venezuelan Winter League and was limited to some impressive bullpen sessions. He throws in the low 90s with movement and has a quality breaking ball.
away_pitcher_note: The slimmed-down 2009 version of Silva is still struggling to return to form as the ground-ball machine the Mariners signed before the 2008 season. His last start was another example. Silva gave up four runs on six hits in five innings against Detroit and was helped out by three Gold Glove-caliber plays by third baseman Adrian Beltre and another gem from shortstop Yuniesky Betancourt. Silva lost his only start against the Rays last year, going six innings and giving up four earned runs on eight hits, and hess 1-2 with a 2.84 against Tampa Bay in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver was impressive by showing his resiliency by lasting for seven strong innings despite allowing a run in each of the first three innings against the Tigers on Tuesday at Angel Stadium. Weaver bounced back after allowing two solo home runs by Curtis Granderson that came in the first and third innings. In all, Weaver tossed seven innings, allowing three runs on seven hits while striking out six. Weaver is 6-3 with a 5.22 ERA against the Mariners in 12 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn is off to his best start, by far, since joining the Mariners prior to the 2006 season. The lefty extended his winning streak to three straight with a solid seven-inning stint against the Rays, holding the reigning AL champs to five hits and two runs over seven innings. He was especially tough against left-handed batters, holding Carl Crawford (0-for-4), Carlos Pena (0-for-3) and Akinori Iwamura (0-for-3) in check all night. Six of Washburn's nine strikeouts were against the three lefties.

home_pitcher_note: All Danks has done this season is continue to establish himself as one the American League's top left-handed starters, and his last start at Baltimore on Wednesday was the latest example. On a night when he thought he was fighting himself, Danks allowed only a run on four hits, retiring 19 of the final 21 men he faced over seven innings. Seattle is one of four AL teams (Toronto, Boston and the Los Angeles Angels are the others) Danks has never beaten. In three career starts versus the Mariners, Danks is 0-3 with a 7.31 ERA in 16 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander absorbed his first major thumping of the season -- including Spring Training -- in his last outing. Making his second start in place of the injured Ryan Rowland-Smith, Jakubauskas surrendered 10 hits and six runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Rays. The pinpoint control he displayed throughout Spring Training and three regular-season outings, was missing.

home_pitcher_note: Colon's last effort, on Thursday at Baltimore, was a disaster. He exited after the third inning, having thrown 63 pitches, and was knocked around Camden Yards by the Orioles. Manager Ozzie Guillen said the early hook was to preserve Colon for later in the season, but Colon won't make it that far unless he improves -- and quickly. Lifetime against the Mariners, Colon is 13-11 with a 4.30 ERA in 28 career starts.

Making his second start in place of the injured Ryan Rowland-Smith, Jakubauskas surrendered 10 hits and six runs in 3 1/3 innings against the Rays. The pinpoint control he displayed throughout Spring Training and three regular-season outings, was missing.

away_pitcher_note: Hernandez had his best outing of the season in his last start, firing seven shutout innings and giving up four hits while striking out seven and walking three as the Mariners beat Tampa Bay, 1-0. Hernandez was in a battle all day, too, going pitch for pitch with the Rays' James Shields, who didn't let up a run other than a solo home run to Ichiro Suzuki on his second pitch of the game.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander suffered his second bout of wildness in two trips to the mound, walking five over 4 1/3 innings during Friday's 14-0 loss to the Blue Jays. Floyd, who walked seven in five innings during a victory at Detroit on April 13, gave up five earned runs on nine hits, while also striking out five. He worked in numerous heavy counts, throwing just 56 of his 94 pitches for strikes, and has issued 14 walks in 23 1/3 innings this season. Floyd had a 1-1 record with a 7.45 ERA against the Mariners last year and is 1-2 with an 8.10 ERA lifetime against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: The top of the Mariners starting rotation continues to produce like a well-oiled machine. Bedard and right-hander Felix Hernandez are giving Seattle one of the best one-two punches in the Major Leagues. Bedard has been solid with his fastball but especially with his curveball, which worked well against the Angels in his last start. The lefty has 29 strikeouts in 26 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: The sigh of relief from Silva could be heard all the way from Disneyland to the Space Needle as the right-hander finally tasted the fruits of victory in his most recent start. He scuffled at times, but worked the five innings needed to qualify for a win, ending a 14-start winless streak. Silva threw 82 pitches and 48 of them were for strikes, but he kept the Angels from erasing all of the three-run lead he got in the top of the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland, 25, picked up his first win of the season Sunday against the visiting Rays with his most encouraging outing of the year. Having lasted four innings and 4 2/3 innings in his two previous starts, Eveland made it through five against the defending American League champs, holding Tampa Bay to one run on four hits and three walks while striking out three. Born in Olympia, Wash., Eveland won all four of his starts against Seattle last season, posting a 2.55 ERA over 24 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn will be looking to bounce back from a rough outing against the Angels on Sunday. Washburn's former team hit two homers off him and generated six runs on eight hits as he absorbed his first loss of the season. To that point, the lefty had been a pleasant surprise in the rotation, compiling a 3-0 record and 1.71 ERA. Throughout his career, Washburn has had mixed results against Oakland, going 8-15 with a 4.10 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill, a 21-year-old rookie who'll be making his fifth start of the season, saw his ERA jump by nearly three runs in his previous outing. Facing the defending American League champion Rays, Cahill was pounded for seven runs on eight hits and two walks over 2 2/3 innings in his shortest outing of the year. Both of the walks he issued came around to score, one of them on Carlos Pena's monster home run during Tampa Bay's five-run third inning. Cahill, who threw 76 pitches, also gave up a home run to Gabe Gross and surrendered four doubles.

home_pitcher_note: Jakubauskas showed the composure the organization was looking for, bouncing back from a rough second career big league start to throw a complete game in his third. Where the 29-year-old rookie got ahead of himself against Tampa Bay, he was able to focus on strike one in Chicago. Jakubauskas retired the first 10 batters in a row on Tuesday as well as the final 13 batters he faced. The White Sox managed two hits that led to two runs, but Jakubauskas was otherwise flawless in a 2-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Outman, who won the fifth spot in Oakland's starting rotation with a strong final appearance at Spring Training in Arizona, posted a 6.48 ERA in his first two assignments and was temporarily moved into the bullpen as the A's went with a four-man rotation in the wake of two off-days and a rainout in the span of a week. While working out of the bullpen, Outman retired six of the seven batters he faced. He'll be starting for the first time since April 17, and it'll be his second start of the year against the Mariners. The first time came April 11, when he gave up three runs on six hits over 4 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez maintained his perfect record and extended his scoreless-inning streak to 19 on Tuesday night against the White Sox. The right-hander allowed four hits over eight innings while striking out nine. This scoreless streak from Hernandez is the longest by a Mariner since J.J. Putz, who went 22 innings in 2007.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood beat the Athletics, 5-4, on Tuesday while going eight innings. He allowed ten hits and two walks but the Athletics were 1-for-11 with runners in scoring position against him. When it was over, Millwood was leading the American League in innings pitched and was fifth in the league in ERA. Millwood was 0-3 with a 7.71 ERA against the Mariners last year and is 7-9 with a 4.72 ERA in 18 career outings against them. He is 2-6 with a 5.05 ERA at Safeco Field, his second most losses in any opposing AL city.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander has struck out 32 and walked only six in 31 innings over his first five starts of the season.  But he threw 92 pitches in five innings in his last start, settling for a no-decision in an eventual Mariners loss to the White Sox. Ideally, he would pitch deeper into the game, although the organization might still be hesitant to get him to the 100-pitch level because of offseason surgery on his left shoulder.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla lost to the Athletics, 4-2, on Thursday and is now 0-2 with an 8.14 ERA in his last four starts. He allowed three runs in six-plus innings against the A's for his first official quality start. Opponents are hitting .330 off him, including .361 by left-handed hitters. Padilla was 2-0 with a 2.05 ERA in five starts against the Mariners last year and is 4-5 with a 4.48 ERA in his career. He is 3-3 with a 4.21 ERA in nine career starts at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Sidney Ponson was battered for the second time in three starts, allowing seven earned runs on nine hits and one walk in 4 1/3 innings against the Twins on Friday at the Metrodome. Ponson gave up five extra-base hits, including two homers, in Kansas City's 7-5 loss. Kansas City wants Ponson to munch innings, but it's tough to go deep in games when batters are as keyed in as Minnesota's were on Friday, a day during which Ponson fell to 0-4. Next up is Seattle. Ponson is 4-4 with a 4.53 ERA in 14 career appearances against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: It was one step forward and two steps back for the frustrated right-hander, who tasted the fruits of victory against the Angels, but then the agony of another defeat against the Athletics in a brief and ineffective outing on Friday night at Safeco Field. Silva went from having a runner on second base with two outs to six runs being scored in the third inning against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Brian Bannister was not as sharp Saturday against the Twins as he was in his first two starts since his return from Triple-A Omaha. Bannister allowed six runs -- three earned -- on eight hits and two walks in 5 1/3 innings. Bannister did not factor into the decision. Bannister kept his ERA under two, although he will have to cut down on the baserunners he has surrendered for that success to continue. Bannister has an opportunity to get in the win column against the Mariners his next time out. He is 0-3 in three career starts against Seattle with a 4.79 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander was able to put his only rocky start of the season behind him and have another quality outing against the Athletics last Saturday night. But he had to settle for another no-decision despite a job well done. After striking out none in his game against the Angels in Anaheim, Washburn fanned six over seven innings vs. Oakland and surrendered just one run. The veteran changed speeds and worked ahead in the count most of the night against Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: Baker carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning of his last start against the Royals but things quickly went downhill for the starter. He gave up five straight hits to start the seventh, including a three-run homer to Jose Guillen that cut the Twins lead to one. Baker was eventually charged with five runs over his six-plus innings and suffered his fourth loss in four starts so far this season. While it was another loss, the Twins took a positive in that Baker was throwing the ball down for those first six innings and was mixing in his pitches better than his previous outings. Next up for Baker will be a start at home against the Mariners -- the team he was supposed to face on Opening Day before a DL stint sidelined those plans. Baker is 0-3 with a 5.50 ERA in six career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: One rough inning seems to be all the rookie right-hander needs to ruin an otherwise solid outing. The three runs he surrendered in the first inning against the Athletics last Sunday did most of the damage, and an opposite-field home run produced two of those runs. Jakubauskas made the mistake of leaving a fastball out over the plate to Athletics slugger Jack Cust, who became the first opposing hitter to go deep against the Mariners pitcher. He had tossed 21 1/3 innings without allowing a home run.

home_pitcher_note: After beginning the season 0-4 over his first five starts, Liriano finally got his first win on Monday against the Tigers. He pitched 7 1/3 innings, allowing just two runs on four hits. He struck out a season-high nine batters in the contest as he held Detroit scoreless over the first five innings of the contest. With a fastball averaging around 91-92 mph and better command of his slider and changeup, Liriano was able to keep the Tigers hitters off-balance for most of the outing. The left-hander said after the start that he hopes he can keep pitching like he did on Monday night -- with better command of all of his pitches. Next he'll face the Mariners, against whom he opened the season. In that start he gave up four runs on four hits over seven innings to take the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez looks to bounce back from his roughest outing of the season, a six-inning stint against the Rangers in Seattle. The right-hander didn't walk a batter while recording nine strikeouts, but he also surrendered 10 hits and six earned runs, only three fewer than he had allowed all season. He had a 22-inning scoreless streak end in the fourth innings. After surrendering one home run in his first 37 innings this season, he was touched for two dingers against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: The sinkerball pitcher couldn't find control of his fastball in his last start, causing problems early in his outing against the Tigers. Blackburn gave up a career-high nine runs (six earned) in just 3 1/3 innings vs. Detroit. It was his shortest start since Sept. 19, 2008, when he went just 1 1/3 innings. Blackburn wasn't helped by a handful of defensive miscues early in his outing, but manager Ron Gardenhire said that Blackburn needs to learn how to take a step back and make pitches when it counts. Five of his runs came in the second inning after Blackburn had retired the first two batters he faced. Blackburn will next face Seattle for the second time this season. He's 1-0 with a 5.73 ERA in two career starts vs. the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander continued his early-season success, holding the Rangers to one run -- a solo home run -- over seven innings. But that long ball erased a one-run lead and Bedard ended up with his third no-decision of the season. He struck out seven and walked none and now has 39 whiffs and six free passes in 38 innings over his first six starts of the season. He has surrendered three home runs this season.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman is 2-0 with a 3.24 ERA in three starts and opponents are hitting .186 off him as a starter. They hit .355 off him as a reliever. He beat the Athletics, 4-2, on Wednesday night by holding them to two runs in six innings. He is now 8-8 with a 4.98 ERA in 28 career starts, going back to last season. Of those, 14 have been "official" quality starts and he is 6-2 with a 2.82 ERA in those games. He has a career 2.57 ERA against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: A start that originally was supposed to go to right-hander Carlos Silva goes instead to Vargas, who makes his first Major League start since 2007 when he was with the Mets. Silva is on the 15-day disabled list with inflammation in his right shoulder. Vargas has worked 3 2/3 scoreless innings of relief since being promoted from Triple-A Tacoma on May 2. He brought with him from Tacoma an 11 2/3-inning scoreless streak.

home_pitcher_note: McCarthy had his shortest outing of the season on Thursday against the Athletics. He lasted just four innings and allowed seven runs in a 9-4 loss. McCarthy is 1-1 with a 7.71 ERA in his past three starts with opponents hitting .339 off him. McCarthy has made 19 starts in his career at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington and is 6-5 with a 4.30 ERA. He is 1-2 with a 7.02 ERA in his career against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn has been solid all season long, and he put up another great outing against the Royals in his last start. Unfortunately for Washburn, he took the loss despite allowing just one earned run in seven innings with five strikeouts. Washburn said his sinker was the key to his seven-inning performance against Kansas City. He threw it to lefties and righties and it kept hitters off balance all night. The 34-year-old left-hander has really surged this season, and he's one of the big reasons the Mariners are floating around the .500 mark.

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old lefty is learning to trust his stuff. Harrison has won three starts in a row and is working on a 19-inning scoreless streak. On Friday night, Harrison submitted a complete-game shutout against the White Sox, retiring 11 batters in a row at one point. He has chipped away at an ERA that rose to 9.20 after a no-decision at Toronto on April 22.
away_pitcher_note: As good as April was for the ace right-hander, May has been just the opposite. For the second time in two May starts, Hernandez had long-ball issues, surrendering two home runs during a four-inning outing against the Twins. After allowing just one home run in his first five starts and 37 innings, he has now given up four dingers in his last 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: It's back the drawing board for the rookie right-hander, who staggered through his roughest outing on the road in his start against the Twins. He might have felt additional pressure with the team on a season-high four-game losing streak, but for whatever reason, the Twins worked him over and saddled him with his fourth straight loss. After surrendering just one home run in his first six outings this season, Joe Mauer and Justin Morneau went back-to-back against him in the fifth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Lester followed up one of his best outings of the young season, a 10-strikeout performance at Yankee Stadium, with arguably his worst last Saturday at Fenway Park. The Rays blasted the Boston left-hander to the tune of eight runs on 10 hits in just 4 1/3 innings, marking the second time in as many starts that Lester has been roughed up by the defending American League champions. A native of Tacoma, Wash., Lester is 1-0 with a 4.67 ERA in three career appearances against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note:
Olson will get this emergency start because a sore hamstring issue has scratched Erik  Bedard. "It feels better. It's just a little sore but he gives us every indication that he'll make his next start against Anaheim," manager Don Wakamatsu said of Bedard. "It's the right decision rather than push it tomorrow." Olson, called up from Triple-A Tacoma on May 6, has had three relief appearances, carrying a 2.57 ERA. He was
2-2 with a 3.08 ERA in five starts with Tacoma.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett appears to be rounding into form after enduring a pair of woeful starts in late April that were reminiscent of the dreadful outings that defined his 2006 season. The fireballing righty is coming off back-to-back quality starts against the Yankees and Rays, a stretch in which he struck out 10 and walked four over 12 innings. Boston's ace is 3-1 with a 3.29 ERA in four career starts against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas made a good impression in his first start for the Mariners, and his first in the Major Leagues since July 3, 2007. He held the Rangers to one run over five innings, a solo home run to Chris Davis in the fifth, and that was enough to cost him any chance of winning his debut start. Vargas, who was working on a pitch-count limit of 75 to 80, was lifted after 73 pitches, 43 of them for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: The lanky sinkerballer struggled with his command in his last start but made it work anyway, allowing just two runs over six innings. Masterson walked four and struck out three, throwing 105 pitches in a no-decision against the Angels. This will likely be his final start in the rotation before Daisuke Matsuzaka returns from the disabled list. In five starts, Masterson is 2-2 with a 4.97 ERA. Masterson has pitched twice against the Mariners in his career, going 1-0 with a 1.04 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Run support wasn't a problem for a change in Washburn's last start. He had a three-run lead in the fourth inning but surrendered four runs in a three-inning stretch and had to settle for his second no-decision of the season. He threw a season-high 110 pitches, one of which was hit for a two-run homer that tied the game. Washburn walked a season-high four batters and surrendered more than two runs for only the second time in seven starts. He is 1-1 against the Angels this season, beating his former team on April 15 at Safeco Field and losing the rematch on April 26 in Anaheim.
away_pitcher_note: Even though he'll be pitching on just one day's rest, Lackey certainly will be well rested for his second turn through the rotation. In the briefest, and perhaps strangest, start of his career, the big Texan lasted two pitches against the Rangers on Saturday. He was ejected after throwing one pitch behind Ian Kinsler and the second into the leadoff man's left side. Lackey had spent six weeks recovering from a strained right forearm. He is 10-8 in his career against the Mariners with a 3.90 ERA in 22 starts. He's 7-5 at Safeco field with a 2.79 ERA in 13 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez turned back the clock to April in his last start, holding the Rangers to four hits and no runs in a stellar performance in Arlington. The staff ace had struggled in his first two May starts, surrendering 16 hits and 12 earned runs in 10 innings, after ending April with a 4-0 record. He had a dazzling two-seamer and location in his start against the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Palmer, the 30-year-old journeyman, continues to flourish with his poise and command, showing both traits in a remarkable effort against the Red Sox on Wednesday night in Anaheim. Down 4-0 after two innings, Palmer went on a run of 20 consecutive outs, finishing with eight strikeouts against two walks, both costing him runs. After going 0-2 in three starts for the Giants last year, the first Major League opportunities of his career, Palmer made an adjustment in his delivery at Triple-A Salt Lake in early April, more leg drive combined with a direct path to the plate, and it has paid dividends in his new home.

home_pitcher_note: Jakubauskas was knocked back on his heels in the first inning against the Red Sox Friday and had to scramble to recover. He allowed a run in both the first and second then two in the third before finally settling down. He allowed just one hit over his last four innings of work. He went six innings, allowing four runs on seven hits while walking two and striking out four. Jakubauskas threw 104 pitches, staying in long enough to leave with the lead. He faced the Angels April 16 at Safeco, a 5-1 loss. He went 5 1/3 innings, allowing five hits and two runs. He struck out three and walked no one.
away_pitcher_note: Santana was solid in his season debut against the Red Sox, showing no ill effects from his sprained right elbow in going five innings and reaching 92 pitches while yielding three earned runs on seven hits. The return of the 2008 American League All-Star is a big boost to the staff. His fastball was in the 91-93 mph range and his slider and changeup complemented it well, accounting for five strikeouts against three walks. He's 6-2 with a 3.98 ERA in his career against the Mariners, and he's 3-1 with a 5.52 ERA at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander missed his last scheduled start because of soreness in his right hamstring. In his previous outing,  he threw a season-high number of pitches over the shortest distance, a combination that would not have qualified him for his third win of the season. Bedard threw 110 pitches in a 4 2/3 inning outing against the Twins in the Mariners' final game at the Metrodome. Five walks and four strikeouts had a major impact in the high pitch count, but Bedard still allowed just two runs despite running into jams virtually every inning. He needs to be more efficient with his pitches or could have a tough time getting his games to the sixth or seventh inning.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was in trouble from start to finish against the Rangers in Texas on Friday night. He yielded three homers in a game for the fourth time in his career, two to Ian Kinsler, surrendering seven earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. His ERA elevated by almost a full run, from 2.66 to 3.59, as he gave up eight hits and two walks while striking out four. Saunders has had his way with the Mariners. He's 5-1 in eight career starts with a 4.13 ERA and is 3-0 in four outings at Safeco Field with a 4.22 ERA, including a win in April when he held the Mariners to one earned run on three hits in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas maintained his spot in the rotation with a solid outing Sunday against a high-powered Boston Red Sox lineup. He went 5 1/3 innings, allowing two runs -- one earned -- and seven hits. He struck out just one and walked three. The 26-year-old is trying to at least make an impression on a team that needs starters, with Ryan Rowland-Smith and Carlos Silva on the DL. It was his second straight start in which he lasted at least five innings but he'll need to work deeper into the game -- he threw 98 pitches. He is penciled in against San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: The Big Unit will return to the city where he became truly big, as an All-Star and Cy Young Award winner between 1989-98. But the 45-year-old has struggled recently, recording an 11.05 ERA in his last three starts. That's based on 18 earned runs allowed in 14 2/3 innings, to go with three walks and 12 strikeouts. Johnson has pitched progressively fewer innings in that span, lasting 5 2/3 May 6 at Colorado, five on May 11 against Washington and four-plus last Saturday against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: For the second time this season, Olson has been tabbed as an emergency starter, getting Saturday night's assignment in place of lefty Jarrod Washburn. Soreness behind his left knee has been bothering Washburn for his last two outings, and though the injury isn't considered serious, Seattle decided to push him back several days. Olson, acquired from the Cubs in late January, went five innings against the Red Sox on May 16 and surrendered five runs in taking the loss. This will be Olson's 35th career start, but he has never faced the Giants. Olson is not overpowering and needs good location to be effective. Three of the five hits he gave up to the Red Sox were home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Despite walking five batters, Cain tossed six scoreless innings in his last start, Sunday against the Mets. He accomplished that by limiting 3-4-5 hitters Carlos Beltran, Gary Sheffield and David Wright to one hit in their first three plate appearances. By contrast, in the series' first three games, the trio combined for 16 hits in their first three plate appearances. Cain has pitched six or more innings in each of his eight starts this season. He has never faced the Mariners, and is 3-7 with a 3.86 ERA in Interleague Play for his career.

home_pitcher_note: The best start of Hernandez's career has been knocked back a few notches during a winless month of May. King Felix's ERA, which had been among the league's best throughout April, climbed over the 4.00 mark for the first time this season when the Angels tagged him for 11 hits and six earned runs in his last outing. It was a total reversal from his previous start, when he held the Rangers scoreless over seven innings. Hernandez has faced the Giants once in his MLB career and notched one of his four Interleague wins.
away_pitcher_note: Zito has reclaimed his 2002 American League Cy Young form. He also has stolen Matt Cain's dubious distinction as the Giants' hard-luck pitcher, having received 1.81 runs per game -- the worst support among NL pitchers. Zito has surged in his last six starts, posting a 2.21 ERA in that span. He has allowed only four home runs this season, though two came in his last outing at San Diego -- a complete-game effort in a 2-1 loss.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson, who has been dealing with a blister on his left index finger for the past three weeks, finally got to do all of his regular between-starts work prior to his most recent outing, and it showed. Five days after giving up nine runs -- three earned -- on six hits and two walks over 3 1/3 innings against the Tigers in Detroit, Anderson, on Wednesday, didn't allow a hit at Tampa Bay until Carlos Pena's two-run homer with two out in the fourth inning. He finished with a line of four runs -- two earned -- on four hits without a walk and five strikeouts while throwing 80 pitches over six innings. A 21-year-old rookie, Anderson made his first big league start against the Mariners on April 10 and gave up five earned runs on seven hits and two walks over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The late-blooming right-hander pitched one of his best games of the season in his last start, holding the Angels to two hits and no runs over six stellar innings. Though he walked two and struck out one, he consistently got ahead of hitters and changed speeds to keep the Angels off-balance. The strikeout and walks came in the same inning, the fifth, when he escaped a bases-loaded jam. The second inning was the only other time Jakubauskas pitched from the stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Braden held the host Rays to three runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four over seven innings his last time out, posting his third quality start in four May assignments, but he remained winless for the month in part because he's not given much room for error. He entered the game with the second-lowest run support in the American League, at 2.42 runs per nine innings, and he was trailing 3-2 when he left the game. Braden has not faced the Mariners this season; last year he made one relief appearance against them, allowing two runs in two innings.
away_pitcher_note: After tossing four solid innings against his former team in his last start, the veteran left-hander surrendered five runs in the fifth inning, and that was the final inning he worked. It was the first time in eight starts this season that he did not get into at least the sixth inning. The six earned runs matched his season high, which previously occurred on April 26 -- against the Angels in Anaheim. This will be Washburn's second start of the season against the Athletics. He held Oakland to five hits and one run over seven innings on May 2 but settled for a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Cahill pitched one of the best games of his young career in his last outing and still didn't win. He allowed two runs on six hits and one walk, recording a career-best five strikeouts in a season-high 7 1/3 innings against the Arizona D-backs on Friday night. Cahill did show that he could put subpar outings behind him, as he lasted just 2 1/3 innings, giving up seven runs, in his previous start. He's making his third start of the season against the Mariners, having given up two runs on nine hits over 13 innings against Seattle thus far. He lost, 1-0, on April 12 and took a no-decision in a 3-2 A's win on May 2.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't the number of hits Bedard surrendered in his last outing but how far those hits went. Juan Rivera hit a solo home run in the first inning and Gary Matthews Jr. hit a solo shot two innings later for the only hits off Bedard during a five-inning start. The veteran missed one start because of a sore right hamstring, but the layoff didn't seem to adversely affect his control, as he walked just two batters.

home_pitcher_note: In his third outing of the season -- against the Dodgers on Saturday night -- Lackey stretched his arm out to seven innings and 101 pitches, leaving with a lead the bullpen didn't hold. He yielded three earned runs on seven hits and one intentional walk while striking out five. Lackey's curveball and fastball got away from him on occasion, accounting for three hit batsmen, but only one cost him a run. He's 11-8 in 23 career starts against the Mariners and is coming off a win against them in Seattle on May 18, when he yielded five runs (four earned) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander looks more and more like a keeper in the Mariners' starting rotation. He was locked in a dandy pitchers' duel with future Hall of Famer Randy Johnson in his last outing, holding the Giants to a first-inning solo home run and a single over seven superb innings. Thought not particularly overpowering, Vargas struck out seven batters and rarely fell behind hitters.

home_pitcher_note: One bad inning -- a four-run second featuring Jamie Hoffmann's three-run homer -- was Palmer's undoing against the Dodgers in a no-decision that ended his streak of five consecutive starts with wins. Palmer settled down after the early assault and lasted 4 2/3 innings, yielding four runs on five hits and two walks, striking out three. In his previous start, he'd picked up a win in Seattle despite giving up five earned runs across five innings. Fastball command backed by a quality breaking ball is Palmer's formula.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez threw 112 pitches against the Giants on Sunday, 83 for strikes, in his eight innings. He got ahead of the hitters, used all his pitches and worked both sides of the plate. He was victimized by an error that opened the door for three runs, all unearned. Now he faces a team that's a personal challenge. The last time he faced the Angels, May 19, they stole five bases. Manager Don Wakamatsu said afterward that he did not step up. But Sunday's effort should increase his confidence.

home_pitcher_note: Santana took a beating -- and so did his ERA -- when he surrendered seven earned runs while getting just three outs against the White Sox at home on Monday night in his third start of the season. He threw only 41 pitches in his brief outing, yielding a three-run homer to Jermaine Dye among the nine hits. Santana had a hard-luck loss to the Mariners in Seattle, yielding only one earned run in 6 2/3 innings, on May 20. He's 6-3 with a 3.76 ERA in 13 career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Seattle manager Don Wakamatsu decided on Friday that Olson will start on Sunday against the Angels instead of right-hander Chris Jakubauskas, who was relegated to the bullpen after lasting just 3 1/3 innings in his last start. Olson pitched well against the Giants on Saturday when he threw six shutout innings, but he didn't figure in the decision. Olson is 1-1 with a 8.68 ERA in three career outings against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: It was like April for the veteran left-hander in his last start as he held the Athletics scoreless for six innings, encountering just one jam during the impressive outing. He escaped a bases-loaded predicament in the first inning and never allowed another runner to reach second base. Even so, that wasn't enough to get his fourth win as the Mariners bullpen took over and quickly surrendered four runs. Washburn won his first three starts this season, but is winless since. He is 6-5 with a 4.84 ERA in his career against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Hill had a tough time in his third start, allowing six earned runs and getting knocked out in the fourth inning. Baltimore's bats snapped back, though, and bailed him out of a loss. The southpaw had pitched well in each of his first two outings before coming back to earth against Toronto. Hill's next outing will come against Seattle, a team that has gone 10-6 against lefty starters this season.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander continued to be the Mariners most reliable starter, holding the Athletics to one run -- a solo home run -- over 6 2/3 innings in his last start. Bedard was so locked into the strike zone that 77 of his 108 pitches were strikes. In two starts this season against the Athletics, Bedard has gotten straight "A's", allowing just two runs in 15 innings with 12 strikeouts and two walks. His next start will be against his former team, the Orioles, the first time he has faced the Birds in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez pitched well in his Major League debut, working into the sixth inning and holding the Tigers to just one run. The right-handed rookie escaped a bases-loaded jam in the first inning of his debut. Hernandez was second in the Triple-A International League in strikeouts at the time of his promotion, and he led the Double-A Eastern League in punchouts last season.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas was effective for the fourth straight time as he shut down the Angels to the tune of just two runs on four hits over 6 2/3 innings on Friday. The win marked his first as a starter since April 13, 2006. He's allowed just five runs in his four starts with four of those runs coming on solo home runs. Vargas has never faced the Orioles in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen went eight innings in his last start, the longest outing of his brief big league career. The right-hander has been knocked out before completing five innings just one time in eight starts, but he has allowed at least four earned runs in half of his outings. Bergesen, who was named the team's Minor League Pitcher of the Year last season, is 0-1 with a 5.50 ERA in three road starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez was superb against the Angels, as the right-hander didn't allow an earned run over 6 1/3 innings on Saturday, but earned the no-decision. Hernandez, though, put together his second successive solid start, striking out six batters and walking just one. Hernandez is 3-3 with a 2.98 ERA in eight career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano's woes continued in his last start against the Rays. The left-hander lasted only four innings for the third straight start, giving up four runs on seven hits. Liriano's 6.60 ERA has him tied with the Indians' Fausto Carmona for the worst in the A.L., and his seven losses are the most in the A.L. as well. Much of Liriano's damage has come in big innings, and the pitcher seemed frustrated after this last loss by his inability to correct the problem.  Despite posting a 12.00 ERA over his last three starts, he'll remain in the rotation for at least the time being. Liriano faces the Mariners, against whom he's 3-2 with a 3.25 in six career starts.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander held the Orioles to one run over seven innings in his last start, the seventh time in 10 starts this season surrendered two or fewer runs. But for the third time in those outings, he did not win as the Mariners scored no runs. He is holding left-handed batters to a .157 average this season, nearly 90 points below his career average against them.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn has become one of the Twins' more reliable starters. He delivered his third straight quality start, and his fourth in the last five outings, against the Rays last Sunday. Blackburn held the Rays to just two runs on seven hits over six innings, both runs coming on solo homers. The right-hander has been using his sinker effectively and working the corners with his four-seam fastball. He'll try to continue that trend when he faces the Mariners. Blackburn is 1-0 with a 3.50 ERA in three career starts vs. Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander continues to be the Mariners' most reliable starter, holding the Orioles to one run over 6 2/3 innings with seven strikeouts in his last start. He has been so locked into the strike zone that 148 of his last 220 pitches have been strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Slowey moved into second place in wins among American League pitchers when he captured No. 8 of the season in his last start against the Indians. The right-hander held Cleveland to just two runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings. It marked Slowey's fifth straight quality start and his seventh of the season. For only the fourth time this season, Slowey did not give up a long ball to Cleveland -- allowing both of his runs on a Kelly Shoppach two-run double in the seventh inning. Slowey will next face the Mariners. He is 1-0 with a 7.50 ERA in one career start vs. Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: With Koji Uehara's likely return to the starting rotation during the upcoming homestand, Orioles manager Dave Trembley said he wanted to keep Bergesen and Jeremy Guthrie as closely aligned to their normal routine as possible. Bergesen will be pitching on five days' rest, and just threw a five-hitter over seven innings in Seattle last Wednesday, though he received a no-decision. Bergesen has put together back-to-back quality starts, allowing four runs on 12 hits over 15 innings for a 2.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas has yet to allow more than two earned runs in a game since joining the Mariners in May, surrendering just seven earned runs in 32 2/3 innings. Acquired in the three-team, 12-player trade with the Mets and Indians last December, Vargas has been arguably the biggest surprise of the season for the Mariners. He won't hit 90 on the radar gun but relies on pinpoint location, which has worked superbly so far. He held the Orioles to two runs over 5 1/3 innings in his last start, six days earlier in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie gave up six hits to the first seven hitters he faced and was hit by a line drive last Friday night in Oakland. He lasted two-thirds of an inning in what was easily his worst start of the year. In his previous two starts, he allowed a combined four runs in 13 innings. He was 1-1 with a 2.28 ERA in three games against the Mariners last year.
away_pitcher_note: The right-handed ace had another quality performance in his last outing, holding the Twins to one run over seven innings, but had to settle for a no-decision. He turned in his team-leading eighth quality start (six or more innings, three or fewer earned runs) and has now struck out at least five batters in 10 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Uehara will be coming off the disabled list (strained left hamstring) to make this start. The Orioles are reluctant to make it official until they need to make a corresponding move. Uehara hasn't pitched since May 23, when he left the game against the Washington Nationals after three scoreless innings. He's 0-3 over his past seven starts, last winning on April 13. He's pitched better than his record. Throw out the seven runs he allowed in a win over the Texas Rangers, and his ERA is 3.15. He's allowed three earned runs or fewer in seven of his nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: The original plan was for left-hander Ryan Rowland-Smith to return to the starting rotation in the series finale against the Orioles, but he had such a rocky rehab outing at Triple-A Tacoma that he remained in the Minors for at least one more start. It is now expected that Olson will face the Orioles after spending time in the bullpen, where he performed swell. He has made three starts this season with so-so results. He's not overpowering, so he needs to keep the ball down and move it around the strike zone to be effective.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez struck out a season-high nine in his last start, but not with the use of his blazing 98 mph fastball. Instead, he fooled Cardinals hitters with offspeed stuff early in counts in eight innings and allowed two runs on four hits for the win. Since May 1, Jimenez is 3-3 with a 2.63 ERA in eight starts. Jimenez will be looking for his first win in Interleague Play, where he's a career 0-3 with a 5.00 ERA, against the Mariners in his next start.
away_pitcher_note: It's difficult to tell by his record, but Washburn is having his best season since 2002, when he won 18 games for the Angels. Washburn is coming off another solid start, when he held the Twins to one run over six innings, striking out six and walking one. It was the eighth time in 11 starts the lefty has allowed two or fewer runs this season, but he has not won a game since April 21. Washburn is 1-0 with a 2.70 ERA in two career starts against the Rockies at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis held the Cardinals to two runs in 6 2/3 innings of efficient pitching while winning Monday at Busch Stadium as the Rockies completed a four-game sweep. Marquis has curried the favor of his fielders because of his penchant for aggressively attacking the bottom of the strike zone with his sinker and his slider. However, Marquis is more effective on the road than at Coors Field (3-2, 5.34 ERA), which is where he'll face the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The hard-throwing right-hander unexpectedly makes his first start of the season, filling in for left-hander Erik Bedard, who was scratched because of slight inflammation in his left shoulder. Morrow, who started five games late last season, began this season as the closer, but lost the job in mid-May and had recently asked the team to re-convert him back to a starter. That was expected to occur at Triple-A Tacoma, not with the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel's excellence on the road continued on Tuesday. After allowing runs in each of the first two innings, the righty stuck around long enough to get a win by lasting six innings in Milwaukee, with nothing more allowed in a tight victory. He has walked just eight batters -- one intentionally as his lone free pass issued Tuesday -- in his last seven starts. He has fallen short of five complete innings in three of his four outings at Coors Field, however.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners know what they'll get from Vargas on most occasions -- a decent enough effort, though unspectacular, that will keep them close. The right-hander needs to throw more first-pitch strikes and command his fastball inside with more efficiency, but he's been a nice find that's bolstered what's become a dependable rotation. The Mariners will closely watch how Vargas reacts to his first loss, a 3-1 setback in Baltimore on Tuesday. He didn't pitch that poorly, giving up three runs on seven hits over 5 2/3 innings. And Vargas was honest when he told reporters that he wasn't happy with his performance, demonstrating that he understands where he needs to improve.

home_pitcher_note: Correia silenced any doubts he couldn't pitch on just three days' rest, allowing just one run on three hits over six innings against the Dodgers on Tuesday. He retired the last 15 batters he faced and walked none on the night, needing just 81 pitches to get through six innings. A lifetime National Leaguer, Correia has pitched against the Mariners just once in his career and allowed two runs in 2/3 innings of relief in 2006.
away_pitcher_note: If nothing else, Hernandez has been consistent, turning in nine quality starts in 13 outings this season. Where he once relied on the fastball to dominate hitters, Hernandez is becoming more adept at using his complimentary pitches, moving a tantalizing slider off the plate and frustrating hitters with a plus-changeup. He's coming off a strong outing on a humid Baltimore night when he scattered seven hits and allowed one run in seven innings. The key to that win: Hernandez escaped a first-inning jam and never let the Orioles seriously threaten again. He was 4-0 in April, won once in six May starts and is unbeaten in two June outings.

home_pitcher_note: Gaudin was roughed up in his last start on June 12 when he allowed eight runs, all earned, on 10 hits in a loss to the Angels. Granted, he was facing a talented lineup and many of the hits he allowed were of the blooper variety, but the fact was Gaudin hasn't executed his pitches very well in recent weeks. He's now allowed 13 earned runs in his last two starts, spanning eight innings. Granted, Gaudin has been able to mostly avoid walks recently, which was a stumbling block early in the season. But he's still been very hittable.
away_pitcher_note: A gutsy effort against his former Orioles teammates on Thursday might have earned the left-hander another opportunity to start. Olson's first victory as a Mariner wasn't a thing of beauty -- he allowed two runs on five hits, walked three and struck out one in five innings -- but he rebounded nicely after a rain delay to save the Seattle bullpen. Olson's at his best when he attacks hitters and lets his fielders do some work behind him. When he starts to nibble tentatively at the plate is when he gets in trouble.

home_pitcher_note: Geer allowed a career-high four home runs in his last start Saturday against the Angels, when he was pressed into duty for Jake Peavy, who went on the disabled list with tendon damage in his right ankle. Home runs have been a big problem for Geer, who has allowed 14 in 58 2/3 innings this season. "I hung a couple of pitches here and there. I worked on staying tall, staying on top of it ... it's one hanger here and there that led to runs," Geer said. "If you are not sharp and leave a pitch up at this level, they can hit them out." This is a lesson Geer is learning, though he did make five starts last September. Geer has always been a guy who pitches to contact and will give up more hits than innings and, by in large, will give up his fair share of home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Morrow makes his second start since being moved back into the rotation. He threw 64 pitches over three innings against the Rockies, which was more than he wanted to throw in such a short amount of time, but surrendered just one run. He still lacks command of his fastball, but is developing a nice slider. His pitch count will be increased to 75 or 80 against the Pads. Morrow has faced the Padres six times in his career and has yet to allow a run.

home_pitcher_note: A streak of three quality starts ended for Washburn at Coors Field, where his own wildness and some bad luck parlayed into an Interleague Play loss. Three of the batters Washburn walked and one that he hit scored runs in the setback. An errant throw to first base that would have ended an inning produced one of the five runs he surrendered in a six-inning stint.
away_pitcher_note: Garland was charged with three runs on six hits in seven innings in the D-backs' 6-4 loss to the Astros on Saturday. The right-hander threw 98 pitches and gave up a two-run home run to Lance Berkman on the way to his fifth consecutive defeat. He remains resilient. Garland's attitude combined with improved effectiveness on the mound could bode well for the D-backs the remainder of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander was going to get two extra days between starts, but a shoulder ailment to Erik Bedard scrapped those plans and Vargas will make his eighth start of the season. He has struggled a bit in his last two outings, which prompted the idea of giving him some extra rest. Vargas has a terrific changeup, but didn't use the pitch often enough in his start against the Rockies and was rocked during a five-run fifth inning. It didn't help that he was working with a rookie catcher.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner is looking for his second victory of the month and hoping to rebound from two consecutive subpar starts. In his last start, Astros shortstop Miguel Tejada hit an RBI double off Buckner for the visitors' first run of the game in the first inning, and Lance Berkman followed with a two-run home run to extend the Astros' lead to 3-0. Buckner was eventually charged with six runs on five hits in five innings for the loss. In his previous start against the Giants, he was charged with eight runs and 13 hits in 5 2/3 innings for the loss. He has been plagued with poor execution of his pitches but is confident he can bounce back in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander continues to perform like a potential All-Star selection, tossing a two-hit shutout over the Padres in his last outing. He has now surrendered three earned runs in his past 37 2/3 innings, a 0.72 ERA. When he has all four of his pitches -- two-seam and four-seam fastball, slider and curve -- working the way they have in his last five starts, he's a tough pitcher to face.
away_pitcher_note: Davis has one win in his past nine starts, but has pitched better than his record would indicate. Last time out, against the Royals, he allowed four runs (three earned) over 5 2/3 innings in what would turn out to be a 5-0 loss. His last win was on June 5 in San Diego, where he worked six shutout innings. The time before that he allowed just two runs in seven innings but came away with no decision. Davis can be frustrating to watch at times. He is a slow worker who puts plenty of baserunners on, but also seems to be able to work his way out of jams. Davis could be trade bait in July as he is in the final year of a three-year, $22 million extension.

home_pitcher_note: Remove two two-strike pitches from Olson's last start and he would get high marks all the way across. The lefty surrendered just two hits over six innings against the Padres, but both hits were home runs on 0-and-2 pitches. The second one came with a runner on base via the only walk Olson issued. Olson threw 94 pitches, 62 of them for strikes. He was able to get ahead of hitters regularly and it worked in his favor most of the time.
away_pitcher_note: Gaudin won't have to scour videotape to find footage of the Mariners, as he faced them five days previous in San Diego. Gaudin allowed three earned runs over six innings with two walks and eight strikeouts in a loss. A two-run home run in the fourth inning by Jose Lopez proved to be the difference, as that was about the only pitch Gaudin would have taken back. After struggling in recent starts, Gaudin got back to being aggressive in the strike zone and keeping the ball down, getting seven ground-ball outs (compared to three fly balls). Gaudin has a history of walks but managed to keep the ball in play the last time out.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander's conversion from reliever to starter took a step in the right direction against the Padres. After surrendering two runs in the first inning, Morrow tossed three scoreless innings, retiring six of the final seven batters he faced. His only walk was issued to the opposing pitcher and marked the second consecutive outing that Morrow walked the pitcher. He will get a rematch against the Padres in his next start.
away_pitcher_note: Right-handed pitcher Geer tossed six innings, allowing three runs (two homers) on six hits, in his last start June 18 for an Interleague win against the Mariners. He struck out six and walked none to earn the fourth quality start his career.  "He's still growing as a pitcher," said Padres manager Bud Black. "He has less than 100 innings in the Major Leagues. He's learning each and every time out what he has to do."

home_pitcher_note: Washburn's winless streak reached 12 starts in his last outing, another quality start that wasn't quite good enough to get him a win. The lefty has the lowest run support average in the American League since 2005 and there appears to be no end in sight. He held the Diamondbacks to three hits in his previous start, but the Mariners did not score while he was in the game.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc didn't last long in his first start of the season for the Padres. A late fill-in for an injured Chris Young, LeBlanc was handed a 2-0 lead on Friday against the A's but allowed the first four batters in his fourth inning of work that day to reach base, two on walks, and he was gone before recording an out. LeBlanc got some good swing-and-misses on his best pitch, the changeup, early but the A's were patient with him. All told, LeBlanc allowed three runs on three hits with two walks and one strikeout.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw seems to have found a rhythm in his last two starts, in which he has thrown 12 2/3 consecutive scoreless innings, including seven shutout innings against the Angels Sunday. He had to overcome a bases-loaded, no-out jam and four walks, but he's also showing the potential dominance that very few 21-year-olds possess. Angels center fielder Torii Hunter called Kershaw "effectively wild."
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander ended a two-game losing streak with a bang, retiring 20 of the final 21 batters he faced against the D-backs. He was supposed to get an extra day between starts, but when a shoulder ailment sidelined fellow lefty Erik Bedard, Vargas pitched on his regular fifth day and was superb against Arizona. He used his changeup more often, which made his high-80s fastball more effective, and had excellent control, working a walk-free seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Milton returns to action and the rotation as the fifth starter after nearly three weeks on the disabled list with a back strain. Milton, resurrecting his career after two years idled by Tommy John surgery, pitched well in four starts with a 2-0 record and 2.89 ERA. He relies on location and not velocity and seemed to have regained the feel for his breaking ball before going to the sidelines. He pitched 5 1/3 scoreless innings in his final rehab start Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander had his personal scoreless inning streak reach 20 frames before it ended on a two-run home run in the eighth inning against the Diamondbacks. Hernandez had to pitch out of a bases-loaded, nobody-out jam in the second inning to keep the streak alive. Even so, he has now surrendered five earned runs in his past 45 innings and continues to bid for his first All-Star Game invitation. This will be Felix's second career start against the Dodgers. He is 0-1, having lost to the NL club at Dodger Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda allowed a Paul Konerko home run but was otherwise dominant for 8 2/3 innings against the White Sox. After allowing nine runs in 11 1/3 innings of his previous two starts, Kuroda made an adjustment of the grip on his two-seam fastball and the increased movement was dramatic, leading to a dozen ground outs in addition to nine strikeouts. In five previous starts, he had not gone deeper than six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Olson's last start against San Diego didn't go as well as his previous outing, which also came against the Padres. The left-hander allowed six runs --all earned -- in 5 1/3 innings, allowing San Diego to break things open in the middle frames after cruising through the first three innings. He didn't walk anyone, but gave up a two-run home run to Adrian Gonzalez in the fourth and never really got comfortable after that, yielding another two runs in the fifth before giving up two more in the sixth. Olson surrendered eight hits while throwing 82 pitches, 59 for strikes. This will be Olson's first career start against the Dodgers.

home_pitcher_note: Chamberlain put together a solid outing against the Braves on Thursday, working 6 1/3 innings and allowing two earned runs while picking up his fourth win of the season. Perhaps the key to his start was his control. He had no walks after surrendering nine bases on balls in his last 10 innings. Chamberlain's strong command led to his longest outing since June 1.
away_pitcher_note: Morrow is steadily gaining traction on the road to becoming a starter.
