His last outing, against the Padres, was the best of his three starts this season, as he allowed three runs on six hits over five innings and put his team in position to claim a 4-3 win. The right-hander is still searching for his first win, but an increasing pitch count -- he threw 87 last time out -- and growing confidence are positive signs that his progression as a starter is coming along nicely.

home_pitcher_note: Pettitte followed arguably his best start of the season with likely his worst. The left-hander squandered an 8-1 lead and exited after just 3 2/3 innings, having surrendered six runs (three earned). Though New York won the game, 11-7, Pettitte let the Braves back in the game and was disgusted with himself afterward. Manager Joe Girardi said Pettitte lost his command in the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn finally got back into the win column in his last start, against the Padres, again providing six solid innings while allowing just two runs in a 9-3 Mariners win. The outing snapped a 12-game winless streak for the left-hander, who had pitched well enough to win in most of those starts. His ERA now sits at 3.22, though he went a little more than two months between victories. Washburn is 5-5 with a 2.56 ERA lifetime against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: If there were any lingering doubts about CC Sabathia's health, he quickly put those to rest in his last start on Friday. He worked seven dominating innings against the Mets, allowing just one run while picking up his seventh win of the season. He surrendered three hits in the fifth, but no other baserunners. This comes after Sabathia was pulled from a game in the second inning in Florida.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball proved troublesome for the lefty in his last start as he surrendered two of them in one game for the first time this season. A three-run jack to a left-handed batter was most costly and Vargas has surrendered almost as many home runs to lefties (four) as he has to right-handers (five) in roughly one-third as many at-bats. This will be his first career appearance against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield has been a rock for the Red Sox all season. His last start, a 1-0 victory over the Braves, was one of his best. He threw six shutout innings, allowing three hits. Wakefield has 10 quality starts and has held opponents to a .255 average. Wakefield has been strong at Fenway this season, going 6-0 with a 3.55 ERA in seven starts. This is his first start this season against Seattle. Lifetime against the Mariners, Wakefield is 4-9 with a 4.06 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez returns to the scene of one of his best career starts -- a one-hitter against the Red Sox at Fenway Park three years ago -- on a big-time roll. The ace right-hander has surrendered five earned runs in his past 53 innings, striking out 51 over that span. His two-seam fastball has been his bread-and-butter pitch, and rookie catcher Rob Johnson has not been shy about calling for it.

home_pitcher_note: The big right-hander has been a rock for the Red Sox of late, giving up three earned runs or fewer in seven of his past eight starts. Penny gave up two runs over six innings in his last start, a 2-1 loss to the Braves. Despite his 1-2 record, June was Penny's best month of the season, as evidenced by his 3.18 ERA. In seven starts at Fenway Park, Penny is 4-1 with a 4.66 ERA. Penny lost his only career start to the Mariners, giving up 10 hits and five runs over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: The first four innings of Olson's last start were about as good as it gets. Olson held the Dodgers to one hit and no runs, and only one runner reached second base. But the fifth inning was more difficult for the journeyman lefty, who surrendered three hits and two runs, the first via a home run that was the 11th circuit clout he has allowed this season. Even so, Olson did his job and handed a two-run lead over to the bullpen. Olson has an 0-3 career record and an 8.82 ERA in three appearances at Fenway Park. There is a chance, though, that lefty Erik Bedard, sidelined since June 7 with left shoulder inflammation, might get the start instead of Olson.

home_pitcher_note: Though Lester got his 2009 season off to an inconsistent start, he comes off arguably his best outing of the year, in which he allowed just five hits over seven shutout innings, striking out eight without walking a batter against Baltimore on Monday. Especially impressive was the action on his breaking pitch, which has gained tightness and depth since doing extra work with pitching coach John Farrell. He seems to have turned the corner and has allowed two or fewer earned runs in five of his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: When the right-hander learns to harness his control, the conversion from reliever to starter could be a lot smoother road. His five walks against the Yankees in his last start hiked his pitch count to 98 in 4 2/3 innings and he was removed from the game before qualifying for his first victory. The good news is that his stamina is at the point where he can reach the 100-pitch level, but he still needs to get quicker outs. Otherwise, he'll have difficulty reaching the six-inning mark.

home_pitcher_note: It was back to the norm last time out for Washburn, who has received the least amount of run support of any starting pitcher in the American League. He held the Yankees to four runs but received just two runs of support and sustained his 105th career loss. Washburn allowed three home runs, the second time in 15 starts this season he surrendered more than one circuit clout in a game and the first hat trick. Washburn will be making his second start against the Orioles this season. He dropped a 1-0 decision to them on June 1 at Safeco Field.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen continued his string of impressive starts, throwing eight innings and giving up just one earned run to pick up his sixth win of the season. He shut down a powerful Red Sox lineup, striking out six batters on 103 pitches. Despite the strong outing, however, the Orioles bullpen gave up a four-run ninth, leaving Bergesen with the no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard's long-awaited, and much-delayed, return to action could be against his former Orioles teammates. Bedard has been sidelined since June 7. He complained of shoulder soreness the following day and eventually went on the 15-day disabled list. He had an MRI on the shoulder, which checked out clean. He figures to be on a 60-pitch limit the first time out. If he makes the start, it will be his second against Baltimore this season. He defeated the Birds on June 2 at Safeco Field.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie pitched relatively well in his last outing, but he gave up two home runs to Bobby Abreu that made the difference in the game. The right-hander has completed six innings in 12 of his 17 starts this season but has also allowed a league-high total of 19 home runs. The former first-round draftee has not won more than two starts in a row this season and has struck out more than five batters just twice.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander battled a flu bug most of the night prior to his last start, against the Yankees, but he felt good enough to pitch and took the game to the fifth inning. He was perspiring heavily during the outing but said he felt good and pleased with holding the Bronx Bombers to four runs. Vargas has faced the Orioles twice this season, receiving a no-decision on June 3, when he held Baltimore to two runs over 5 1/3 innings and absorbed the loss in a 3-1 Mariners defeat six days later in Baltimore.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez turned in perhaps his best start in his last outing, when he worked into the seventh inning in front of a friendly crowd at Angels Stadium. The right-hander made just one mistake in that game -- a two-run homer by Kendry Morales -- and later said it actually came on a good pitch. Hernandez, a strikeout artist in the Minors, has yet to strike out more than three batters in a big league start.

home_pitcher_note: Fresh off being named the American League's Pitcher of the Month for June, Hernandez had his 15-inning scoreless streak end at Fenway Park, but he remained unbeaten at the AL's oldest facility. The three earned runs he allowed were the most in a start since May 19, when the Angels scored six earned runs off the righty.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter allowed one earned run over 5 1/3 innings against the Rays on Friday, which happened to be his 23rd birthday. He picked up his first Major League win. Hunter struck out a career-high five batters and 55 of his 90 pitches were strikes. In all three of his starts this season, he has logged five innings and allowed three runs or less. The 2.31 ERA he has posted over his last two starts lower his season figure from 5.06 to 3.17. He has never faced the Mariners in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Signs of progress were seen in the converted reliever's most recent start as he held the Red Sox to three runs over six innings at Fenway Park, striking out a season-high seven batters. All three runs came via solo home runs, but he walked just two and departed with a one-run lead. He has surrendered just four earned runs in his last two starts, covering 10 2/3 innings. He has improved in each outing on changing speeds and using his slider and changeup more often.
away_pitcher_note: Feldman gave up two runs -- one earned -- over six innings on Sunday against the Rays, allowing four walks but just three hits. As a starter this season, Feldman has held opponents to a .217 average (65-for-299). Feldman has posted nine quality starts this season and has logged at least five innings in all 14 of his starts this season, posting six or more innings 11 times. The right-hander is 7-2 with a 3.25 ERA as a starter this season, and he has a 2.30 ERA in 12 games -- three starts -- spanning 27 1/3 innings against the Mariners in his career. In four games at SAFECO Field, Feldman hasn't allowed an earned run in 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn pitched one of the best games ever by a Mariner at Safeco Field his last time out, as he twirled a complete-game, one-hit shutout in a 5-0 win over Baltimore. Washburn retired 27 of the 28 batters he faced, allowing only a soft single to left field in the fourth inning. It was the fourth shutout of his career, the 10th one-hitter in franchise history and the first ever at Safeco Field by a Seattle pitcher. His four-seam and two-seam fastballs were especially effective, as he needed to throw just one changeup the entire game. Washburn is 8-8 with a 4.29 ERA in his career against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Millwood lost for only the second time in his last eight starts when he was beaten by the Angels, 9-4, on Monday. He tied a career high by allowing nine runs in five innings. He was 4-1 with a 1.30 ERA in five starts in June but has a 10.33 ERA in two starts in July. He is 8-9 with a 4.81 ERA in 19 career starts against the Mariners and is 3-6 with a 5.18 ERA in 11 starts at Safeco Field. He won there, 6-5, on May 4 to snap a four-game losing streak against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard showed good stuff in his first start back from the disabled list, retiring the last 10 batters he faced in four innings of work against Baltimore. He ran into trouble in the first inning, running up his pitch count early, causing his removal after the fourth inning. Two runs on two hits was all the Orioles managed, though, and the left-hander still managed to rack up eight strikeouts while throwing 72 pitches. Bedard is expected to be on a higher pitch count in this one. He's 4-2 lifetime against the Rangers with a 3.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Nippert made his return from the 60-day disabled list against the Angels on Tuesday, and he gets his second start of the season against the Mariners. He went 3 2/3 innings his last time out, allowing three runs on seven hits in an 8-5 Texas win. Nippert threw 72 pitches in that game, and manager Ron Washington said he doesn't have a set plan on how many innings he'll allow Nippert to throw against Seattle. That means he's not likely to be on any kind of strict pitch count. Nippert is 1-0 with a 1.59 ERA in his career against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Cliff Lee is coming off two straight quality starts, but he got the loss in each of them.  Lee is tied for the Major League lead in losses, but is 12th in the American League in ERA.  Lee is suffering from a lack of run support, but he has done a good job of locating his pitches.  The reigning AL Cy Young Award winner is 7-1 lifetime against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners come out of the All-Star break with Olson making his ninth start of the season. He has been solid at times and shaky at other times, winning all three of his games in a starting role. His most recent start was July 4 against the Red Sox at Fenway Park and it was one of his better ones. He held the Sox to four hits and two earned runs in 6 1/3 innings. He walked four and struck out five, which figured in a high pitch count. He's most effective when changing speeds, keeping hitters off-balance. This will be his third career appearance against the Indians and he is 1-0 with a 5.25 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Huff has been the beneficiary of a lot of run support lately. In his most recent outing against the White Sox, he went 4 1/3 innings, giving up eight runs, but the Indians scored 10. Prior to that, Huff went six innings, giving up three runs to the A's, as the Indians racked up 15 runs of their own. Huff has never faced the Mariners. The left-hander has been very hittable, giving up 74 hits in his 56 1/3 innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: The first-time All-Star takes a five-game winning streak into his first start of the second half, hoping to build on a string of seven consecutive stellar starts. Besides being named to the Midsummer Classic team, Hernandez garnered AL Pitcher of the Month honors for June, and he already has won as many games this season as he did all of 2008. His attitude has changed immensely since being challenged by manager Don Wakamatsu following a subpar effort against the Angels on May 19, and he has worked especially well with backup catcher Rob Johnson. Hernandez was 2-0 against the Tribe last season and is 2-1 in his career against them.

home_pitcher_note: Ohka is pitching for a job in the rotation. With the demotion of Jeremy Sowers, Ohka has a chance to emerge as a regular in the Indians rotation. In order to be successful, Ohka has to keep the ball down. He doesn't possess dominant stuff, which makes location crucial for him. When he gets the ball up, opposing hitters tee off. Ohka averages giving up one home run about every four innings. Right-handers especially get to him; they hit .354 against the veteran, while lefties hit .239.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn acknowledges that he has pitched better this season than at any time of his career. A sinker that pitching coach Rick Adair helped Washburn develop during Spring Training is the pitch that has become his best weapon. Washburn has made nine starts since May 18 and surrendered two or fewer runs in seven of them. He has a career record of 7-7 with a 4.56 ERA in 19 appearances against the Indians. He is 6-3 in Cleveland.

home_pitcher_note: In his three career games against the Mariners, Laffey has given up 13 runs in 15 2/3 innings, but only eight of the runs were earned.  He also served up three home runs in that time.  Laffey has done a great job of keeping opposing hitters in the ballpark this season.  He's given up just one home run in 40 1/3 innings of work.  This will be Laffey's second start since coming off the disabled list earlier this month for a strained oblique.  In his most recent outing, Laffey went six innings, giving up four runs in a loss to the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: More than a month and one MRI after making his last start, the left-hander returned to the rotation on the final day before the All-Star break and pitched in and out of trouble against the Rangers. He threw 93 pitches over 5 2/3 innings, walking four and striking out five. Perhaps the long layoff affected his ability to command his curveball, which wasn't as sharp in the strikezone as it normally is. But he came out of the game healthy and that is the Mariners' main concern. When 100 percent, not 99 or below, he is as good as any pitcher in the American League. Bedard has career record of 2-0 with a 3.61 ERA against the Indians.

home_pitcher_note: Porcello will make his first start since July 5, the result of the Tigers' effort to hold down his workload as the 20-year-old enters the second half of his rookie season. He pitched 125 innings last year in his only full pro season, and he's at 87 innings now, leaving manager Jim Leyland to estimate he has about 15 starts left in him this year. If he starts every five games after this, not counting Friday's day-night doubleheader, he'd use up 14 of those in the regular season. His first of those pits him against the same Mariners squad he beat for his first Major League win with seven innings of one-run ball on April 19 at Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Olson never got going on Thursday against the Indians, giving up three runs, two earned, on five hits and three walks before the Tribe chased him in the third inning. Olson will have the ball in the series opener against the Tigers as manager Don Wakamatsu plans to experiment with a four-man rotation until he decides who will take the fifth spot. In two starts against Detroit last season, Olson gave up 10 earned runs on 11 hits and seven walks in 7 2-3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his first-ever meeting against the Mariners, Galarraga will try to pick up his pitching recovery that had been building before the All-Star break. He lost his last start with four runs on nine hits over six-plus innings against Cleveland last Saturday, but he pitched into the seventh inning with one run allowed in both of his previous outings. Pitching into the seventh itself is big for Galarraga and the Tigers, who badly need a third starter who can take on a big workload alongside Justin Verlander and Edwin Jackson. If Galarraga can do it effectively, the Tigers rotation looks deep heading into their playoff run.
away_pitcher_note: In his most recent start, Hernandez dominated the Indians most of the night, striking out eight and allowing two runs on five hits and a walk over eight innings in earning his 10th victory of 2009. Against the Tigers, who beat Hernandez in his debut in 2005, Hernandez has won four straight. In Detroit's first shot at King Felix this season, on April 17, Hernandez scattered seven hits and a walk over six innings of work, allowing three runs while earning the win. Hernandez is 4-2 lifetime against the Tigers.

home_pitcher_note: French put on a good show in his most recent start, a no-decision effort against the Yankees in New York on July 17 in which he gave up two runs, only one of which was earned, on five hits over five innings. He left with a 3-2 lead and the bullpen did a melt down in the seventh inning. French, in three starts since being called up from Triple-A Toledo, has given up just four earned runs in 16 innings. He made two relief appearances against Oakland, giving up no runs and no hits over three innings. He has never pitched against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: Washburn said he wasn't sharp after his last outing against Cleveland, but the Indians would dispute that. The left-hander allowed one run in 6 2/3 innings in winning for the third straight start and for the fourth time in his last five starts. Washburn gave up eight hits, struck out three and didn't walk a batter. He has allowed two runs in his last 23 2/3 innings. Washburn didn't have a good feel for his breaking pitches, but relied on his fastball, which had good movement. He will face a good test against Detroit's potent lineup.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith has been called up from Triple-A Tacoma to make his second start of the season. Manager Don Wakamatsu is happy with the progress of the 26-year-old, whose numbers rapidly progressed over his few outings in the Minors. Rowland-Smith has bounced between the rotation and the bullpen for Seattle over the last few years, including a 5-3 record and 3.42 ERA in 47 games (12 starts, two saves) in 2008. There seems to be a rotation spot for the taking if Rowland-Smith can answer the call.
away_pitcher_note: Laffey, making his second start since his return from a right oblique strain, settled down after a rough first inning against the Mariners on Sunday. He gave up three runs on eight hits with two walks and three strikeouts in six innings. In this outing, he'll have to make adjustments against a Mariners lineup that now knows him well.

home_pitcher_note: Bedard received an extra day off from manager Don Wakamatsu and will be pitching on five days rest. He has given up six earned runs in 14 1/3 innings since coming off the disabled list in early July after left shoulder inflammation. Bedard has actually been significantly better against right-handed batters this year than left (1.08 WHIP against righties and 1.38 WHIP versus lefties). He is 2-0 with a 3.55 ERA lifetime against Cleveland in eight starts, including a no-decision in his last start against Cleveland on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: The Indians will give Sowers yet another chance to prove he can be an effective starter at this level. Sowers, who will be promoted from Triple-A Columbus just two weeks after he was last sent down, has shown flashes this season, but he struggles as the game wears on. The opposition is hitting .196 off him the first time through the order, .244 the second time and .558 the third time. Sowers is 2-1 with a 2.52 ERA in four career starts against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: There was talk that Brandon Morrow would be recalled to make this start, but Jason Vargas will get the ball instead. It's his first outing since a July 8 start against the Orioles, in which he tossed five scoreless innings but received a no-decision. Vargas has yet to face the Indians in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Record aside, Lee, the subject of many trade rumors in advance of the July 31 Trade Deadline, has been on top of his game much of this season and particularly in his last two starts. He's tossed consecutive complete games, with two wins to show for it. He became the first Tribe pitcher to throw consecutive complete games with no walks allowed since CC Sabathia did so in July 2006. Lee's ERA is the lowest among AL pitchers with a losing record, and his 2.79 ERA over the last two years is second in the AL only to Roy Halladay's 2.76 mark.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez hasn't wavered from his status as one of the premier aces in baseball. He's won seven starts in a row, the most recent coming in a seven-inning effort against Detroit. Hernandez gave up one run on six hits to earn the victory. The 23-year-old right-hander is 7-0 with a 1.29 ERA in his last 11 starts. This is his first start against Toronto this season, but he is 2-1 with a 2.89 ERA in four career starts against the Blue Jays.
away_pitcher_note: Romero won his first game in four starts in a 10-6 victory over the Indians on Wednesday at Rogers Centre. He gave up four runs (all earned) on four hits, lasting 5 1/3 innings. He struggled with his command, issuing five walks, which tied a season high. He had only two strikeouts -- tied for the fewest in any start this season. Three of the four runs he gave up came on a sixth-inning home run by Luis Valbuena -- the last batter Romero faced. Of the last 37 earned runs Romero has given up, 23 have come via the home run. He has never faced Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Washburn has pitched like a Cy Young candidate over his last seven starts. He's 5-1 during that span with a 1.81 ERA, and he's given up just two earned runs in his last four starts. Last time out, he got the win against the Tigers by throwing seven scoreless innings and allowing just two hits. This will be his first start against the Blue Jays this season, and he's 4-7 lifetime against Toronto with a 4.23 ERA. Washburn hasn't lost since July 1.
away_pitcher_note: Rzepczynski did not record a quality start for the first time in his four Major League starts, taking the loss as the Indians beat the Jays, 5-4, on Thursday at Rogers Centre. In his shortest start this year, Rzepczynski gave up four runs on three hits in 4 1/3 innings. Only two of the runs were earned, as a fielding error by third baseman Jose Bautista led to a pair of unearned runs in the fifth inning. Rzepczynski issued four walks, hit a batter and struck out six. He has never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith made his first start after a long rehab stint with Triple-A Tacoma, against the Indians, and he didn't disappoint. Things got away from him a little bit in the seventh inning when he gave up two home runs, and he ended up allowing four runs over seven innings in the M's 9-0 loss. But he retired 14 batters in a row at one point, and said his curveball felt particularly sharp. The left-hander has made three career appearances against Toronto, and is 0-0 with a 5.63 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay pitched nine innings for the fourth time this season, allowing only two runs, but came away with a no-decision in a 10-inning, 4-2 loss to the Rays on Friday at Rogers Centre. One of the two runs was unearned due to a third-inning passed ball by catcher Rod Barajas. Halladay allowed four hits and issued three walks. He struck out 10, marking the second time this year he has fanned 10 or more batters. Halladay has not faced Seattle this year, but is 5-4 with a 2.67 ERA in 11 career starts (13 appearances) against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Holland is 1-5 with a 6.42 ERA in nine starts this season after a 6-3 loss to the Royals on Saturday night. He is 1-2 with a 7.52 ERA in his last four starts. He has made five starts and four relief appearances at home this season where he is 2-4 with an 8.18 ERA. Left-handed hitters are batting .282 off him this season, but right-handers are hitting .320 and opponents are hitting .346 with runners in scoring position. He is 1-0 with a 3.86 ERA in three relief appearances against the Mariners this year.
away_pitcher_note: It's really anyone's guess as to who is going to start this game for Seattle, since it's Erik Bedard's turn and he just went on the disabled list. Olson seems like the logical choice, even though he was sent to the bullpen after a rough outing against Detroit in which he couldn't get out of the second inning. Chris Jakubauskas and Brandon Morrow are also possible options, though Jakubauskas has worked quite a bit out of the bullpen recently and Morrow was sent to Triple-A prior to the All Star break to work on becoming a starter. With trade rumors heating up, a lot could change by the time this game comes around. If Olson does make the start, it would be the first time he's faced Texas as a starter this season. The left-hander has made three relief appearances against the Rangers, pitching an inning of scoreless ball in each of them.

home_pitcher_note: Padilla was scratched from last Wednesday's start due to swine flu and Tuesday's start because he didn't think his legs would last. He hasn't started since July 17, when he allowed five earned runs over seven innings against the Twins. Padilla posted a 4.15 ERA over two starts in July. In his career against the Mariners, Padilla is 4-5 with a 4.03 ERA over 80 1/3 innings in 15 games, including 13 starts. He is 18-17 over 48 career starts at Rangers Ballpark in Arlington.
away_pitcher_note: Since the Mariners could be short on starting pitching soon, depending on what happens with Jarrod Washburn at the non-waiver July 31 Trade Deadline, Vargas will probably make this start despite a rough outing last week. He went just four-plus innings against the Indians in his first start back from Triple-A, allowing six runs in a blowout loss. He got into a bit of a groove after the second inning but ran into trouble in the fifth and exited with the bases loaded and nobody out. The left-hander has faced Texas once this season, when he gave up one run in five innings in a 7-1 loss. He did not get a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hunter pitched a career-high seven innings against the Tigers on Monday, allowing one earned run. He has now won in three consecutive decisions over his last four starts. In his past five starts since being called up from Triple-A, Hunter is 3-1 with a 1.47 ERA.  He has thrown four quality starts over that span. He has thrown at least six innings in four of his six starts this season. In one career start against the Mariners, Hunter received a no-decision, allowing no earned runs over six innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: The staff ace attempts to bounce back from an uncharacteristic outing, surrendering a season-high seven runs in a loss to the Blue Jays. The setback ended a personal seven-game winning streak, which catapulted him into his first All-Star Game. He was not the same, as the Jays hit two home runs off him, the first time that had happened since May 9.

home_pitcher_note: Feldman allowed six earned runs on 10 hits over 2 1/3 innings on Wednesday against the Tigers. He faced 18 batters, which tied the fewest his faced this season in a start. (The other came when he was pulled after a lengthy delay on June 13.) It was the shortest outing in 43 career starts for Feldman and the most runs allowed this season. He had thrown at least five innings in 17 starts entering tonight and snapped a streak of six consecutive quality starts. Feldman needed 38 pitches to escape the first inning and 18 more to record just one out in the third. In his career against the Athletics, he is 3-2 with a 3.73 ERA in 41 innings pitched. He has posted a 5.19 ERA in 60 games -- 21 starts -- away from home.
away_pitcher_note: Snell makes his Mariners debut after being acquired from the Pirates in a seven-player trade on Wednesday. He went 2-8 with a 5.36 ERA in 15 starts for the Pirates and was 2-2 with a 0.96 ERA in six starts for Triple-A Indianapolis in the International League. He struck out 17 batters over seven innings in his first Triple-A start on June 28 against Toledo. Snell becomes the 10th pitcher to start a game for the Mariners this season. This will be his second career start against the Rangers. He pitched a complete game victory on June 13, 2007.

home_pitcher_note: Hochevar's run of four straight winning decisions ended at Baltimore last Thursday when he gave up 11 hits and seven runs in six innings. He couldn't do much good with his breaking pitches, so the Orioles sat on his fastball and whacked away. His control continued to be good, though, and he walked just one -- his only pass in his last three games. Hochevar's strikeouts dipped to just four after he'd racked up 22 in his previous two starts including a career-high 13 against Texas.
away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith is coming off perhaps the best game of his career. He went seven innings Wednesday, allowing three hits and two runs, walking none and striking out four. He no-hit the potent Blue Jays lineup for six innings. It was his second straight outing in which he went seven innings and he has gone at least six in 10 of his last 11 starts. He's becoming more consistent, using all his pitches aggressively to keep hitters off balance. He does not have a decision against Kansas City in five career starts. He has a 3.38 ERA against the Royals.

home_pitcher_note: Sidney Ponson was scheduled to make this start but he's been designated for assignment, and Davies was recalled from Triple-A Omaha to again assume a spot in the rotation. After going to Omaha on June 20, he had a 4-2 record and a 2.14 ERA in eight starts. In 46 1/3 innings, he gave up 47 hits and 14 walks with 44 strikeouts. One of his assignments was to harness command of his fastball, an ongoing concern for the right-hander, and he made progress, although manager Trey Hillman said he still needs to work on it.
away_pitcher_note: Acquired in a two-for-one trade with the Tigers on Friday, the 23-year-old lefty makes his debut with Seattle against the team he defeated on July 8. He held the Royals to six hits and one run over 6 1/3 innings and walked one. He says the keys to his success is throwing strikes, keeping the ball down and mixing speeds. French was an eighth-round Draft choice by the Royals out of Colorado.

home_pitcher_note: Chen, the only left-hander in the Royals rotation, last Saturday had the longest and the best outing since being called up from Triple-A. He went 6 2/3 innings at Tampa Bay and held the Rays to five hits and three runs. As has been customary, the Royals gave him precious little backing (one run) and his run support in seven starts is a staff-low 2.3. Chen has added a cutter to his pitch list and he's been more successful in keeping the ball down, a must for him. He got seven groundouts against the Rays and had seven strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: One bad inning, or bad one pitch as he put it, put a damper on his previous start. A strike away from getting out of the fifth inning against the Rangers with the game tied, he surrendered two singles and a home run, absorbing his fifth loss of the season. A couple of misplaced changeups led to his downfall and that has been a dependable pitch for him since becoming part of the starting rotation. He's averaging a little more than twice as many strikeouts (45) as walks.

home_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander battled with his command for seven innings in his last start but still managed to beat the Rangers and notch his 12th win of the season. A lot of fortitude and a little luck worked in his favor as he went as he could without his best fastball or slider. It was his second straight substandard outing for the All-Star, but neither he nor the club seems concerned. This will be his first start of the season against the Rays, the only team the Mariners have not played. Felix started one game against Tampa Bay last season, held the eventual AL champs to one run over eight innings, but had to settle for a no-decision. He is 1-1 with a 2.54 ERA in five career starts against the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: The unforeseen sterling season for Jeff Niemann continued Saturday, as the rookie right-hander became the first Rays pitcher to reach double digits in wins this season. Since May 13, he's 8-2 with a 2.70 ERA and is 2-0 with a 0.52 ERA in two starts against Kansas City. It was his eighth quality start and the fifth time he's pitched eight-plus innings this year. Certainly Niemann is a candidate for American League Rookie of the Year, and he may even find himself in a Cy Young race if he keeps at this pace. Manager Joe Maddon was particularly pleased how he maintained composure all game long despite not having great command with his curveball, which is his normally his best pitch.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander, acquired from the Pirates in the Jack Wilson deal, makes his home debut when he faces the reigning AL-champion Rays at Safeco Field. Snell looked sharp in his first start for Seattle, holding the Rangers to three hits and two runs -- both on solo home runs -- over six innings in Arlington. Snell kept the Rangers off balance with an assortment of fastballs, sliders and a changeup that ranged in speed from 81 to 94 mph. His strike-to-ball ratio wasn't terrific, but he received good reviews for his effort. This will be Snell's first career appearance against the Rays, but he has faced Pat Burrell 15 times and surrendered four hits, including a double, but no RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: Shields flirted with history. Then he became a victim to a silent Rays offense once again. It was a devastating loss for Shields and the Rays against Kansas City on Sunday. The right-hander took a no-hitter into the eighth inning but the game remained in a scoreless tie. He ended up giving up two hits and two runs -- one earned -- but took the loss as the Rays simply couldn't muster any support. Shields has received the second-lowest run support in the American League this season, and his deepening frustration after the game on Sunday showed. He's winless in his last eight starts while the Rays have failed to score at least three runs in 14 of his 23 outings this year.

home_pitcher_note: It's hard to tell what to expect from the left-hander from Australia from one start to the next. After looking superb against the Twins on July 29, taking a no-hitter into the sixth inning and notching his first win of the season, Rowland-Smith had a clunker against the Royals, surrendering six hits and five runs (four earned) during a rather wobbly four-inning stint. The leadoff hitter reached base in three of the four innings he pitched and two of them scored. Rowland-Smith was 0-0 with one save in three appearances against the Rays last season and has faced them four times in his MLB career.
away_pitcher_note: Kazmir won his second start in a row on Monday, beating Zack Greinke and the Royals to even up his record on the season. Kazmir said he has been feeling better and better since the All-Star break and his confidence continues to build. He's faced a tough stretch of opposing pitchers over the past four starts, yet he has battled through with a 2-1 record and 3.60 during that span. Kazmir's velocity remains in the low 90s, which he feels is a range he is comfortable with and can control. So far, he's making Tampa Bay look wise not to trade him.

home_pitcher_note: As debuts go, the left-hander acquired from the Tigers a few hours before the non-waiver Trade Deadline had a real good one in the strike-throwing department. Of the 89 pitches he threw against the Royals, 61 of them were strikes. French pitched ahead in the count most of the game. Two of the nine hits he allowed were first-pitch home runs with a runner on base. This will be his first career outing against the White Sox, and he not faced anyone on the Sox's current roster.
away_pitcher_note: Floyd was masterful in his last outing, a 6-2 victory against the Angels on Wednesday night. He lasted eight-plus innings, allowing two runs -- one earned -- on six hits while striking out six and walking one. White Sox manager Ozzie Guillen made a mound visit to Floyd with two outs in the eighth with two runners on and Floyd having thrown 96 pitches. Guillen decided to leave Floyd in the contest, and the move paid off. Floyd struck out Bobby Abreu to end the eighth. Floyd now has tossed 12 quality starts in his last 14 outings. Over that span, which dates back to May 22, he is 7-2 with a 2.24 ERA. Floyd also improved to 5-0 with a 1.54 ERA over his last eight home starts. He is 1-2 with a 7.15 ERA against the Mariners lifetime in six games (four starts).

home_pitcher_note: Fister moves into the rotation spot that left-hander Jason Vargas had before he pitched himself back to the Minor Leagues. This will be Fister's first start as a Major Leaguer, though he did make his MLB debut by pitching a scoreless ninth inning in a 10-4 loss to the Rays on Saturday. He was 6-4 with a 3.81 ERA in 22 games (17 starts) with Triple-A Tacoma. Mariners manager Don Wakamatsu describes him as a command pitcher with five different pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Danks did well to push himself to the seventh inning in his last start, a 9-5 loss against the Angels. He did not pitch particularly well in the game's first three innings, surrendering six runs and two homers, but appeared to settle down beyond that point, allowing one run from there. He allowed three home runs in a game for the second time this season and gave up five or more runs for the third time. Lifetime against the Mariners, Danks is 0-4 in four starts with a 8.10 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: He got bailed out by some late-game heroics, but Hernandez wasn't sharp in his last outing against the Rays. He walked six batters in six innings, gave up five runs on five hits and fell behind batters more than normal. The M's defense didn't help, though, as some passed balls and an error may have run up Hernandez's pitch count a little more than it should have. The right-hander was dominant in his only start against the White Sox this season, striking out nine and holding Chicago scoreless on four hits in eight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Since tossing the 18th perfect game in Major League history on July 23, Buehrle has gone 0-3 with an 8.35 ERA. He also lost back-to-back home starts for the first time since Sept. 7-18, 2006. On Friday night against the Indians, Buehrle was far from sharp. He allowed a runner to reach base in every inning, surrendering six runs on 11 hits in 7 2/3 innings of work. By allowing so many balls in play, Buehrle also became the first Major League pitcher to induce six double-play grounders since Kansas City's Dick Drago on May 6, 1972. Lifetime against the Mariners, Buehrle is 7-4 with a 4.02 ERA in 14 games (13 starts).

home_pitcher_note: Snell's first item of business in this one: Throw strikes. He didn't do that in his last outing, when he lasted just 1 1/3 innings after walking six batters against Tampa Bay. The right-hander had no command of his fastball and said he felt nervous and jittery in his first career appearance at Safeco Field. The stuff is there, he just has to learn how to harness it, which has been a problem his entire career. This will be Snell's first career start against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia looks for his 13th win of the season after hurling 7 2/3 outstanding innings to defeat the Red Sox in his last start, striking out a season-high nine and allowing just two hits in what played as his signature performance thus far in pinstripes. He retired his first 13 batters before allowing a two-out single to Jacoby Ellsbury in the sixth and is 17-2 in the month of August since 2005, the most wins in the Majors for that month over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith had another solid outing in his fourth start back from a lengthy rehab stint, allowing two runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings to earn his second win of the season. He gave up a two-run homer in the second inning but then settled down to retire 13 of his next 15 batters. The left-hander notched six strikeouts and threw 109 pitches, something he was pleased with. Rowland-Smith has made five appearances and pitched 10 innings in his career against the Yankees, who have collected 13 hits and eight earned runs against the lefty.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte will try to pitch the Yankees to another victory on Friday in the second game of a four-game set at Safeco Field. The lefty is coming off what Joe Girardi thought was his finest outing of the season, a seven-inning showing against the Red Sox on Sunday in which he took a no-decision, but allowed just five hits while walking two and striking out four. Pettitte has allowed just seven earned runs in his last five starts (33 2/3 innings), for a 1.87 ERA. He beat the Mariners on July 1 in New York, hurling seven innings of two-run ball in a 4-2 Yankees win.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie's home debut was both good and bad. He held the White Sox to three hits over 5 1/3 innings, but the six walks he issued -- including three in the sixth inning -- provided a dark side to the outing. French turned defensive in his final inning, trying to hit the corners and was not successful. The six free passes were the most the 23-year-old had allowed in any appearance this season -- including 13 in the Minor Leagues, seven with the Tigers and one with Seattle. away_pitcher_note: The Yankees are sticking with Mitre for at least one more turn through the rotation after the right-hander was tagged with his first loss of the season on Aug. 10, hit for five runs (three earned) and six hits in five innings by the Blue Jays. home_pitcher_note: The rookie gave himself a tough act to follow in his maiden voyage in the big leagues as a starter. His fastball topped out at 90 mph, but he had good movement on his pitches and changed speeds well.
away_pitcher_note: The Yankees eased off their rest plan by putting Chamberlain back in the rotation for Sunday's start against the Mariners at Safeco Field. home_pitcher_note: Porcello should be well rested after throwing just 15 pitches Tuesday at Boston, where Kevin Youkilis' charge of the mound after a second-inning pitch off his back started a bench-clearing fracas and led to their respective five-game suspensions. away_pitcher_note: After three sub-par performances, the staff ace returned to the All-Star version of Felix, holding the White Sox scoreless over seven innings on Wednesday night. home_pitcher_note: The way Verlander is pitching in big games, it's becoming tougher to keep him out of discussions about potential American League Cy Young candidates heading into the home stretch. away_pitcher_note: Snell's second start at Safeco Field lasted much longer than the first one, but he remains winless in his new uniform. away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith is coming off a start worthy of a win. He held the Yankees to a pair of tainted runs and had to settle for a no-decision. home_pitcher_note: Huff won his second successive start by topping the Twins on Saturday. Despite struggling, he was able to hang on long enough to earn his seventh win. Huff has lasted at least six innings in only six starts out of 17 in his rookie campaign. away_pitcher_note: If not for some shoddy defense behind him, French might have won his second game for the Mariners since being acquired from the Tigers. This will be French's first start of the season against the Indians.

He did so, producing this final line -- 5 1/3 innings, three earned runs, five hits, four walks and two strikeouts. Laffey is 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA against the Mariners in two starts this year. away_pitcher_note: The scouting report on Fister indicates that he throws a lot of strikes and has a fastball that rarely reaches the 90-mph mark. The rookie right-hander has a solid pitching repertoire, from fastball to changeup, and he feels confident throwing any of them during any count.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona had his first real setback in four starts since returning to the Indians rotation. Carmona gave up as many runs -- five -- in his first three innings against the Angels as he had in his previous three games combined. In all Carmona gave up three earned runs on ten hits with four strikeouts and two walks in just five innings. away_pitcher_note: The team's top winner had to settle for his ninth no-decision of the season in his last start after holding the Tigers to one run over seven innings. home_pitcher_note: The fourth time was the charm for the right-hander acquired from the Pirates on July 29. Snell went with sinkers most of the way. A small tweak in his delivery, improving the take-away from his glove, seemed to help with his command. away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Mazzaro got out of a pair of bases-loaded jams to hold the Yankees to two runs (one earned) over five innings, allowing six hits and striking out two. The rookie is 2-0 with a 3.52 ERA over his past three starts after going 0-8 with a 7.22 ERA in his previous 10. This will be Snell's first start against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty from Australia had mixed results in his previous outing. All three of the runners he left on base when he departed in the sixth inning scored, which hiked his ERA over the 4.00 mark. Opponents are 3-for-23 against him in the first inning. away_pitcher_note: Anderson threw seven impressive innings on Wednesday but surrendered a two-run home run to Mark Teixeira that proved to be the difference in a 3-2 loss to the Yankees. away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez continued his efforts in improving his command and pounding the strike zone in his last start but took a loss against a tough Detroit lineup. home_pitcher_note:

away_pitcher_note: In his last outing against the Twins, Davies gave up six runs in 5 2/3 innings although he allowed just four hits along with three walks. away_pitcher_note: After winning two games with uninspiring five-inning efforts, Meche's third start since returning from the disabled list was a solid seven-inning performance. away_pitcher_note: Greinke returned to his old dominant self with a 15-strikeout performance against the Indians in his last start. home_pitcher_note: French seems to be finding his way nicely for the Mariners, as he went 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the A's, earning the win by allowing three runs on six hits. He's won two starts in a row now and is 3-1 with Seattle since coming over in a July 31 trade from Detroit. The rookie left-hander also was better with his control, walking just one batter after walking a combined 12 in his previous three starts. He's faced Kansas City twice this year, once each with the Mariners and Tigers. He won both decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders looked more like his old self with a solid start against the Tigers on Wednesday at Angel Stadium. After missing two weeks on the disabled list with a knot in his throwing shoulder, Saunders came back with increased velocity and struck out six batters to show it. He allowed two runs over five innings with the two runs coming on a homer by Adam Everett with two outs in the fifth inning. Saunders faces the Mariners, a team he has fared well against in the past, with a 6-1 career record and a 3.60 ERA in eight starts against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Fister finally looked like a rookie in his last outing, surrendering three home runs to the Royals in his first Major League loss. The right-hander only gave up five hits, but the three long balls also put up five runs against him and he exited after the sixth inning despite throwing just 86 pitches. He did have good command, walking just one and throwing 57 of his pitches for strikes. This will be Fister's first career appearance against the Angels.
away_pitcher_note: Santana pitched capably, but he was outdueled by the Athletics' Trevor Cahill in a 2-0 loss on Thursday night at home. Santana held the A's to two earned runs on eight hits and two walks, striking out six men, but lost to Oakland for only the second time in 12 career decisions. Santana is 6-2 with a 4.50 ERA on the road but has struggled (1-5) at home. Santana is 0-1 in two starts against the Mariners with a 6.75 ERA this season but is 6-3 lifetime with a 4.36 ERA in 14 outings. At Safeco Field he's 3-2 with a 4.75 ERA in six outings.

home_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander returned to his winning ways in his last outing, holding the Royals to three runs on five hits over seven innings. He hadn't won since Aug. 1. Perhaps the most important thing now for Hernandez is keeping pace in the Cy Young Award race, and he'll have to do that against some pretty stiff competition. Four of the six teams Hernandez is on schedule to face are playoff contenders. He lost his only start against the Angels this year, when he allowed six runs and 11 hits over 5 2/3 innings on May 30.
away_pitcher_note: The Angels will slot in their new left-hander for his first start since coming over in a trade from the Rays against Mariners ace Felix Hernandez, a tough spot to be sure. But Kazmir has had good success against the Mariners in his career, going 3-1 with a 3.21 ERA in six career starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: Tomko's first start, he beat the team that had recently released him, the American League East-leading Yankees. His next time out, he beat the AL Central-leading Tigers. In his most recent outing, he held the AL West-leading Angels to four hits and a walk while striking out five over 5 2/3 innings and left the game with a 6-1 lead, but the Halos stormed back to win and stick Tomko with a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Snell gave up three hits and two runs in five innings against the Royals in his last outing, but he left after five innings because of swelling in his right forearm after taking a line drive off the arm in the fifth. He finished the frame, and his day was done after just 68 pitches. X-rays were negative, and Snell should be ready to go for his next start. Despite the early exit, Snell still found his way to the win column for the third consecutive start, and he has now allowed just four earned runs in his past three outings. Snell gave up 13 runs in his first three starts with the Mariners. His only appearance against the A's this season was during the Mariners' last homestand, when he held Oakland to one run on four hits over six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired in the July trade that sent Matt Holliday to the Cardinals, Mortensen is making a spot start in place of rookie right-hander Vin Mazzaro, who has been temporarily shut down with shoulder tendinitis. Mortensen, a 24-year-old who has a 9-8 record with a 4.39 ERA in 23 starts at Triple-A this season, made his A's debut on Aug. 8 against the Royals and allowed eight runs on eight hits and three walks over four innings. He was sent back down after the outing.
away_pitcher_note: A lack of run support continues to haunt Rowland-Smith, who has experienced the feeling in his past two outings. Rowland-Smith threw 113 pitches -- 80 for strikes -- in a stellar, but losing, effort. Rowland-Smith is holding opponents to .212 (7-for-33) average in the first inning. This will be the lefty's third start against the Athletics this season, and he has yet to record a decision.

away_pitcher_note: Fister gets the award for best turnaround in back-to-back starts. The classy lefty retired 18 in a row before walking Mike Sweeney on four pitches to lead off the seventh, Sweeney scoring on Bill Hall's one-out double. He used his combination of his trademark slider and his newly-developed splitter to near-perfection, not to mention the kind of swings and misses he couldn't produce as often the past couple years while he tried to deal with decreased velocity. He'll try to repeat his success in his home state of Washington against a Mariners squad that has struggled offensively early on.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty from Australia is coming off a confidence-boosting outing against the Athletics. Though tagged with the loss in Seattle's home opener at Safeco Field, Rowland-Smith surrendered just three hits over seven innings. However, he also walked five batters, including the first three batters in the fourth inning, which led to a run. He's not a strikeout pitcher -- two in 12 innings this season -- so he must throw quality strikes consistently and put the ball in play. Rowland-Smith has started two games against the Tigers and received no-decisions in both. He has a 5.13 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: In many ways, Verlander's start to this season closely resembles his first month of last season -- potentially dominant stuff but inconsistent command of his secondary pitches, leaving him struggling to finish off hitters in tight spots. He had an encouraging sign against the Mariners in April of last season, despite a big inning, and he's hoping to find his first win of the year in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: A death in the family forced the right-hander to leave the team for a few days and return to his offseason home in Florida, but he's expected to make his third start on schedule. Snell is coming off a rocky outing, lasting just three innings against the Rangers, but manager Don Wakamatsu attributed some of that to the personal issues that were tugging at him. Snell is 1-1 with a 2.13 ERA in two career starts against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: After the Royals put up better approaches at the plate against Scherzer in their second meeting, Scherzer gets an opponent he has never faced in Seattle. A foul ball dropped by Miguel Cabrera extended the fourth inning for the Royals on Monday, and they pounced on Scherzer with a two-run homer from Jose Guillen. Errors, combined with nine Royals hits, forced 101 pitches out of Scherzer over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Fresno State product pitched his best game in the Major Leagues in his most recent outing, holding the Athletics to three hits over eight scoreless innings. He threw strikes with all of his pitches and changed speeds to keep the hitters off-balance. Only one runner advanced beyond first base in the masterpiece. Of the 100 pitches he threw, 71 of them were strikes. If he can come anywhere close to duplicating that performance against the Tigers, he could stay in the rotation even when left-hander Cliff Lee returns from the disabled list. This will be Fister's first career appearance against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Bergesen allowed five earned runs on seven hits, walking two and fanning three over three-plus innings to take the loss against the Rays on Wednesday. The Orioles' home-opener starter, Bergesen hasn't had a favorable start yet and has struggled to find the sink on his ball that makes him so effective. He said following Wednesday's start that he was going to work with pitching coach Rick Kranitz to make a minor adjustment on his arm angle, and will look to get back on track against the Mariners. Bergesen is 1-1 with a 2.14 ERA in three career starts against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander had the most economical outing of the season for the Mariners, needing only 89 pitches to navigate six solid innings against the Athletics in his last outing. He was around the plate all night long and finished with no walks and six strikeouts. It was the second time in 16 starts with Seattle that he pitched at least six innings and did not issue any free passes. This will be Vargas' fourth career start against the Orioles. He is 0-1 with a 2.81 ERA versus the Birds.
away_pitcher_note: Orioles starter David Hernandez got into trouble early Thursday night, allowing the A's leadoff man to reach base in four of his first five innings. Several defensive miscues behind him didn't help and Hernandez exited after five innings, yielding five runs (four earned) on seven hits and a walk. The young right-hander struck out six in the 99-pitch effort, and settled down considerably following the first two innings. He will look to get his first win of the season on Tuesday, and his first career win against Seattle at that. In two career games against the Mariners, Hernandez is 0-1 with a 5.56 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The third quality start of the season turned out to be the charm for the ace right-hander, who dominated the Tigers to the tune of four hits and season-high nine strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings in his last start. Hernandez is working on a Major League-best 16-game streak of quality starts. For the first time in 2010, he was able to click into cruise control as the Mariners showered him with 11 runs. Hernandez varied the speed of his pitches against the Tigers, reaching 97 mph with his fastball and backing off with 88-mph changeups. Hernandez has now won 16 of his past 18 decisions.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, it took Millwood 75 pitches to get through the game's first 10 outs, but to his credit, he stayed on the mound through six innings. The veteran right-hander said his fastball and slider "stunk" but he still gutted out an impressive 115-pitch performance against the A's. Millwood struck out nine batters -- an Orioles season high -- and for the third time this season, he gave the O's a quality start without a quality outcome, falling to 0-2. He will look to buck that trend against Seattle. Millwood is 8-11 with a 5.08 ERA in 21 career starts against the Mariners. He is 3-7 with a 5.25 ERA in 12 starts at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: To classify Floyd's brief 51-pitch trip to the mound on Sunday in Cleveland as one of the worst in his successful career would be an understatement. Floyd faced 13 batters in one-plus innings and retired only three. In contrast, reliever Tony Pena came into the contest with a runner on first and nobody out and needed one pitch to retire two in the second on a double play. Floyd gave up seven runs on six hits, including Shin-Soo Choo's grand slam, walking four and striking out two. Floyd will be working on normal four days rest when he opens the weekend series against Seattle. The right-hander has a 1-4 record with a lofty 7.47 ERA over six starts and eight games pitched in total against the Mariners, but Floyd does hold a 16-9 lifetime record at U.S. Cellular Field.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander pitched well enough to win his first game of the season in his last outing, holding the Tigers to two runs over six-plus innings -- a quality start -- but had to settle for a no-decision in his duel against Detroit ace Justin Verlander. A breaking ball that ended up in Magglio Ordonez's wheelhouse was the first hit Rowland-Smith surrendered. Two of the four hits he allowed were for extra bases and he struck out a season-high three. Rowland-Smith is 1-0 with a 1.08 ERA in two career appearances, including one start, against the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The term used for the rotation change involving Garcia this weeks is not that he is being skipped but instead Garcia will receive a couple of extra days in between starts. With Garcia's regular turn being pushed back from Wednesday to Saturday, the veteran will have an eight-day respite and the front four of the rotation will stay on their regular rest. Garcia needs to produce a far better showing than his last trip to the mound, when Toronto tattooed him from seven runs on eight hits in three-plus innings. Garcia has allowed 11 hits and walked eight over 10 innings this season, while fanning seven. The one-time ace of the Seattle staff will be making start No. 8 against his old team, entering with a 3-3 ledger and a 6.04 ERA when facing the Mariners. Garcia has a 47-20 career record in day games.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander's confidence is at an all-time high following a best-of-his-career start against the Orioles. Fister took a no-hitter into the seventh inning before settling for a three-hitter and second consecutive win. The 6-foot-8 hurler throws over the top on a downward plane, giving his fastball a late break, which makes it difficult for hitters to center the ball. Though not overpowering, topping out at about 92 mph, he changes speed effectively and uses a changeup and sharp-breaking curve to keep hitters honest. He is developing an excellent working relationship with catcher Rob Johnson, allowing just one earned run in their two games together. Fister has made one previous start against the White Sox, holding them to one hit over six scoreless innings in a no-decision outing last season.

home_pitcher_note: The southpaw stopped the proverbial bleeding for the White Sox on Tuesday night, with his stellar start ending a four-game losing streak for his team and cutting short Tampa Bay's seven-game winning streak. Danks allowed two hits and two walks over eight innings, striking out nine in a tremendous 113-pitch effort. He had his cutter working well in the early innings, used his changeup once the Tampa Bay order turned over and then felt comfortable throwing any of his four pitches for a strike later in the game. Danks has given up just four hits and two earned runs over his last 15 innings. He has a 1-4 record and 5.00 ERA lifetime against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty is coming off one of the best outings of his year-plus career with the Mariners, holding the Orioles to three hits and one run over seven innings at Safeco Field last Tuesday night. Finally completely healthy after hip surgery almost two years ago, he has combined power with precision to post back-to-back quality starts and his strikeout-walk ratio (16-3) is outstanding. He has mastered the changeup, which has made his fastball look faster than it actually is, but hitters have a difficult time with it. Vargas is making a strong bid to stay in the rotation when Cliff Lee returns on April 30. He has faced the White Sox only once in his career, a two-thirds inning relief stint.

home_pitcher_note: Davies got through six innings of his last start at Toronto holding a 3-2 lead but ran into trouble in the seventh. The Blue Jays took the lead with two runs -- and saddled Davies with a loss -- before he could get an out. But Davies was toppled by a deep fly ball that might have been caught and two infield singles. In short, he pitched pretty well, as he's been doing rather consistently in his first three starts. Davies' charge to himself is to be aggressive and avoid being too nitpicky, thereby avoiding the control issues that have plagued him in other years. In his career against Seattle, Davies is 2-1 with a 4.74 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The staff ace is off to another terrific start this season, eating up the innings as the leading starter usually does. Hernandez has made four starts and pitched into the seventh inning in each of them, including a complete-game victory in his last outing. He surrendered nine hits to the Orioles, but only two runners advanced beyond second base and the run he allowed was unearned. Felix has now made 17 consecutive quality starts, a franchise record, and won his last nine decisions, dating to last August. Hernandez was 1-0 with a 3.86 in one start against the Royals last season.

home_pitcher_note: The 2009 American League Cy Young Award winner is looking for his first win of the season after four starts. Last year, Greinke won his first six starts. The stuff has been just about as good as last year, but until his April 21 start against the Blue Jays, the command wasn't where it should be. In Toronto, he pitched seven two-hit innings and left with a lead. The first Toronto hit of the game was a two-run homer by Alex Gonzalez in the fourth after Greinke hit Fred Lewis with a pitch to start the inning. Greinke had one walk, in the first inning, but that was eliminated on a double play. He struck out eight and had 66 strikes from 109 pitches. It was an improvement over his previous start in Toronto last June 5, which was probably his worst outing of 2009, when he gave up seven runs (five earned) on nine hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: A death in the family forced the right-hander to leave the team for a few days and return to his offseason home in Florida, delaying his most recent start by one day. The between-start inactivity and bacterial virus took its toll on Snell, but he managed to go five innings against the Tigers at Safeco Field. It was a gutty performance, but a losing one, thanks to a three-run home run he surrendered. The four walks increased his pitch count to the point he had to leave prematurely. Snell made two starts against the White Sox last season, going 0-1 with a 8.10 ERA -- nine earned runs in 10 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Meche and the Royals are thoroughly perplexed about the right-hander's struggles in his first three starts. His 2010 debut was delayed a few days as he recovered from a Spring Training bout with right shoulder stiffness, but everyone insists that's no longer a factor. The club honchos have been dissecting his mechanics and delivery, but so far no one has uncovered any flaws -- at least for public consumption. In his last outing, against Minnesota, Meche had trouble controlling his breaking balls and changeups; they were coming in much too low and he couldn't seem to correct that. So far, he's given up 12 walks in 12 2/3 innings along with 19 hits (two homers). He's faced his former club six times, posting a 2-2 record and a 5.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Don Wakamatsu sensed that the left-hander is feeling the pressure of trying to remain a part of the starting staff when lefty Cliff Lee enters the five-man rotation for the first time on Friday. The skipper and pitching coach Rick Adair advised Rowland-Smith to trust his stuff and not worry about anything else. Wakamatsu said Rowland-Smith is not in danger of leaving the rotation, but he must start producing to stay in the mix. Rowland-Smith is at his best when he works quickly and moves the ball around the strike zone, pitching to contact. His 10 walks and five strikeouts are not what the Mariners are looking for. Rowland-Smith was 0-1 with a 5.25 ERA in two starts against the Royals last season.

home_pitcher_note: The much-anticipated regular season debut of the 2008 American League Cy Young Award winner arrives as Lee takes on the Rangers at Safeco Field. A foot injury at the beginning of Spring Training, a strained lower abdominal muscle and a five-game suspension that was rescinded are all behind the veteran lefty, and it's full-speed ahead. Lee tuned up for Friday's start with six scoreless innings in a rehab start for Triple-A Tacoma last Sunday. He threw all of his pitches, commanded the strike zone and was basically pleased with the way he felt. He needed just 65 pitches to make it through six innings but should be able to reach the 100-pitch mark on Friday night without any problems.
away_pitcher_note: Lewis beat the Tigers on Sunday while allowing four runs in 6 1/3 innings. He allowed the four runs in the first two innings, but then retired 15 of 16 hitters to get the victory. He struck out 10 for the second time in four starts. He is only the third Rangers pitcher to strike out 10 or more batters in multiple April starts; Nolan Ryan did it in 1989, and Bobby Witt did it in 1986. Opponents are hitting .136 off Lewis with runners in scoring position through his first four starts. He has a 4.35 ERA in two starts on the road. Lewis made his first start of the season against the Mariners, allowing one run in seven innings in a 5-1 victory.

home_pitcher_note: A personal nine-decision winning streak, dating to last August 28, came to an end for the ace right-hander in his last start, although he extended his streak of quality starts to 18. He said the lack of run support has not affected the way he has gone about his work, but it's difficult to pitch when you know one or two runs could be enough to lose the game. He has pitched into the seventh inning in each of his five starts, but there simply is no room for mistakes with every outing being so closely contested, making every pitch critical to the outcome. This will be Felix's second start against the Rangers this season. He settled for a no-decision against them on April 10 in Arlington, allowing three runs (two earned) over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Harrison allowed six runs in six innings in Monday's start against the Tigers and has allowed 12 runs in 10 innings over his last two starts. He allowed just two earned runs in 13 innings in his first two starts. The Rangers lost, 8-6, on Monday and have now lost all four games that Harrison has started. His first start of the season was against the Mariners on April 10 at the Ballpark and he allowed one run in six innings. He left with a 3-1 lead but the Mariners scored three in the ninth to steal his victory. Harrison has made four starts against the Mariners, his most against any American League opponent, and is 1-1 with a 3.91 ERA against them. But this will be his first start at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Fister did a nice job of holding Cliff Lee's place in the rotation through his first four starts, posting a 1.67 ERA (best among the team's starters) and a 2-1 record. With Lee back in the fold, Fister could give the Mariners an elite one-two-three punch if he stays hot. He lasted just four innings, threw 96 pitches and took the loss in his first outing of the season against Oakland, but since then, Fister has notched three quality starts in a row. He allowed just six hits and one walk during his next two appearances -- both wins -- and gave up two runs in eight innings against the White Sox last week, a game Seattle lost after closer David Aardsma was tagged for two homers in the ninth. Fister doesn't have a high strikeout rate (4.33 per nine innings), but his pitch-to-contact style works well at Safeco Field. As long as he doesn't put himself in harm's way by issuing free passes, he could thrive with the Mariners' solid defense behind him.
away_pitcher_note: Wilson beat the White Sox, 4-2, in his last start on Tuesday by allowing two runs in six innings. It was his fourth straight quality start to begin the year, the first member of the Rangers' Opening Day rotation to post four quality starts to begin a season since both Kevin Brown (six) and Charlie Leibrandt (four) accomplished the feat in 1993. The last Texas pitcher with an ERA of 1.75 or lower in four starts or more in April was Brown, who had a 1.14 ERA in his first four starts in 1993. Wilson is 1-1 with a 2.13 ERA in his first two starts on the road. He is 5-2 with a 5.77 ERA in 38 career appearances against the Mariners. That's his most appearances and most wins against any team in his career. He has a 6.28 ERA against the Mariners at Safeco.

home_pitcher_note: Much like teammate Doug Fister, Vargas bounced back from a rough debut to post three straight quality starts. He was tagged for eight hits and five runs in a 5 1/3-inning, season-opening loss at Texas, then allowed just five runs total in his next three outings. He notched wins against Oakland and Baltimore, then took a no-decision against the White Sox after leaving a 2-2 ballgame after 6 2/3 innings. While not a dominant arm, Vargas has shown an ability to strike batters out. He ranks behind Felix Hernandez on the club in that category with 19 in 25 innings, along with just six walks. With Cliff Lee and Hernandez around for the heavy lifting, the Mariners need Vargas to stay consistent and not give away runs with control problems. At any rate, he did enough to keep his spot in the rotation, as Ian Snell was bounced to the bullpen upon Lee's return.
away_pitcher_note: Shields went seven innings against Oakland Wednesday night to pick up his third win of the season. The right-hander allowed one earned run on a home run in the first, but he dominated after the early blemish, finishing with 12 strikeouts to tie a career high. At 28, Shields is the old man of a young Rays staff and serves as a leader at the top of the rotation. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth innings, which is evidenced by three consecutive seasons with at least 215 innings pitched. He is a master at using his fastball command to set up one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields is 2-2 with a 2.34 ERA in six career starts against the Mariners; he is 2-2 with a 2.55 ERA in five career starts at SAFECO Field.

home_pitcher_note: Lee certainly didn't disappoint in his much-anticipated debut, throwing seven shutout innings, striking out eight, walking zero and not allowing a runner past first base. As Mariners manager Don Wakamatsu said after the game, you can't ask for much more than that. Seattle wasted the strong outing though, failing to score a run despite numerous chances and dropping a 2-0 game in 12 innings. The good news is, Lee felt no ill effects from the 98-pitch evening, his first Major League start since suffering an abdominal strain during Spring Training. His fastball hovered around 93 miles per hour, and he threw 73 strikes, a promising beginning to a season the Mariners hope will match his 2008 Cy Young Award performance.
away_pitcher_note: Garza will make his sixth start of the year after going six innings and earning a win against Kansas City on Thursday, when he allowed five hits and one earned run while striking out nine batters and walking just two. Garza had plenty of early run support, as the Rays scored 10 runs in the first four innings, but he never gave the Royals a chance to close the gap. This will be Garza's fifth career start against the Mariners and his third at Safeco Field. He holds a 1-1 record against Seattle, having pitched 17 2/3 innings with a 9.17 ERA -- the highest against any opponent other than the Cardinals for Garza.

home_pitcher_note: After a lackluster start, Rowland-Smith seemed a good candidate to get bumped to the bullpen upon Cliff Lee's return. But manager Don Wakamatsu is showing confidence in the Australian, who has a reputation for being a slow starter. He lived up to that so far, going 0-1 in five starts, and he hasn't made it through the sixth inning in any of his outings on the road. He fares better at home, as his fly-ball-inducing style (69 fly balls and 32 ground balls) fits better at Safeco Field. He has struck out just nine of the 127 batters faced, putting him in the Doug Fister category of pitching to contact and letting the Mariners' defense do the heavy lifting.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann will make his sixth start of the season against the Mariners, following up his 7 1/3-inning, three-hit performance on Friday against the Royals. The big right-hander gave up just one earned run to Kansas City while striking out three batters and walking four, one of which was intentional. Niemann benefited from some great defense behind him in that outing, including three inning-ending double plays. He works quick, as he is averaging only 13.6 pitches per inning -- putting him just below Minnesota's Francisco Liriano, who led the American League in that category before Friday's game with 13.9.

home_pitcher_note: The staff ace had his franchise record of 18 consecutive quality starts end in his last outing, thanks to a misplay in left field by Milton Bradley and a stiff lower back that contributed to his earliest departure of the season -- one out into the fifth inning against the Rangers on May 1. The discomfort has subsided and Hernandez says he's ready for his seventh start of the season, which comes against the AL West-rival Angels at Safeco Field. Felix has had his way with Angels first baseman Howie Kendrick, who is 2-for-18 with one RBI off Hernandez, while second baseman Kendry Morales is 10-for-28 with one home run and five RBIs against Felix.
away_pitcher_note: Weaver, the new ace of the staff, had his first substandard start of the season in Detroit on Sunday, lasting only 4 2/3 innings and giving up four earned runs on seven hits and one walk, striking out six men. He needed 107 pitches, having thrown 80 after four scoreless rounds before trouble materialized. Weaver is 8-3 with a 4.61 ERA in 14 career starts against Seattle and is 3-3 with a 6.00 ERA in eight outings at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: Fister has been the most -- and maybe only -- pleasant surprise for the Mariners. Through five starts, his ERA and WHIP are the best in baseball, feats he has accomplished by leaning on Seattle's solid defense rather than making batters look foolish at the plate. His strikeout rate per nine innings is 4.11. Without dominant stuff, Fister relies on location and by forcing contact. The key is to avoid walks, something he has done well in his past four starts, handing out just two free passes in 31 innings. He's also getting more ground balls than fly balls, a reason why he hasn't allowed a home run yet this season.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders' struggles continued with his third consecutive dismal outing, lasting only four innings amid a barrage of Boston hits, including homers by Kevin Youkilis and Bill Hall. Yielding seven earned runs on nine hits and four walks, Saunders was unable to put his pitches in good locations after working a perfect first inning. He'll try to regain command in Seattle's friendly confines, where he is 5-0 in six career starts with a 2.55 ERA. Saunders is 7-1, 3.19 in 10 career outings against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas has made a strong case for why he should stay in the rotation when Erik Bedard returns.
