After giving up five runs in his first start of the year, Vargas has allowed eight over his next four outings. His formula is along the same lines of Doug Fister's: don't walk batters and let the defense do the talking. But Vargas has shown some bark, too. He struck out a career-high eight batters against Tampa Bay, when he gave up three runs on four hits in 6 2/3 innings. Vargas is pitching consistently, but with an average run support of 3.13, he has been pitching with a slim margin for error.
away_pitcher_note: Santana showed his composure and high-quality stuff in holding the Red Sox to one run across seven innings on Tuesday night at Fenway Park. Boston scored in the first inning but was 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position as Santana struck out seven while allowing seven hits and one walk. He was throwing 93-95 mph with an excellent slider. The Angels have scored only 21 runs in his six starts. Santana is 6-3 with a 4.18 ERA in 15 career starts against the Mariners and is 3-2 with a 4.29 mark in seven starts at Safeco Field.

home_pitcher_note: The Orioles' fifth starter, Hernandez is coming off his worst start this season. The young right-hander allowed a season-high six earned runs on six hits and four walks and did not make it out of the fourth inning in Thursday's game at the new Yankee Stadium. Hernandez never looked comfortable on the hill and has struggled at times to command his stuff. He is still looking for his first win and will try to get back on track in Monday's opener against the Mariners. Hernandez is a careeer 0-2 with a 5.09 ERA in three starts against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: He's only two starts into the season, but the Mariners already know what they're going to get when Lee takes the mound. Lee was kicking himself after his most recent outing -- an 8-3 loss to Tampa Bay in which he allowed five runs (one unearned) on 10 hits in eight innings -- for letting the Rays back into the game right after the Mariners took a lead. Manager Don Wakamatsu places the blame on the ineffective Seattle offense, which he says puts pressure on pitchers to be perfect. Lee puts that pressure on himself anyway.

home_pitcher_note: Bergesen tossed his best start this season in Thursday's series opener against the Twins, picking up his second win in the process. The right-hander got off to a rocky start and was sent to Triple-A to get his sinker back and regain the confidence in his pitches. Bergesen credited that time for helping him give a performance like Thursday's. He allowed six hits over 6 2/3 scoreless outings, collecting season highs in both categories. Bergesen will try to take that momentum in Tuesday's start against Seattle. In four career starts against the Mariners, Bergesen is 1-2 with a 3.42 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith earned manager Don Wakamatsu's trust last season, and that helped keep him in the rotation despite a slow start when Cliff Lee returned from injury. But his form didn't improve Thursday against Tampa Bay, which scored six runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings. He has only gone deeper than six innings in one of his six starts. It's not the end of the world this early in the season, but if he doesn't turn it around soon, he may find himself in the bullpen when Erik Bedard returns from injury, possibly as early as the end of May. A start against the Orioles -- owners of the worst record in baseball -- could do the trick.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran and de facto ace of the Orioles staff, Millwood has pitched much better than his record indicates. A true pro who sets the tone for the younger arms, Millwood allowed three earned runs over seven innings in Saturday's loss to the Twins in the nightcap of a doubleheader. Afterwards, Millwood joked that his lack of run support must mean this was his "lucky year." All kidding aside, the right-hander has earned some help from the O's offense. Millwood got one run of support in seven innings Saturday (a Luke Scott solo blast in the fifth), and the O's have plated a total of 12 runs in the seven starts he's been on the hill -- a stretch that spans 47 frames. He will look to buck that trend in Thursday's start. Millwood is a career 8-12 with a 5.05 ERA in 22 starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez suffered a tough loss against the Angels in his last outing, giving up three home runs and only lasting 3 1/3 innings, his shortest stint of 2010 and only the second time in his career that he pitched fewer than four innings in a start, the other time coming on May 15, 2007, also against the Angels. He matched his career high in home runs allowed in one game. Manager Don Wakamatsu said the problem wasn't a stiff back that had hurt Hernandez in his previous start, but rather inconsistency in his mechanics. Hernandez is working on fixing the problem with pitching coach Rick Adair.

home_pitcher_note: After outdueling reigning AL Cy Young winner Zack Greinke in a 2-1 win over Kansas City, Davis struggled for the second time this season against Oakland. He lasted just five innings, allowing six hits and three runs. Davis had runners on base in every inning except the fifth. By then, he had already thrown 99 pitches, 59 of those strikes, and he was done for the day. He struggled with control of his off-speed pitches and got hurt when he left some of them up. In his first start this season against the A's, he gave up seven hits and four runs and lasted just five innings, throwing 95 pitches, 58 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: One of the biggest surprises of the early season takes his game indoors for the first time as he faces the Rays in the opener of a three-game series in St. Petersburg. This will be his seventh start of the season and he has strung together five consecutive quality starts. He has held opposing hitters to a .205 batting average with an assortment of over-the-top fastballs and breaking pitches that have late movement. His 18 strikeouts and six walks in 42 innings is an indication of how often he's around the strike zone. He has made one career appearance against the Rays, tossing a scoreless inning of relief in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Shields pitched well enough to win against Oakland on Sunday when he allowed two earned runs on 11 hits in six innings. Working against him largely was the fact that Oakland left-hander Dallas Braden pitched a perfect game. The 28-year-old right-hander is the old man of a young Rays staff and serves as a leader at the top of the rotation. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth innings. Shields is off to a good start this season with six quality starts in seven outings. He is a master at using his fastball command to setup one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields is 3-2 with a 2.32 ERA in seven career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas has been among the most consistent pitchers in the rotation this season and is coming off a splendid performance against the Angels, a win that snapped an eight-game losing streak. He kept the Angels hitters off-balance with fastballs and change-ups over 7 1/3 innings, retiring 15 of the 18 batters he faced between the first and seventh innings. He has emerged as a top-of-the-line starter in a rotation that has done exceedingly well most of the season. This will be his first career start against the Rays, against whom he has made one career appearance, retiring both batters he faced in a relief outing in 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Garza gave up four early runs Monday night against the Angels, but he still managed to hang in the game for 7 1/3 innings, allowing no further damage and giving the Rays a chance to win. The Rays ended up tying the score, which gave Garza a no-decision. The 26-year-old right-hander has pitched eight innings in four of his seven starts this season. Garza has the best stuff on the staff, which he can put on display in any given start and he seems to be maturing on the mound, which has led to his no longer allowing his emotions get the best of him. Garza is 2-1 with a 7.01 ERA in five career starts against the Mariners; he is 14-9, 3.10 in 35 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander has taken all three of his starts into the seventh inning and is working on a streak of 22 1/3 walk-free innings. Lee hasn't been overpowering by any stretch of the imagination, but has been the epitome of a pitcher, moving the ball inside and out. He has enjoyed success against the Ray, posting a 6-3 record and 2.53 ERA against them in 11 career starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez lasted just four innings in his last start on Wednesday, giving up four earned runs on nine hits while striking out three. Gonzalez attributed his struggles to lack of command, saying he left too many balls up in the strike zone during the 10-1 Rangers' win. It was Gonzalez's shortest outing of the year, and followed three performances when he completed at least 6 2/3 innings. In his previous start against the Mariners on April 14, Gonzalez went 4 2/3 innings, giving up two earned runs on six hits and four walks while striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: It has been a rough go for Rowland-Smith so far this season, but the left-hander gets another chance to show what he can do as a starter. His spot in the rotation could be be slipping away, and he needs a strong effort to rebuild his confidence. Rowland-Smith has made seven starts, the most recent being a tough three-inning defeat to the Orioles in Baltimore. Afterward, Rowland-Smith said he needs to get back to pitching "with a chip on my shoulder." He is 2-2 with a 3.62 ERA in his career against the Athletics. In three starts at the Oakland Coliseum, he is 1-0 with a 3.31 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his second straight quality outing on Thursday, though it came in a 2-1 extra innings loss in Texas. He went six innings, giving up an earned run on three hits and three walks while striking out eight. It was the second straight start that Sheets had recorded eight strikeouts. Both his manager Bob Geren and catcher Josh Donaldson said Sheets has added a cutter to his repertoire, though Sheets wouldn't confirm such talk. Sheets faced the Mariners on Opening Day, giving up three runs (two earned) on four hits and four walks while striking out three.
away_pitcher_note: The ace right-hander takes his second shot at getting his record back to the break-even point. Hernandez pitched well enough in his last outing to snap his personal three-game skid, surrendering just one run over seven innings against the Orioles, but the four-run lead he gave to the bullpen went out the window in the eighth inning and he had to settle for a no-decision. Hernandez did, however, pronounce himself "back" after three subpar performances.  The righty has faced the Athletics once this season, winning on Opening Night in Oakland.

home_pitcher_note: One of the biggest surprises in the Major Leagues during the first month and half of the season, Fister hopes to continue his state-of-the-art pitching against the visiting Blue Jays as the Mariners begin a homestand. Fister ranks third in the American League in ERA and is a close second to Cliff Lee as the most consistent starter in the Seattle rotation. He was put to a stern test in his previous start, holding the Rays to one run over five tough innings. A high pitch count got him out of the game, not the Rays hitters. He has struck out 20 batters and walked nine in seven starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cecil gave up hits to his first four batters in his start against the Texas Rangers on Friday. Not surprisingly, he lasted two innings and was raked for eight hits and eight earned runs along with two walks. The eight earned runs were the most Cecil has allowed in his big league career and it was the shortest start of his career. But the Blue Jays had their aerial game working, and five home runs helped overcome Cecil's subpar outing to produce a 16-10 victory and present him with a no-decision. Fortunately for Cecil, he won't have to face the Rangers this time. He has allowed 15 earned runs over seven innings in two career starts against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: Saturday in Tampa Bay was same old, same old for Vargas, who allowed just two runs and four hits through seven innings but took a no-decision after a late bullpen mistake and lack of run support led to a 3-2 loss. In his seven outings, the Mariners have scored two runs four times, making life difficult during his string of six straight quality starts. Vargas and Doug Fister have been Seattle's pleasant surprises, and after showing consistency, it's time to stop regarding their success as lucky starts to the season.
away_pitcher_note: Romero saw his season ERA plummet from 3.42 to 2.88 over the course or nine crisp innings at home against the Rangers on Saturday afternoon. The left-hander completed the first shutout of his young career, holding Texas' potent lineup to five hits (all singles) with just one walk issued. Along the way, Romero matched a career high with 12 strikeouts. Romero featured a strong changeup, as well as an effective, curve, cutter and fastball. He concentrated on throwing to the middle of the plate, allowing his strong pitch movement to do the rest. It worked, considering Romero threw 70 percent (81-for-116) of his pitches for strikes. Romero threw one ball or fewer to 24 of the 32 hitters he faced. The strong performance came after the sophomore yielded 12 runs on 21 hits with 11 walks over 17 1/3 innings across his previous three turns. Romero has gone 1-0 with a 5.11 ERA in two career games against the Mariners.

LeBlanc did not allow a hit until the sixth inning against the Dodgers on Sunday, and surrendered only one run on two hits over seven innings, but took the loss nonetheless. The San Diego offense was shut out by Chad Billingsley and two Dodgers relievers, giving LeBlanc little margin for error. The left-hander had seen his team win all five of his previous outings, and certainly did enough to give the Padres a chance to win despite the one hiccup in the sixth when Russell Martin pushed across a run with a single. Already having strung together a 20 1/3 inning scoreless stretch earlier this year, LeBlanc will look to build on his success when Interleague Play opens on Friday.

home_pitcher_note: Saturday is Snell's welcome-back start. When Cliff Lee returned from injury, Snell was bounced to the bullpen because of four so-so outings. He lasted six innings just once, but with Ryan Rowland-Smith's recent struggles, Snell was brought back to the rotation after three appearances in long relief. The Mariners' other four starters have either been solid or are named Felix, so Snell is hoping for a sterling second first impression to keep him as a starter through Erik Bedard's return, expected sometime in June.
away_pitcher_note: Both of the last two outings for Richard were lasted seven innings against the division rival Giants, and both were wins. Richard's lost only two starts this season, his first two outings in April, and even those weren't bad. He's yet to allow more than three runs and go fewer than five innings in a start. May was Richard's strongest month in 2009, when he posted a 2.83 ERA and a 2-0 record in four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez just hasn't been himself lately. Ever since a 4 1/3-inning outing against the Rangers where he experienced back problems, Hernandez has been a bit off. He wedged a seven-inning, one-run performance against the Orioles between a 3 1/3-frame loss against the Angels and an 11-hit outing in Oakland on Tuesday. That's not the kind of consistency the Mariners have come to expect, and with a struggling offense, Seattle can't afford to have one of its aces faltering.
away_pitcher_note: Latos found himself apologizing this week for accidentally throwing a baseball beyond left field at AT&T and damaging a broadcaster's car. Latos' performance on the mound has not required any apologies this month. He didn't repeat near-perfection in his last outing, a six-inning, two-run performance against the Giants in a 12-inning loss. In his previous outing, Latos threw a one-hit shutout. For the month, Latos is 2-1 with a 1.24 ERA in 29 innings over four starts, and he's struck out six times as many batters (24) as he's walked (4) in that span.

home_pitcher_note: Fister bounced back from a five-inning outing in Tampa Bay by throwing eight gutsy frames in a 3-2 loss to Toronto. The Jays got him on the ropes with three runs in the third and fourth, but he fought back and retired the final 14 batters he faced in order to notch his sixth quality start in eight tries. He also rung up a season-high five strikeouts in that contest and leads the Mariners talented pitching staff in ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The Mariners saddled Verlander with one of his two losses on the season during the Tigers' last trip to Seattle, where Verlander dropped a pitchers' duel despite seven innings of three-run ball. The Tigers are heading back to the Great Northwest, but it's a nastier Verlander coming with them, having allowed a lone run on eight hits in 15 2/3 innings over his past two outings. He's pitching to more contact these days and getting quicker, deeper outings from it. Verander has lost his past three starts against the Mariners and hasn't beaten them since 2008.

home_pitcher_note: His five-run season-debut aside, Vargas has been excellent, posting six-straight quality starts. He pitched well enough to win in his last outing but took a no-decision after the Mariners made a ninth-inning comeback to top Toronto, 4-3, and he's just 1-1 in May despite giving up nine runs in 27 2/3 innings across four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Bonderman comes back to his home state for the second time in just over a month with a chance for revenge after the Mariners roughed him up for 10 runs, eight earned, over four innings in April. What he's really seeking, though, is a continuing of a very solid May in which he has three quality starts in as many starting assignments and has honed the bite on his slider. He struck out eight Athletics while holding Oakland to a run on three hits over six innings on Thursday for his first victory since April 10. Opponents are batting just .219 with a .561 OPS against him in day games this year, compared with .253 and .684 at night.

home_pitcher_note: In a season of experimenting on the fly with his delivery and arm slot, Kazmir appeared to put it all together on Saturday in St. Louis, holding the Cardinals to six baserunners and three hits across seven innings, yielding three earned runs while striking out five. He had good command of his fastball and brought in his slider and changeup with good effect. He isn't throwing as hard as he has in the past, but his fastball has movement and deception. Kazmir is 3-2 with a 2.68 career ERA in eight starts against the Mariners, and he's 2-1, 5.06 in three outings at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Lee had a rough go in his last start, but still netted his second win of the season to become the first pitcher in Mariners history to get a victory despite allowing eight runs. It was his worst outing since 2007, and he failed to complete seven innings for the first time this year. Lee said he just didn't have his best stuff, but there's no reason to expect he'll repeat that performance. If anything, it's good he got it out of the way on a night where Seattle's offense actually clicked.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver rebounded from a horrible outing in Texas with a more characteristic performance in St. Louis on Sunday, holding the Cards to three runs (two earned) on five hits and two walks in six innings, striking out eight men. His fastball was razor-sharp and his breaking stuff was hitting the right spots as well. He threw 98 pitches and wanted to go deeper in the game. He was dominant against the Mariners in Seattle on May 7, shutting them out on two hits and three walks across 7 1/3 innings, striking out seven. Weaver is 9-3 with a 4.24 ERA in 15 career outings against the Mariners and is 2-1 with a 2.25 ERA this season at home in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Felix took a step in the right direction during an 8-1 loss to San Diego on Sunday, tossing seven innings and allowing three runs on seven hits. His control was back after a few Jekyll-and-Hyde outings, and he rung up six Padres, but took the loss after getting only one run of support. The King may not be back to quite the level that's expected, but his latest appearance established some much-needed consistency.

home_pitcher_note: Saunders was solid against the Blue Jays on Monday at Angel Stadium, allowing three runs on just four hits over 6 1/3 innings. But the Angels offense struggled mightily, recording just two hits on the night in a 6-0 loss. Saunders did struggle with his command, however, as he walked five batters and needed 115 pitches to record 19 outs. Saunders is 7-1 with a 3.06 ERA in 11 career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: After a demotion to the bullpen, Snell got a do-over as a starter and made a solid second first impression. He only went five innings because of a predetermined pitch count of around 90 and wasn't very economical, but holding the Padres to one run on five hits certainly counts for something. Especially when the man he replaced, Ryan Rowland-Smith, had been struggling mightily. Snell said he worked the kinks out of his slider while in the bullpen and has restored his confidence in the pitch, giving him more versatility than he had before being demoted.

home_pitcher_note: Fister continued his impressive start to the season when he limited the Tigers to just three runs (two earned) over seven innings on Tuesday. He simply pitched to contact as he didn't allow a walk and struck out just one batter. Fister will be facing the Twins for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano has dropped his last three decisions after starting the season 4-0. In that stretch, he has given up 15 of his 21 total runs. However, Liriano looked good in his last outing, leaving the game with the score tied. He gave up only two runs and struck out seven batters Wednesday against the Yankees. He pitched through seven innings in that outing, the longest he has gone since his May 2 start against the Indians. He is holding left-handed batters to a .191 average, whereas right-handers are hitting .271 off Liriano. The left-hander has struck out 59 batters this season, 23 since his last win, which was also on May 2.

home_pitcher_note: Vargas was solid against the Tigers on Wednesday, allowing just two runs, but he lasted only five innings for his shortest start of the season. He suffered from some command issues as he walked three batters and needed 109 pitches to get through five frames, but proved he can get results even without his best stuff. He's made one career appearance against the Twins in relief, holding Minnesota scoreless for 1 1/3 innings when he faced the club last season.
away_pitcher_note: Blackburn was strong in his last outing against the Yankees on Thursday. He pitched seven innings and gave up only two runs off nine hits. Blackburn is the only Twins pitcher who has been able to record wins against the Yankees in the past two seasons, getting two in the past two weeks. The right-hander is on a five-game winning streak and hasn't dropped an outing since April 11 against the White Sox. Despite his success, Blackburn credits his wins to the Minnesota offense. In his nine outings, the Twins have managed to put together 57 runs -- the most run support for any starting pitcher. This is compared to the 29 runs Blackburn has allowed this season.

home_pitcher_note: Lee shook off a shaky first inning in which he allowed two runs -- keyed by his wild throwing error to home plate -- but was simply sensational after that rocky first frame against the Angels on Friday. He allowed just three runs (two earned) over eight innings, allowing just four hits and two walks while striking out 10. He also recorded nine straight outs by strikeout, but was so locked in while on the mound he didn't even realize it until he was told after the game. The left-hander is 8-3 with a 3.57 ERA in 17 career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing Friday, Slowey held the Rangers to only one run and six hits through 6 2/3 innings. That start is the longest outing Slowey has had since he threw eight innings on April 20 against Cleveland. Pitching late into the game has been an issue for Slowey as he has made it past the sixth inning in only two starts this season. Pitching coach Rick Anderson said the right-hander has been working on his command and separating his hands quicker on his pitches, and that work showed in Friday's outing. Anderson said Slowey often overthinks his pitches, but his past two outings have been solid and Slowey is gaining confidence. Slowey had five strikeouts against the Rangers and gave up only one walk. His six wins are tied with Nick Blackburn for the most for the Twins and tied for second in the AL.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez didn't hesitate to call his performance against the Angels on Saturday his best of the season. The right-hander allowed only one run over eight-plus innings, with seven strikeouts and just six hits allowed. But he received just one run of support and remained winless for his seventh straight start. He is 3-3 with a 2.77 ERA in nine career starts against the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Pavano held the division-leading Rangers to only two runs on seven hits. Pavano has pitched well nearly all season, but the Twins' offense has not been able to give him much support in his starts. Entering his start Saturday, he had the least amount of run support of any Twins starter. However, after an eight-run effort by Minnesota in his last outing Pavano is now right along with his fellow starters. Pavano has allowed two runs or fewer in seven of his 10 starts this season. His one strikeout against the Rangers was his lowest mark of the year. He has 42 total strikeouts this season. In his last outing, he managed to get his ERA below the 4.00 mark for the first time since May 12.

home_pitcher_note: Snell lasted just four-plus innings against the Angels on Sunday, allowing three runs on four hits. He had problems with his command, as he walked four batters and needed 82 pitches to record just 12 outs. He'll face the Angels again on Friday and will look to improve on his career 7.04 ERA in three starts against the Halos.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders is coming off a rough outing where he ended up with a no-decision last Sunday against the Mariners. The left-hander gave up 10 hits and seven earned runs with three walks as he only last 4 1/3 innings. The Mariners tagged Saunders for six runs in the fourth inning before he was taken out early in the fifth. Saunders will look for his revenge on the Mariners as the Angels open up a three-game series in Seattle.

Santana is rolling as he picked up his fourth consecutive victory against the Royals last Monday. Santana didn't walk a single batter over seven innings, giving up seven hits and one earned run with six strikeouts. He  improved to 4-0 with a 1.86 ERA over his last four starts. The right-hander will look for his sixth victor of the season as the Angels travel to Seattle. In eight career starts at Safeco Field, Santana is 3-3 with a 4.62 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander had another quality start in his last outing, holding the Twins to six hits and one run over seven innings to join teammate Doug Fister in the under-3.00 ERA club. With four wins, Vargas needs just one more to match his single-season high, set with the Marlins in 2005, when he went 5-5. Vargas has surrendered three or fewer runs in nine of his 10 starts this season. He isn't overpowering, striking out 40 batters in 64 2/3 innings, but keeps balls in the park. Vargas has allowed just six home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro is coming off a complete-game loss to the Royals last Tuesday, where he went eight innings, giving up six earned runs on 10 hits, while striking out two, as the Angels lost 6-3. Pineiro is 1-5 in high last eight starts and his ERA has climbed from 1.77 to 5.16.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the White Sox, Feldman went eight innings, giving up five runs on eight hits in a 9-5 win. In his only start against the Mariners this season, Feldman went seven innings while giving up just two runs on seven hits with four strikeouts in a 9-2 win on April 11. In seven career starts against the Mariners, Feldman is 3-1 with a 2.67 ERA and 25 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last two starts, both eight-inning outings, Lee notched twice as many strikeouts (18) as hits allowed and gave up a total of four runs. That was a nice way to bounce back from his worst outing since 2007, an eight-run, 11-hit start against the Padres on May 21. He showed remarkable command Wednesday against the Twins, throwing 80 of his 112 pitches for strikes and walking just one. He was tagged for a solo home run by Michael Cuddyer, the first dinger he'd allowed in 50 2/3 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the White Sox, Lewis suffered the loss after giving up four runs on seven hits in 6 1/3 innings of work. Lewis has already started against the Mariners twice this season, going 1-0 with a 0.56 ERA. He's given up only one run to Seattle in 16 innings of work along with 13 strikeouts. For his career, Lewis is 3-2 with a 3.95 ERA in eight starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez was on fire Thursday against the Twins, as he struck out nine and allowed just one run on five hits in eight innings to earn his first win since April 21. Catcher Rob Johnson called it Hernandez's best outing of the season, and he put the finishing touches on in historic style by striking out four in his final frame. That was made possible after a wild pitch/strikeout combo landed Joe Mauer at first, and Hernandez responded by fanning Justin Morneau to end his night. The King was fired up after the fourth K, and rightly so. It was the first time a Seattle pitcher accomplished the feat since Kazuhiro Sasaki in 2003.

home_pitcher_note: Wilson matched starter Colby Lewis for the most wins on the staff with a 9-6 win over the Rays on Friday. Wilson pitched five-plus innings, giving up five runs on six hits with five strikeouts. It was his first win since May 7 against the Royals. Still, Wilson has left with the bases loaded in each of his last two starts, with four of those runners eventually scoring. In his only start this season against the Mariners, Wilson earned a no-decision in a 3-1 Rangers win in 11 innings. He went seven innings, giving up one run on five hits with four strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Snell is coming off a complete game if you had his last two starts together. He lasted just 5 1/3 against the Angels on Friday while throwing 98 pitches (60 strikes), walking four and surrendering three hits and four runs. In his three starts since returning to the rotation from bullpen duty, Snell has yet to make it through the sixth inning. His main issue has been aggressiveness, as his inability to attack the strike zone has led to walks (nine compared to four strikeouts) and a rising pitch count that doesn't give him a chance to go deep into games.

home_pitcher_note: In his first Major League start of the season, Hunter picked up a complete-game win against the Rays, giving up just one run on five hits with four strikeouts. He had excellent control of his fastball, issuing no walks and inducing 13 ground-ball outs. Of the 117 pitches he threw, 76 were for strikes. Hunter made four starts against the Mariners last season, going 1-2 with a 2.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith is a placeholder in the rotation for Doug Fister, who's on the disabled list until at least June 16 with shoulder fatigue. Rowland-Smith's first spot start went well, as he allowed only one run on four hits to drop his ERA below seven for the first time since before being demoted to the bullpen following his May 17 start. Thanks to lots of foul balls and some long at-bats, his pitch count rose quickly and he was bounced after throwing 86 pitches in five innings. But he finished strong by staying down in the strike zone -- his problem in his first eight, mostly poor, starts -- and won back some faith from manager Don Wakamatsu. He'll be on a longer leash this time around with a chance to impress, even though it's unlikely to keep him in the rotation barring a setback from Ian Snell.

home_pitcher_note: Correia is coming off his shortest outing of the season, as he allowed five runs on four hits in 1 2/3 innings on Sunday against the Phillies. But he got the no-decision after the Padres came back to win, 6-5, in 10 innings. Correia struck out four batters and walked three and didn't exactly get help from his defense in a four-run second inning by the Phillies. Correia has given up four earned runs or more in four of his past five starts and has just two quality starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas posted his ninth quality start in 11 tries last time out, but two errors led to an unearned run and a rising pitch count to cut short a strong performance after six innings. He forced the Angels to beat him with their bats, walking none of the 30 batters he faced and inducing 21 fly balls to just five grounders. He'll get his first chance to hit in San Diego, an exciting prospect for the career .292 batter, who posted a .354 mark as a designated hitter at Long Beach State.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc tossed a gem on Monday in Philadelphia, allowing no runs on four hits in seven innings to earn his first win since April 29. He walked one, struck out two and retired the final 14 batters he faced. "I was just focused on throwing strike one, something that was lacking my last four starts," LeBlanc said after the game. The Padres have won three of LeBlanc's six starts at PETCO Park this season, where he sports a 2.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander has been a strike-throwing machine all season in general and his past two starts in particular. He threw 107 pitches in his complete-game outing against the Rangers on a hot and humid Monday night in Arlington and 84 of them were strikes. In his previous start against the Twins, 80 of Lee's 112 pitches were strikes. Lee has walked just four batters in 61 2/3 innings this season while striking out 57, pitched two complete games and pitched into the seventh inning in all eight of his starts. This will be his second start against the Padres this season. The first one was rocky as they hit Lee for seven earned runs in 6 1/3 innings, but Lee won the game.

home_pitcher_note: Richard has not allowed more than a run in four of his past six starts. But for the second consecutive start, he shackled his opponent without getting a win. In his last two starts -- both against the Mets -- Richard has pitched 13 innings and allowed two runs with nothing to show for it. After winning three consecutive starts from May 12-22, Richard has been held without a victory in his last three. Except for allowing four runs against the Nationals on May 28, he doesn't have to blame himself for that.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Rangers, Hernandez gave up seven runs on eight hits in six innings with five strikeouts in a 7-1 loss on Tuesday. It was just the third time in 21 career June starts that he was defeated. In his only start against the Padres this season, he took the loss by giving up three runs on seven hits with six strikeouts in seven innings of work. In six career starts against San Diego, Hernandez is 2-2 with a 3.69 ERA and 36 strikeouts in 39 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright didn't have his best stuff against the Dodgers on Wednesday, when he allowed four runs on eight hits over six innings, along with a season-high five walks and six strikeouts. He uncharacteristically struggled with his control and needed 113 pitches to get through those six innings. Wainwright has never faced the Mariners in his six-year career with the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander acquired from the Tigers last season for Jarrod Washburn makes his first start of this season, mostly because of the ineffectiveness of right-hander Ian Snell, winless in five decisions. French started the season at Triple-A Tacoma, where he was used primarily as a starter.  He replaced Snell in the second inning against the Rangers last Wednesday and was impressive enough to get a shot in the Seattle rotation. He relies on location and changing speeds. This will be French's first career start against the Cardinals and the only player on the St. Louis roster he has faced is Matt Holiday, who walked. French also could get his first career at-bat.

home_pitcher_note: Suppan has to be activated first, but he will be, and then he'll get this start. He's struggled this year, but the bar is pretty low after some less-than-satisfying outings by fill-in Cardinals starters recently. His velocity has remained intact, so the question is location. Then again, with Suppan, the question is always location. If he can be even passable, giving the Cardinals six decent innings on a semi-regular basis, they'll be pleased.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps a start against a National League team will help Rowland-Smith get his winless season turned around. Encouraged by a strong outing against the Angels on June 5, when he surrendered just one run over five innings, the lefty from Australia was rocked for 11 hits and eight runs (four earned) in a loss to the Rangers in Arlington. Two of the hits were home runs, the 11th and 12th off Rowland-Smith, this season. In 51 2/3 innings, Rowland-Smith has walked 22 and struck out 22, a ratio that has worked against him big-time. He has never faced the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia needs to regain the efficiency that marked his early starts. It's doubly important now with the club dealing with a battered back of the starting rotation. Every time Garcia runs his pitch count up in five innings, it puts strain on the bullpen. He can be a little more aggressive, but he's also finding hitters laying off his offspeed stuff more, so he'll need to adjust to that. He's still getting outs and putting up zeroes, so it's not a bad problem to have, but the Cards would still benefit from improvement from the rookie.
away_pitcher_note: The unsung left-hander continues to pitch well in his first injury-free season in several years. In 11 starts since being hit hard in his first outing of the campaign, Vargas has yielded three or fewer runs each time and given the team a chance to win. He's not overpowering, striking out 49 in 76 2/3 innings, but he works both sides of the plate and utilizes a superb changeup to keep hitters off-balance. He has pitched at least six innings in 10 of his 12 starts this season. Vargas has faced six Cardinals who are a combined 8-for-25 (.320) against him with no home runs.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander makes his 10th start of the season and no doubt is glad to have the Padres behind him for the remainder of the season -- unless he's traded to a National League team. The rumor mill already has started to link the potential free agent to several contending teams heading toward the July 31 non-waiver Trade Deadline. Of the 22 runs Lee has allowed this season, 10 were scored by San Diego. Lee continues to pepper the strike zone, walking just four batters in 68 2/3 innings this season while striking out 60. He faced the Reds once last season, allowing three runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto had one rough inning in his last outing, Saturday against the Royals, as he allowed five runs in the second inning. He said it was a matter of overthrowing his pitches, and he settled down, pitched six innings and picked up a win with the help of an offense that scored 11 runs. Cueto hasn't lost since April 24 -- he's 6-0 in his last nine starts. He is 4-2 with a 3.91 ERA in nine career Interleague starts, but this will be his first appearance against the Mariners. Milton Bradley (six at-bats) and Franklin Gutierrez (two at-bats) are the only Seattle players Cueto has faced, and neither has a hit against him.

home_pitcher_note: After scuffling for almost a month, Hernandez was vintage Felix in his last outing against the Padres. He repeatedly threw first-pitch strikes and dominated the NL team, holding San Diego to four hits over 8 2/3 innings while striking out nine, matching his season high. The Mariners had lost eight of his previous nine starts, a total reversal from last season when Seattle had a 25-9 record in games he started. This will be Hernandez's first appearance against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: He's faced Chris Carpenter, Matt Cain and Zack Greinke. Now he gets Felix Hernandez. LeCure has done a lot of things well since taking the injured Homer Bailey's place in the rotation. However, luck has not managed to follow him. Carpenter, Cain and Greinke all turned in ace-worthy performances to beat LeCure in his past three starts. Last time out, LeCure threw 120 pitches and gave up four runs in 6 2/3 innings, but Greinke went the distance and the Reds lost to Kansas City, 7-3.

home_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith took some steps in the right direction in his last start, holding the Cardinals scoreless over three innings before surrendering three runs in the fourth and exiting after 59 pitches. An improved arm slot helped him keep his pitches down in the zone early in the game and Rowland-Smith hopes to maintain the success he had through the middle innings as well and begin to pitch deep into games. His frustration began to boil over in his last start, but he kept his cool and said the positives outweighed the negatives.
away_pitcher_note: The Dodgers jumped on Harang early on Tuesday, tagging him for three runs in the first inning. Harang threw 98 pitches in 4 1/3 innings before rain delayed the game for more than two hours and he was removed from what ended up being a 12-0 Reds loss. Harang has started four games against the Mariners in his career, but only one of those starts has occurred since 2003. In 2007, Harang pitched eight scoreless innings to pick up a win against Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: If there's one complaint to have about Vargas this season, it's that high pitch counts often limit how far into games he can go. That wasn't an issue in his most recent start, in which he went 7 2/3 innings in a 2-1 win at St. Louis. That gave him 11 quality starts in 13 tries, tying him for sixth in the Majors, and he did it on 94 pitches with no walks.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster notched his ninth quality start in his last outing against the Athletics. He gave up two runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings, throwing 120 pitches. It's the fourth time he's thrown at least 120. Dempster also struck out seven as he won for the third time in his past five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Lee was nothing short of brilliant in a 1-0 shutout win against the Reds on Friday. He worked out of trouble in the first and cruised the rest of the way. His ability to avoid walks has been a major key to his success, as he's issued just four free passes while dealing 67 strikeouts. Only three other pitchers since 1900 have tallied as many strikeouts with so few walks (Bret Saberhagen, Greg Maddux and Ben Sheets) in a 10-start period, and Lee's the only one to do it in his first 10 outings of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Wells got back on track in his last start. He held the A's to two runs on seven hits over seven innings. The problem in his previous starts was that he was falling off the rubber. A couple of side sessions, some work with pitching coach Larry Rothschild, advice from Greg Maddux and a good look at video helped Wells figure it out. Wells has never faced the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez has taken four of his past five starts through at least eight innings, and his most recent outing was his best yet. He followed up Cliff Lee's shutout with a one-run complete game, walking one and striking out nine. That was a point of pride for Hernandez, who wasn't happy about having to leave his previous start after 8 2/3 innings. To say the least, he and Lee make a formidable pair. There's just no telling how much longer it will last.
away_pitcher_note: Lilly struggled in his last start, giving up eight runs (six earned) on nine hits over 5 1/3 innings against the Angels. It was the most runs he's served up since being charged with nine on July 20, 2009, at Philadelphia. Lilly gave up four runs in the first inning; he had given up one run in the first in his previous 10 starts combined. The lefty gave up multiple homers for the third time, and second this month.

home_pitcher_note: Bush will have gone nine days without a start when he takes the mound against the Mariners. Manager Ken Macha shuffled the rotation at a time the Mariners were batting just .235 against right-handed pitchers and billed the move as a bonus for Bush. But the pitcher, who pitched 7 1/3 scoreless innings in Anaheim on June 15, had a different view, saying, "I'd rather stay on a regular schedule. I feel like the way I threw the ball last time, I earned the right to go back out there."
away_pitcher_note: Hyphen got the outing he'd been looking for all year against the Reds on Sunday, earning his first win and throwing six shutout innings. Rowland-Smith hasn't had the kind of season he'd hoped for and is likely the odd starter out when Erik Bedard returns from the disabled list, but a few more good performances could at least make that decision tougher for manager Don Wakamatsu.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf has bounced back nicely since surrendering a career-high five home runs in a June 9 loss to the Cubs at Miller Park. On the Brewers' recent road trip, he tossed a pair of quality starts, combining to limit the Angels and Rockies to three runs on six hits in 14 innings. Wolf only allowed one run in seven innings in Colorado, and it came when Rox right fielder Brad Hawpe hit just enough of a slider to send it the opposite way to the left-field seats. Wolf has faced the Mariners only twice in his career and lost both games.
away_pitcher_note: Fister is scheduled to make his first start after going on the disabled list with shoulder fatigue on June 1. His biggest value (despite his 2.45 ERA) has been his ability to get deep into games, but that likely won't be the case Saturday. He'll be on a pitch count of about 85, which could keep him shy of his average of just under seven innings per start.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson got the nod for his last start when right-hander Dave Bush was pushed back due to poor career numbers against the Twins, including a career-worst outing at Target Field earlier this season in which Bush was unable to get out of the first inning. Through six batters, Narveson was doing his best Bush impression. The rest of the way, he got 15 outs while facing just 16 batters. First-inning struggles have been common for Narveson, whose first-inning ERA jumped to 12.27 for the season after allowing three in the first on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas has taken tips from Seattle ace Cliff Lee to improve his approach on the mound, and it's clearly paying off. He notched his fifth quality start in a row with seven shutout innings against the Cubs on Tuesday, dropping his ERA to 2.66. He's walked a total of three batters in his last four starts while striking out 20, and he hasn't taken a loss since May 4.

home_pitcher_note: After having a start skipped with his innings limit in mind, Hughes will go for his sixth straight win. Hughes has pitched like an All-Star -- in five starts since the Mets dealt him his only loss on May 22, Hughes is 5-0 with a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Lee's club-record streak of innings without a walk will be put to the test against the Yankees, the AL's most patient team. Lee has not allowed a walk in 37 innings, and he has 76 strikeouts to four walks in his past 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez hopes to finish June in strong fashion, looking to continue the progress he made while going 3-1 with a 3.00 ERA in five starts this month leading into his effort against Seattle. Vazquez took a no-decision on June 23 at Arizona, allowing four runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez has been benefiting the Mariners bullpen with some workhorse performances, going nine innings in each of his past two starts. He lasted 8 2/3 innings three starts ago.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia will go for his sixth straight win on Thursday against Seattle. Sabathia beat the Dodgers on June 25 with eight innings of one-run, four-hit ball and has a 2.19 ERA over his last five starts, having limited opponents to a .191 batting average.
away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith was bitten by back-to-back home runs in his last outing in Milwaukee -- blasts by atypical power sources Jonathan Lucroy and Carlos Gomez. With Erik Bedard inching closer to the Majors, his hold on a rotation spot is tenuous.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will try to continue the high-powered, high-strikeout pitching that brought him back from the doghouse in June. He came an out shy of his fourth straight quality start Saturday, but still finished with 5 2/3 scoreless innings and eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start following a monthlong disabled-list stint with shoulder fatigue, Fister exceeded his prescribed pitch count of 75-80 pitches by throwing 92 in four frames. An off-day earlier in the week gives Fister an extra day's rest for this outing.

home_pitcher_note: An extra day of rest has usually meant extra trouble for Verlander this year, and he'll face that again this time around. He talked last week about changing up his routine and learning to keep his arm fresh, but this will be his first time trying to put that into practice.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas allowed a series of baserunners in the fifth inning of his last start, in Milwaukee, leading to a pair of runs and ending his day earlier than any other June start. Still, his streak of three earned runs or fewer extended to 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bonderman was brutally honest about his last outing, saying he escaped Minnesota with a win by luck. He owns quality starts in his last five home outings despite inducing more flyouts than groundouts each time, but he has won only one of those starts.
away_pitcher_note: With the clock ticking toward the non-waiver Trade Deadline, Lee, a potential free agent, begins a new month in pursuit of his fourth consecutive complete game and sixth of the season in 13 starts. His control has been practically perfect -- five walks in 96 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his past three starts, King Felix has looked like the 19-game winner from last year, and he's coming off a dominating, two-hit, complete game masterpiece against the Yankees. An improving changeup has made his two- and four-seam fastballs even more devastating to hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister picked up his sixth loss in his last start against the White Sox. He lasted just four innings, allowing four earned runs on eight hits, with two walks and four strikeouts. Bannister will look to stay above .500 as he opens up a three-game road series in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Hyphen's time in the rotation was prolonged thanks to Erik Bedard's shoulder stiffness. Rowland-Smith was solid in his last outing, holding the Yankees to two runs on five hits in six innings, but the Mariners fell 4-2.
away_pitcher_note: Finally, Greinke has half as many victories as losses. Breezing along for seven innings Wednesday against the White Sox, he suddenly gave up five straight hits and five runs in the eighth but won, 7-6. The last time he pitched in Seattle, he threw a one-hitter Aug. 30, 2009.

home_pitcher_note: Fister is experiencing the dreaded regressing to the mean. After a hot start to the season, he has cooled off lately. He's 0-3 in his last five starts (broken up by a stint on the DL), a span in which his ERA has nearly doubled from 1.72.
away_pitcher_note: Davies kept the ball low and the scoring down to one run vs. the Angels on Friday. Although he pitched an excellent 7 2/3 innings, he didn't get a decision in the Royals' extra-inning win. His command was on track again, and he's walked just three in his last 14 2/3 frames.

home_pitcher_note: Fatigue may be setting in for Vargas. A workhorse all year, he lasted a season-low 4 1/3 innings in his last start against the Tigers, allowing a season-high six runs on eight hits. He's struggled getting deep into games lately, a signal that he may be due for a rest.
away_pitcher_note: Pettitte makes his first start since being named an American League All-Star, looking for his third consecutive winning decision. He hurled six innings of three-run, five-hit ball against the Blue Jays on Sunday to earn his 10th win.

home_pitcher_note: Cliff Lee was supposed to start before he was traded to the Rangers.
away_pitcher_note: Hughes looks to snap a series of subpar outings with this start at Safeco Field. Hughes is 0-1 with a 8.49 ERA in his last two efforts against the Mariners and Blue Jays. Since May 17, he is 5-2 with a 5.56 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: When seven innings and two runs allowed are a mild disappointment, a pitcher is on fire. Monday against the Royals was the King's shortest outing in five tries, but his ERA is steadily dropping and it's clear he's in top form.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez beat the A's in his last start is becoming the innings-eater the Yankees though they were trading for, shaking off his poor beginning. In nine starts since May 21, Vazquez is 5-3 with a 3.12 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hyphen may be hitting his stride. His start against the Royals (seven innings, three runs) was his longest since April, but he did it by pitching to contact and playing defense as he didn't register a strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: Sabathia will try to make it eight wins in eight starts when he tackles the Mariners to wrap up the first half. He is 7-0 with a 1.88 ERA over his last seven efforts, limiting opponents to a .199 batting average.

home_pitcher_note: The Angels' key offseason acquisition, Pineiro finished with wins in his final six decisions of the first half, emerging as a front-end starter behind ace Jered Weaver. Pineiro has been effective mixing in his other pitches along with his bread-and-butter sinker.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander is gradually returning to his early-season form, relying on an over-the-top motion that creates movement on his pitches and frustration for the hitters. He held the Royals to one run over six innings in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver, fitting comfortably into the role of staff ace, made his first All-Star team after leading the Majors in strikeouts at the break with 137 in 120 innings, getting deeper in games. He has sharpened his changeup and curveball to go with his fastball and slider.
away_pitcher_note: His record aside, Hernandez is having All-Star-caliber season, ranking among the MLB leaders with four complete games and a current streak of six quality starts. He has taken his games into the seventh inning in nine of his past 10 outings.

home_pitcher_note: It was a fitful first half for Saunders, who would find his command, lose it, find it again, then go into another skid. Three of his final five starts were substandard. He needs to find consistency with his fastball command, complementing it with quality off-speed stuff.
away_pitcher_note: A tough season for the Australian native is best reflected in the team-high 17 home runs he has surrendered and his 36-32 walk-to-strikeout ratio. His self-confidence needs a major boost heading into the final two-plus months.

home_pitcher_note: Santana has been a model of consistency and durability, going at least five innings in each of his 18 starts and exceeding four earned runs only twice. His fastball has been consistently in the mid-90s with an evolving changeup and deadly slider.
away_pitcher_note: After a stellar June, when he posted a 3-1 record and 2.33 ERA in six starts, Vargas wobbled in his first outing this month, suggesting that he might be wearing down as he reached the 100-inning mark. But he bounced back in his last outing and the All-Star break should help.

home_pitcher_note: Pauley makes his second start of the season and the first one was a good one. He limited the Yankees to two hits and one earned run over five innings, but he absorbed the loss. He's a pitch-to-contact hurler and must keep the ball down to be successful.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander is trying to secure a rotation spot as Jake Peavy's injury replacement. Hudson didn't earn the win in his only other 2010 start against the Royals, despite the White Sox scoring 15 runs, as he was pulled after four-plus innings and five runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: One bad inning got the second half off to a rocky start, though Fister said he felt good and strong in his 5 2/3-inning stint against the Angels. But his command still isn't as sharp as it was earlier in the season and he surrendered a season-high 12 hits.
away_pitcher_note: Double-digit victories for a third straight season are on the line for Danks after rattling off two straight wins. Danks also has the chance to go over .500 for his career, currently sitting at 40-40.

home_pitcher_note: Lack of run support continues to haunt the staff ace, who is coming off his career-high fifth complete game of the season, albeit a one-run loss to the Angels. His trademark two-seam fastball took the night off, but he found a way to hold the hitters at bay.
away_pitcher_note: Four errors committed by the usually sure-handed White Sox defense led to three unearned runs and a tough loss for Floyd Friday in Minneapolis. Floyd has not performed well in Seattle, with a 1-4 mark and 7.41 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The second half of the season started upside-down for the lefty from Down Under as he surrendered his team-high 18th home run of the campaign during a 3 1/3 inning outing against the Angels. His confidence took another huge hit in the process.

The unheralded left-hander ranks among the MLB leaders with seven starts allowing one or fewer earned runs, including his first post All-Star Game outing. CC Sabathia, who has eight, is the only AL hurler with more such games than Vargas. Lefties are batting .215.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett, who has been on the DL since May 19 with a lower back strain, allowed three runs in four innings Saturday in a Triple-A rehab start. He was winless in his final six starts before the injury, with his lone '10 victory coming April 10 vs. K.C.

home_pitcher_note: Pauley is coming off another good-enough-to-win effort with a loss, making one bad pitch, a hanging slider, that cost him a tie-breaking two-run home run against the White Sox. He has received one run of support in his two starts with Seattle, covering 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester allowed four runs (three earned) on nine hits while walking three and striking out six in eight innings of work against the Rangers in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie righty showed early-season form in his last start, striking out a season- and career-high six batters while walking one in a loss to the White Sox. He surrendered three runs over six innings, but remained winless since May 14.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka fired 6 2/3 innings, alllowing one earned run on two hits while walking two and striking out six in a win over the A's in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Danks moved over .500 for his career, at 41-40, with 7 2/3 scoreless innings thrown Tuesday at Safeco Field. The southpaw gave up one infield hit in the second and didn't give up another hit, solid or otherwise, until Ichiro's single with two outs in the eighth.
away_pitcher_note: After ending a three-game set at home against the Sox with a scoreless eight-inning effort, Felix begins the Mariners' four-game rematch on the road. He ranks among the league leaders in innings pitched and ERA, but lack of run support has affected his win output.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd was locked in a duel with Seattle ace Felix Hernandez on Wednesday. Floyd worked seven and did not allow a Seattle runner to reach scoring position. He has a 1.16 ERA over his past nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Rowland-Smith's last three starts have not gone well. He's allowed 14 earned runs in 13 1/3 innings, raising his ERA from 5.74 to 6.27. Manager Don Wakamatsu said Hyphen will stay in the rotation because he's part of the clubs long-term plans.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle had his first complete game of the season in his last start, limiting the A's to one run on four hits. The 31-year-old has notched eight consecutive quality starts and has a 2.20 ERA in that span.
away_pitcher_note: With Cliff Lee gone, Vargas is the new complement to Felix Hernandez. He's in the AL's top 10 for ERA and has a quality start in eight of his past 10 appearances. Unfortunately, he's gotten just nine runs of support in his past seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia has been a pleasant surprise as a dependable back-of-the-rotation starter this season. Last time out, however, was a forgettable outing for the righty. He'll try to rebound after surrendering five earned runs in 1 1/3 innings vs. the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Pauley -- brought into the rotation as a spot starter -- has shown enough to keep himself around. In three starts, he's held opponents to just five earned runs. The next task is getting deeper into games, as he hasn't gone farther than six innings yet.

home_pitcher_note: Baker appears to have put the elbow tendinitis that plagued him before the All-Star break behind him. The right-hander is 2-4 over his last six starts but he'll try to build off his last start when he held the Orioles to two runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander attempts to win his first game since May 14, when he was cruising along with the best ERA in the AL, and end July on a positive note. This is his second start of the year against the Twins who saddled him with his third loss.

home_pitcher_note: Like Nick Blackburn, who was moved out of the rotation, Slowey had appeared to be on tenuous ground for his starting spot. But Slowey has turned things around by attacking the strike zone and trusting his catcher more in his last two outings.
away_pitcher_note: Felix has managed to keep his cool despite consistent lack of run support. He has pitched nearly as well this season as he did during his 19-win breakout a year ago, but has received just seven runs of support in his seven losses.

home_pitcher_note: Liriano has been on a tear since the All-Star break, going 3-0 and allowing just two runs in 21 2/3 innings. Another positive sign was Liriano's ability not to get flustered in his last start when his slider wasn't sharp early in the outing.
away_pitcher_note: French, promoted from Triple-A Tacoma on Tuesday, hopes he can pick up where he left off in the Minors, where he went 11-3 with a 2.94 ERA and earned a spot on the PCL All-Star team. He relies more on good location than high velocity.

home_pitcher_note: Home is where most of the wins have been for the left-hander. He has a 5-2 record and 2.23 ERA in 11 starts at Safeco Field, holding opposing batters to a .234 average. Vargas is coming off a tough outing -- three homers in a loss to the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start vs. the A's, Lewis took the loss despite giving up just one run on five hits with eight strikeouts in seven innings. He registered quality starts in four of his five July outings. In four starts at Safeco, he is 0-2 with a 3.56 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The early-season bout with a fatigued shoulder is behind him, and Fister is coming off his strongest outing since a stint on the DL. But three unearned runs contributed to his loss to the Twins, and he's winless since May 14.y
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Athletics, Wilson got the win after giving up three runs on seven hits with five strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings of work. In two starts against the Mariners this season, Wilson is 1-0 with a 1.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The lack of run support is getting to be absurd for the ace right-hander. He has the second-best ERA in the AL but has received seven runs of support in his eight losses while he's in the game. He almost has to pitch a shutout this season to win.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter had an eight-game winning streak snapped with a 9-7 loss to the Angels on Friday. He allowed eight runs in three innings. He is 2-2 with a 2.67 ERA in five starts against the Mariners in his career. He allowed three runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: A more confident French pitched well against the Twins in his first start since being promoted from the Minors, but lack of run support and unsuccessful diving catch attempt saddled him with the loss. But he drew rave reviews for his strong outing.
away_pitcher_note: Two starts ago, Greinke was rocked for eight earned runs over four innings. In his last start, however, Greinke returned to his Cy Young Award form, pitching eight innings, allowing three earned runs on seven hits with three walks and six strikeouts.

In his last start, Chen was serviceable, throwing five innings, allowing seven hits, three runs (two earned) with three walks and four strikeouts, before handing it over to the bullpen, which preserved his sixth win of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Six of the left-hander's wins have come at Safeco Field, where he has allowed 2.29 earned runs per outing. His 16 quality starts this season rank second on the team to Felix Hernandez and he has held opponents to two or fewer earned runs 14 times.
away_pitcher_note: By his assessment, Davies had great stuff last Tuesday at Oakland, it was just that old bugaboo -- throwing strikes -- that dogged him. He got through five innings with five walks and 95 pitches but gave up just two runs, keeping KC in the game.

home_pitcher_note: A pitch that missed its intended target by several inches and became a home run by several feet stung the rookie right-hander in his last outing. A season that started out so well has fallen on hard times. His last win occurred on May 14.
away_pitcher_note: Mazzaro rebounded from his worst start of the year to toss six innings of two-run ball in Tuesday's 3-2 loss to the Royals. Mazzaro allowed five hits and two walks while striking out five. Over his past eight starts, Mazzaro is 4-2 with a 3.10 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Run support continues to haunt the ace right-hander. The Mariners have scored two or fewer runs in each of his last five starts, leaving him closer to double-figure losses than double-digit wins.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson looks like he's returning to form after missing two months with left elbow inflammation. On Wednesday against the Royals, he pitched seven innings of two-run ball to lead the A's to a 6-2 win and earn his first victory since May 29.

home_pitcher_note: Since returning from the Minors, where he was 11-3 with a 2.94 ERA, French has been a solid addition to the rotation. He is coming off a stellar performance against the Royals, outpitching Cy Young Award winner Zack Greinke at Safeco Field.
away_pitcher_note: Braden gave up four runs over six innings in a 5-1 loss to the Rangers on Friday. He left after 88 pitches because of jaw pain, the result of a prior dental procedure. Braden said he doesn't expect to be affected by the injury going forward.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona has had two rough outings in his last three starts. He was beaten up for five runs on 10 hits over 7 1/3 innings against the Twins in a loss Saturday. The good news? He didn't walk anybody and has just three walks in his last four starts.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander had a shaky start in his last outing, throwing 46 pitches in the first two innings against KC, but allowed just two runs over five innings. He does a good job of keeping the ball down with his bread-and-butter pitch, the sinker.

home_pitcher_note: Talbot returns to the Indians rotation following his stint on the 15-day disabled list with a back strain. The rookie righty is 0-1 with a 4.97 ERA in three starts since the All-Star break. He has never faced the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: It's back on the road for the left-hander, who has fared much better at Safeco Field this season than anywhere else. He is 7-2 with a 2.23 ERA in 13 home starts this season, but 1-3 with a 4.50 ERA in nine road outings.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson surrendered seven runs (four earned) on six hits and three walks with three K's over five frames in a loss to the O's on Tuesday. The 25-year-old has lost three of his past four starts, posting a 6.55 ERA during that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, on Tuesday against the A's, Hernandez established a career high with 13 strikeouts. He has yet to face Cleveland this season.

home_pitcher_note: Bergesen was dominant in his last outing, tossing a two-hit, complete-game shutout against the Indians. It's been a rocky year for Bergesen, who has twice been sent to Triple-A, but he has turned in three straight quality outings.
away_pitcher_note: With his losing streak finally behind him, the righty can focus on having a solid finish to an injury-interrupted season. He definitely has pitched his way onto the rotation for the remainder of this season and into the 2011 campaign as well.

home_pitcher_note: Millwood had a rocky start, but he managed to battle through seven innings and turn in another quality start for a resurging rotation. He held the Indians to three runs on nine hits and one walk.
away_pitcher_note: Since returning from the Minors, French has been off and on -- good when he commands the strike zone and not so good when he falls behind in the count and must challenge the hitters. Pitching ahead in the count is crucial.

home_pitcher_note: Emerging as the clear ace of the staff, Guthrie lowered his post-All-Star break ERA to 1.51 in his sixth second-half outing and team-high sixth straight quality outing.
away_pitcher_note: Pauley earned his first Major League victory on Friday, tossing six innings of two-run ball against the Indians. The 27-year-old righty is 1-4 with a 3.81 ERA in six starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Burnett turned in one of his finest performances of the season on Sunday in Kansas City, only to suffer a rare complete-game loss. He allowed just one run on four hits in eight innings. Burnett has had two consecutive quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: After hurling 6 2/3 scoreless frames against the Indians on Sunday, Hernandez yielded six unearned runs following Chone Figgins fielding error. Hernandez has not allowed an earned run in his past 14 2/3 innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez's loss to the Tigers on Monday is hard to judge, considering that he threw 106 pitches in just four innings, all the while limiting Detroit to two runs. After an exemplary two-month stretch, Vazquez's ERA in his past six starts is 6.19.
away_pitcher_note: Vargas worked seven innings of three-run ball Saturday in a victory against the Indians. The 27-year-old lefty has won his past three starts, posting a 2.84 ERA over that stretch.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia was on Tuesday, holding the Tigers to two runs in seven innings in picking up his 16th win. He did surrender a pair of home runs -- he had allowed just one in his previous 13 starts -- but they were both solo homers.

away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez failed to get through the sixth for the third time in four starts. Against the Twins, he struggled at times with command, walking three in 5 1/3 frames while giving up five runs on nine hits. He has allowed 11 runs over his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Swanson lost his first two big league starts but drew praise for getting ahead of hitters and staying aggressive. Two home runs by San Diego’s Franmil Reyes doomed him in his previous start, but Swanson also retired 12 of 13 batters before Reyes’ second blast.
away_pitcher_note: A proven commodity (84-59 lifetime), Lynn is regarded by the Rangers as a source of stability. In Lynn’s lone appearance against Seattle,  he earned the decision in New York’s 4-2 victory last Sept. 8 while pitching for the Yankees. He allowed two runs and three hits in six innings.

away_pitcher_note: Hamels will try to improve to 4-0 as the Cubs open a three-game series in Seattle. He held the Dodgers to three runs on three hits in a game the Cubs won, 7-6.

away_pitcher_note: Lester is set to make his second start since coming off the injured list on Thursday, when he held the Dodgers to a run on four hits while striking out five in five innings but took the loss because the Cubs were shut out until the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: Bieber opens the homestand looking to improve upon his 6.12 career ERA at Progressive Field. He allowed one run on four hits over six-plus innings in an April 16 win vs. the Mariners. He struck out five and walked three, recording 12 fly ball outs.
away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi threw one perfect inning in his last start as the Mariners look to limit his workload, but he’ll now be back to normal duty. He picked up his first MLB win in his previous outing in Anaheim, though he held the lead in four prior no-decisions.

away_pitcher_note: Since starting the year with two wins, Leake has gone 0-3 with a 6.14 ERA and eight home runs allowed in four starts. His best outing in that stretch was against the Indians, allowing eight hits and two runs in six innings in a 4-2 loss in Seattle on April 16.

home_pitcher_note: With Mike Clevinger and Corey Kluber on the injured list, Anderson will make his first big league start since Sept. 24, 2016. He missed the last two seasons after Tommy John surgery, returning on April 13. He's posted a 5.40 ERA in five innings of relief.
away_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old rookie makes his fourth start in place of the injured Wade LeBlanc, still looking for his first win. His best outing came in his starting debut vs. the Indians, allowing two hits and one run in six innings in a 1-0 loss in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia joined the illustrious 3,000-strikeouts club in his last start, taking the loss in a 3-1 defeat at Arizona. Sabathia has completed at least five innings in all four of his starts this year, allowing two runs or fewer in three of the four.
away_pitcher_note: Though he hasn't won since his season debut, Hernandez is coming off back-to-back eight-strikeout games and will be looking to conjure up some of his past success at new Yankee Stadium, where he's 6-1 with a 1.44 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Tanaka will be happy to take the mound in the Bronx, coming off a difficult road trip in which he took a pair of losses, allowing nine runs (eight earned) in 9 2/3 innings to the Angels and D-backs (7.45 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: Gonzales will try to bounce back from his worst start of the young season, as he was roughed up for six runs (three earned) with three walks and five hits allowed in just 1 2/3 innings against the Cubs on May 1.

away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi limited the Indians to one run on three hits with one walk over seven innings in a no-decision Friday. Coming off a one-inning start as a means of limiting his 2019 innings, his fastball showed more life, touching 97 mph.

away_pitcher_note: Leake pitched six innings and allowed three runs in his last start on Saturday at Cleveland, but didn't figure in the decision. He is 1-1 with a 5.01 ERA in four road starts this season, striking out 18 over 23 1/3 innings.

away_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old rookie picked up his first Major League win Sunday in Cleveland, allowing just one hit in six innings in a 10-0 victory. Swanson has issued just three walks in 21 2/3 innings in his first 4 starts in place of the injured Wade LeBlanc.

home_pitcher_note: The righty has gone from a rough start to a certified roll. In his last four starts, Porcello is 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA. Lifetime against the Mariners, he is 6-6 with a 4.10 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie from Japan held the Yankees to three hits and one run in 7 2/3 innings his last start and has allowed just six hits and two runs in 14 2/3 innings his past two outings. He took a no-decision vs. the A's in his MLB debut in Tokyo in March.
away_pitcher_note: It'll be tough for Fiers to follow his last outing, when he made history by tossing the 300th no-hitter in MLB history. He'll get another crack at the Mariners, who roughed him up for five runs over three innings on Opening Day in Japan.

home_pitcher_note: Leake is looking for his first win of the season since April 6. He pitched seven innings in his last outing on Thursday, in which he gave up six hits and only one run in a loss to the Yankees. Leake is 1-2 with a 4.57 ERA over his career against the A's.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson will look to keep his streak of starts with at least six innings pitched going for a third consecutive outing. He's had plenty of success against Seattle, going 8-4 with a 2.19 ERA over 19 games, 18 of them being starts.

away_pitcher_note: Perez sustained a contusion after taking a line drive off his left foot in his last outing, but he is expected to make his next scheduled start in Seattle. His 15-inning scoreless streak was snapped vs. Detroit, but he allowed only four hits in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old rookie from Japan has found his groove in his last three starts, going 1-0 with a 2.18 ERA and holding the Indians, Yankees and A’s to a .155/.197/.324 slash line. This will be his first time facing the Twins.
away_pitcher_note: After a shaky start to the season, Gibson has a 2.73 ERA in his last five starts and collected his fourth win of 2019 on Tuesday, when he cruised through five innings before five runners reached base in the sixth as he lost control of his mechanics.

home_pitcher_note: Mengden makes his third start of 2019 looking to carry the momentum from an impressive performance of one run allowed over seven innings at Detroit last week. The right-hander is 0-2 with a 5.89 ERA in four career games (three starts) against Seattle.
away_pitcher_note: LeBlanc lasted just 2 1/3 innings while allowing 7 hits and 7 runs vs. the Twins after a five-week layoff with a strained right oblique. He'll look to get on track against the A's, who he held scoreless for 11 innings in two starts last year.

home_pitcher_note: Kikuchi will look to bounce back from a 3 1/3-inning outing at Oakland where he gave up 10 hits and 5 runs (4 earned). The rookie from Japan beat the Angels for his first MLB win on April 20, when he allowed 10 hits and 4 runs in 5 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Pena will be used either as the second pitcher in the game after an "opener" handles the first inning, as the "opener", or simply as the starter. Pena is 0-1 with a 4.15 ERA in four starts and 2-0, 2.63 in six relief appearances.

away_pitcher_note: Skaggs' record never has drifted more than a game above or below .500, though he won back-to-back decisions April 26 against Kansas City and May 2 against Toronto. In 5 career starts at Seattle, Skaggs is 1-1 with a 3.30 ERA and 31 strikeouts.
