away_pitcher_note: Heaney is 1-3 with a 3.76 ERA in seven career starts against Seattle, including 1-3, 4.19 in four T-Mobile Park outings. This marks the fifth consecutive season in which Heaney has made at least one appearance with the Angels.

away_pitcher_note: Suarez, the club's No. 5 prospect per MLB Pipeline, is set to make his Major League debut. Suarez had a 3.91 ERA in 23 innings at Triple-A Salt Lake after missing time early with a sore shoulder.

away_pitcher_note: After striking out nine batters in 5 1/3 innings in his MLB debut on May 12, the rookie prospect is 0-1 with a 6.55 ERA in his last three starts. Martin has allowed eight walks, 16 hits, five home runs and struck out seven over 11 innings in those starts.

home_pitcher_note: The 25-year-old was called up from Double-A Arkansas to make a spot start in place of Yusei Kikuchi, who is being skipped for one turn in the rotation. Moore went 1-3 with a 6.34 ERA in seven games (six starts) for Seattle in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Miley has allowed three runs or fewer in 11 of 12 starts. He's coming off his longest outing of the season, allowing two runs while striking out nine over seven innings vs. the Cubs. The Astros are 8-4 in games started by Miley, who has walked 16 in 69 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Leake is coming off one of his best starts of the season, allowing five hits and two runs over seven innings in a 4-3 win over the Angels on Friday.  The 31-year-old was 0-3 with a 5.55 ERA in four starts vs. Houston last year.

home_pitcher_note: Adams, a reliever, will make his first MLB start as the “opener,” with Tommy Milone to follow. Milone has filled in well in three starts since replacing rookie Erik Swanson, though a high pitch count limited his initial outings.

home_pitcher_note: Heaney has been solid in his two starts this season, striking out 18 in 11 innings, but he has had trouble keeping the ball in the park. He's served up four homers with two in each start.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzales went 5-0 with a 2.80 ERA in his first seven starts, but he's gone 0-6 with a 7.79 ERA in his last seven. He faced the Angels on Sunday, allowing nine hits and 10 runs in 4 2/3 innings in a 13-3 loss in Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Peters will be recalled from Triple-A Salt Lake to pitch, but there's a chance the Angels use an opener before his outing. The lefty had been pitching well at Triple-A with a 3.12 ERA in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Bassitt held Texas to 3 ER in his last start but took the hard-luck loss when the offense ran out of gas during its third game in 24 hours. He is 0-2 with a 3.33 ERA in five career appearances (four starts) against the Mariners.

home_pitcher_note: Montas hasn't lost a decision since April 29 vs. the Red Sox, a stretch of seven starts during which he's gone 4-0 with a 2.74 ERA. He's 3-0 at home over 5 starts this season, with a 3.54 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: This will be Bautista's second appearance as an "opener" for Seattle. Wednesday against the Twins, he pitched 1 1/3 shutout innings to begin the game. home_pitcher_note: Anderson earned himself a second Major League start after impressing in his first, allowing just two runs over 5 2/3 innings in a 6-2 loss to the Rays on Monday. This will be Anderson's first career start at the Coliseum.
away_pitcher_note: Since losing to the A's on May 26 in Oakland, Leake has turned things around with three of his best outings of the year, going 2-0 with a 2.35 ERA in 23 innings. He's 1-2 with a 4.99 ERA in seven starts vs. the A's over the past two years.

home_pitcher_note: Scott gets the start. Tommy Milone, who fired six innings of three-run ball in relief of an opener in Minnesota, is expected to come out of the bullpen again for the series opener vs. Kansas City.
away_pitcher_note: Duffy pitched arguably his best game of 2019 in a no-decision against the Tigers on Wednesday. He gave up just four hits and two runs. He also walked two -- the first two batters he faced -- and struck out seven.

home_pitcher_note: Kikuchi is in a slump, having recorded a 10.20 ERA in his last four outings. Prior to that, he enjoyed a four-start stretch in which he compiled a 1.66 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Bailey was on top of his game when the Royals beat the Tigers 7-3 in Omaha on Thursday. Bailey gave up just two singles through six shutout innings. He walked three and struck out six.

away_pitcher_note: Cashner overcame the threat of a blister -- he had what was termed as a "hot" finger -- to limit the A's to three runs (one earned) and four hits in six innings. Cashner is 2-5 with a 4.22 ERA in 11 career games (10 starts) vs. Seattle.

away_pitcher_note: The 27-year-old rookie will try to repeat the scoreless first inning he threw in his initial shot as an opener on Wednesday vs. the Brewers, with veteran lefty Tommy Milone to follow. Milone has a 2.55 ERA in 17 2/3 innings in three games in that role.

away_pitcher_note: Gonzales pitched well in his last start vs. the Brewers on Tuesday, tossing five innings and allowing just two earned runs while striking out four in the Mariners' 8-3 victory. The southpaw has won each of his last four starts.

home_pitcher_note: Ohtani traded zeros with Oakland's Sean Manaea through five innings in his last start, but he ended up dinged for three runs in six innings in a loss. The two-way star has only made one career start against the Mariners, allowing two runs in six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Dugger is taking the spot of Justin Dunn, who was placed on the IL on Wednesday. Dugger has multi-inning ability, but he’ll only throw two to three innings tops, with Héctor Santiago slated to follow.

home_pitcher_note: Cobb has been phenomenal since returning from the injured list, allowing one run in 12 innings with 12 strikeouts in two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi carried a no-hitter into the sixth inning his last time out against Texas, flashing much more intent behind his two-strike pitches than ever before. He’s gone at least six innings in nine of his 10 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Sandoval has fared well in three starts this season, posting a 2.57 ERA with nine strikeouts in 14 innings. He threw five scoreless innings against the A's in his last start on May 27.
away_pitcher_note: Gilbert showed all of his potential in his most recent outing against Oakland, pitching 6 innings that marked his most in a professional game since Aug. 24, 2019, when he was with Double-A Arkansas. He also had an electric fastball that averaged 95 mph and topped out at 98.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 1.94 ERA over his first seven starts, Boyd has a 7.84 ERA over his past four outings, including three homers last week in Milwaukee. A home start against the struggling Mariners could give Boyd the opportunity to get rolling again.
away_pitcher_note: In his return start from the IL, Gonzales threw four innings, allowed one run and struck out six on 50 pitches. Gonzales was set to only throw three innings, but he managed to get a fourth frame completed in his efficient outing.

home_pitcher_note: Mize has been better in rematches against opponents this season, but he’ll be hard-pressed to top the 7 2/3 innings of one-run ball he tossed against the Mariners last month in Seattle. He allowed three home runs in his last start against the White Sox.
away_pitcher_note: Flexen has struggled on the road, posting an 8.10 ERA in four starts away from T-Mobile Park compared to a 2.67 ERA in six home starts. Flexen went six innings in his last start against the A’s, but he gave up five runs.

home_pitcher_note: Alexander will step in to make his second start in as many weeks, again as part of a bullpen game. He’ll likely get a longer outing than the May 31 start in Milwaukee, where he lasted one inning before being lifted for a pinch-hitter with the bases loaded.
away_pitcher_note: Sheffield has provided some durability for Seattle, going at least five innings in each of his 10 starts this season. In his last outing against the Angels, Sheffield gave up two runs in 5 2/3 innings and allowed six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Civale returns to the hill looking to find the form that made him one of the AL's top wins leaders in May. In his previous two outings, Civale allowed a total of eight earned runs, after allowing three over the two starts before that. He carries an 0-1 record with a 6.75 ERA against the Mariners in one career start.
away_pitcher_note: Dunn (right shoulder inflammation) will be activated from the 10-day IL and start in Cleveland. The right-hander missed only one turn through the rotation after first experiencing the issue after his last outing on May 29 against Texas.

home_pitcher_note: McKenzie has already made two starts in the Majors since his demotion to Triple-A, but this time, he'll look to stay with the big league team for good. Two starts ago, he tossed five scoreless innings before fanning 10 batters in his next outing.
away_pitcher_note: Kikuchi avoided a scare against the Angels on Saturday, when he had to exit early after taking a hard-hit grounder to his right knee. But he recovered nicely this week and won’t have to miss his scheduled start.

home_pitcher_note: Bieber takes the mound after tossing six innings of one-run ball on Tuesday against the Cardinals. He is 3-0 with a 1.80 ERA, 24 strikeouts and five runs allowed (four earned) in 20 innings in his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Gilbert is coming off two strong starts over the division-rival A’s and Angels, in which he gave up a combined three runs on seven hits to the 47 batters he faced in 11 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzales didn’t have his crispest stuff his last time out in Detroit, but he finished with a pair of 1-2-3 innings to end his day. Had his leash been longer, he likely would’ve pitched beyond the fourth inning. But the Mariners continue to build his workload following a forearm injury.
away_pitcher_note: Following a rehab start with Triple-A St. Paul on Wednesday, Maeda will be activated from the 10-day IL to make his first MLB start since May 22. He hopes that his struggles with persistent groin tightness and arm weakness are behind him.

home_pitcher_note: Flexen has pitched at least six innings in each of his past three starts, over which he has a 3.79 ERA and .681 OPS against. He helped lead the Mariners to a road win in Detroit his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Happ held steady against his former team in his last outing, as he limited the Yankees to four runs in five innings, using 101 pitches to keep the Twins in the game before Josh Donaldson and Nelson Cruz powered Minnesota to a walk-off win in the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: Sheffield struggled mightily with diminished velocity and hard contact from the Tigers his last time out, lasting a season-low four innings. The lefty has been laboring far more this season after a stellar rookie campaign in 2020.
away_pitcher_note: Considering Ober had a 100-to-nine K-BB ratio in his last Minor League season in 2019, it's no surprise that he has 15 strikeouts and two walks through three MLB outings. He's impressed the Twins enough that he'll stay in the rotation for another turn.

home_pitcher_note: Dunn labored in his return from the 10-day IL his last time out in Cleveland, allowing each of his first five baserunners to reach and pitching just three innings. He and the Mariners chalked it mostly up to some rust after he skipped one turn through due to right shoulder inflammation.
away_pitcher_note: Hill said he "ran out of gas" in the final inning of his last start Saturday, when he allowed two walks and a homer against the Orioles. Overall, it could just be a bump in the road for the veteran left-hander, who posted a 0.99 ERA in eight previous starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kikuchi was stellar in Cleveland on Saturday, pitching seven shutout innings in a dominant effort. He’s gone at least six in each of his past eight starts, aside from a June 5 outing in Anaheim that was cut short when he took a foul ball off his right knee and had to exit early.

Gilbert turned in the best start of his young career on Sunday at Progressive Field, coming one out shy of finishing the seventh inning. He located his fastball impressively at the top of the zone and dropped in his wicked curve for strikes, with nine whiffs on secondary pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Fleming is coming off an excellent outing after an opener, as he fired four hitless innings with one walk and three strikeouts vs. the Orioles last Sunday. This will be Fleming's first time facing Seattle and only his second career West Coast start.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzales was hit hard his last time out, which has been a more alarming trend for the Mariners’ No. 1 starter. But Seattle was able to overcome his three runs allowed in a win over the Twins on Monday. He should be fully stretched out against Tampa Bay after a five-week stint on the IL curbed his workload.
away_pitcher_note: McClanahan bounced back on Tuesday after two rough starts, holding a tough White Sox lineup to three runs on seven hits in five innings. But he is still struggling with first-pitch strikes, which he'll need to address to fully unlock his elite stuff.

home_pitcher_note: Flexen is coming off the best start of his career, throwing eight shutout innings with eight strikeouts against the Twins. The right-hander has been a reliable innings eater in recent starts, going at least six innings in each of his last four outings.
away_pitcher_note: Freeland's re-entry to active pitching has been difficult -- a 9.58 ERA in five starts after recovering from a left shoulder strain. But he has faced the Mariners twice, both in Seattle, and is 1-0 with a 2.45 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Sheffield was lit up in his last start against the Twins, allowing a season-high seven earned runs on 10 hits in five innings. Sheffield has allowed two home runs in each of his three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Márquez held the Brewers to one hit and no runs over six innings in his last start before leaving with cramps -- something that has happened on several occasions at Coors Field. Seattle may be less of a problem.
